This is one of the first difficult instances of the game.  You have packs of 3-4 20-22nd level elites to contend with and serious challenges to face before you can get to Arugal.  An experienced party can do this with care and attention to aggro range, focusing their attacks precisely.  Inexperienced groups (unless way overlevelled) will wipe again and again.

Arugal himself is quite dangerous and teleports continuously during the fight within a two leveled environment that makes it difficult for melee characters to reacquire him as a target.

Anyone telling you this is an easy instance is either lying, bragging or carried through by other more sensible players and blindly confusing their competence with ease.

There is an easy way to kill Arugal. Tag him and run back to the main chamber, where you killed Fenrus. The person who has aggro stays in the Fenrus room. Everyone else goes to Arugal's room. What will happen is Arugal charges towards the Fenrus room and then whacks one or two times (at most, sometimes none at all) and teleports back to his main room. This allows the other members of the group to smack Arugal around until his aggro changes to someone else. This new person can then go to Fenrus' room and repeat as before. Everytime he teleports, he'll erase any dots on him, but he will not reset his health (as of 4/3/06). This most likely will be patched, however. 

A few other tips. Do not go into the room to kill Fenrus. Kill him in the hallway. Have the tank stand in the hallway to attract the mobs that spawn afterwards. If you kill a named, sometimes a new wolf-man spawns in a place that you may have cleared. For example, when you kill the Baron, a wearwolf spawns in the room adjacent to the courtyard and adjacent to the Baron's room. This can complicate pulling, so go back and kill this. The tricky pull spot is the Knight's room (up the stairs past the Baron's room). Here is a way to pull this room. Have a warlock cast Eye of Kelrog and have a priest cast the spell-shield on it. The eye can get aggro, but the mobs ignore it unless it gets too close. As a result, you can pull fewer mobs and sometimes even singles from clusters of mobs. (This works in general.) In the Kni

As a 30 Hunter,spec'd mostly in Beastmastery, I could not solo this instance.  One trick I used over and over again, was to pick a mob in a group, send my pet to it, and concentrate on that one mob with my ranged attacks. my pet would of course die since there were usually 3-4 mobs beating on him, but not before we took down that ONE.  Soon as pet was about to die, I'd FD, let the mobs go back to sleep, wake up, revive my pet, feed him and tackle the next mob.  This way, we were able to wean down larger groups one mob at a time, painfully slow though.

Note that in ANY place I could, I would naturally pull them one at a time, and that went quite fast.

At 30, I can safely tackle 2 level 24 Elites, 3 is troublesome especially if they summon.

I guess, eventually, I could have got through the entire instance this way, but the amount of time involved became not worth it.  Over 3 hours and I still had quite a ways to go.

Read my posts for each of the named for a little info. This quest can be completed by a full group of level 40's, or below. We started this quest a few weeks a go and as we leveled up we moved from instance to instace.  There are 4 instances you must go through to complete this quest. The first is an AE instance (to the left when entering the area), bring an AE group. A level 35 or lower group can do this one. Next you move on to the second instance(to the right). I'd recommend a 35+ group here, you clear everything, just watch out monks are tough. The boss here drops a key to enter the final 2 instances. The key is the Scarlet Key. These two instances are the easy ones. Now you move to the harder stuff. The instance on the right behind the door that requires the key is the third instance and the one on the left is the fourth and final instance.  Elites are now 36-38 and the boss of the third instance is a level 40 mob with an AE. This boss is the only one we had trouble with, but that was because we didnt know he had an AE ^^ Please see my post on Herod for more info by clicking his link above. The final instance we have attempted, and won, only once. It is fairly easy, but there are two elite mobs you need to fight here, both of which are 42. I dont want to ruin the suprise more than I already have, so check the strategy posted for the fight under Scarlet Commander Mograine's link. 

Every fight was done by members of this group as we all leveled up over a period of about a

Houndmaster Locksley is in the Library. We just had the warrior keep his attention while the rest of the group picked off the hounds one by one. Pretty easy.

Herod is in the Armory. This guy is a bit more tricky. Have the tank grab aggro obviously, and then BE SURE to back off when he yells "Blades of Light!" because he goes into some spinny move that will tear you appart if you are close to him. Use these times to get the group healed. Goes into some berserk mode at about half life and hits a lot harder! Keep healing when he does the spinny move and you will be fine. After he dies about 20 non-elite trainees run into the room. They drop like flies with AOE!

The Scarlet Commander guy is in the Cathedral. MAKE SURE, MAKE SURE, MAKE SURE, that you have killed all the other guys in the Cathedral, otherwise when he yells you will be looking at him and 30 Lunatics charging at you. But if hes solo then just tear him apart.

Inquisitor girl is in the Cathedral after you kill The Scarlet Commander. Once he is dead she comes out and starts casting damaging spells. Once she gets to about a Third of her life she stuns the whole party and rezzes the first boss. Have the tank keep the first boss busy while the rest of the group plows through the girl. Once the girl is dead, do the same thing for the Commander again. Dying hasnt made him stroner... 

Those are all the bosses needed to complete the quest. Enjoy your new rewards!

Im a 44 warlock and i still farm SM with my guildies occassionally, as i have finished the quest and moved on to greater things.

For horde players (dont know alliance, never played) the quest begins with varimathras the dreadlord in UC and although its red when you get it, you can start in the library with loskey and getting the key to armory and cathedral.

Loskey- No big deal really, have a tank or pet hold him while you deal with the dogs.Fear if you cleared the courtyard outside his room.

Herod- Armory is a bit more tricky, as mobs are lvs 37-40 and packed in groups of 4-5.Keep aggro away from your dps and you are good.Herod owns cloth with his "Blades of Light!" so keep away as far as you can and just burn him down.Hes immune to magic when he spins so just back away and heal.

Morgaine/Whitemane- Long ass pulls from the cathedral onto the lawn will do the trick.And she WILL put everyone to sleep no matter how far away from her you are, just kill them both again.AND clear the cathedral BEFORE the final fight.I know its been said but there is always the impatient ass who wont listen to reason, which is if you lay a finger on Morgaine, each and every mob in there will run on you.Kill them all first, including the side rooms.

Conclusion-Team work,speed and crowd control are the game here.Designate roles, manage your aggro, 
keep mobs from running away and watch for respawns, as in the cathedral atleast you will be standing in one place for a great deal of time.

[b]To Get To Scarlet Monastery [/b]

If you started off in In spamming /2 LFG SM, like most of us you will be very relieved once you find a group. ONce you do find your group you need to fly to Southshore. Once you are there, begin your journey north. When you hit the mountain type area you want to follow it more NW. You will eventualy end up at Dalaran. You will see a busted up area with wizards and Elementals, KEEP GOING. Then you run into a lake. Swim across the lake to the islands there. The mobs are lvl 18, if you die, the only way you can solve your problem is by deleting your acct. So continue hopping islands until you are at teh northern most island. Hop in the water and swim again until you see an outline of a castle on the bank. To the left of the castle there is a part where you can walk up, swim here and then you can get up. Once you arrive on land walk over to the road, travel the road N until you see the SECOND fork. There is a sign that says monastery. Follow the road, but off to the left of it to avoid attracting the death gaurds. Meet back up with the road, and follow it all the way to the monastery. In there are minor elites that you dont have to worry about, but there are gankers. They protect the doored instances and kill you alot. IF you are about to die, hop into a portal. Ok, Library is the portal on your right. Armory is door on the right. CAth is the door on the left. And Graveyard is the portal on the left. Thats how you get there.

Hound Master Loksey 
-------------------
Library (Portal to the right)

Loksey is in a room off the courtyard near the beginning of the library.  Also in the library (though not needed in this quest) are the Mythology of the Titans and the scarlet key.  Doan is the final boss here.

Herod
-----
Armory (Righthand door)

Herod is the final boss.  At one time the whipping boy of mages the world over, he is now immune to movement imparing effects (frost) and has a charge in case you happen to get too far out in front (blink).  Mages beware of aggro =).  When Herod dies a mob of low health followers storms into his room.

High Inquisitor Whitemane
Scarlet Commander Mograine
--------------------------
Cathedral (Lefthand door)

Mograine stands at the head of the cathedral proper.  Be careful to clear all followers inside before engaging, because he calls them to battle if you don't.  When Mograine dies his *ahem* inquisitor, Whitemane, rushes out of the large door behind the altar.  At 50% health she will sleep your whole party, resurrect Mograine, and fully heal herself.  Twink parties beware, it is possible to kill her before she completes this event - at which point no one will get kill credits for either of them and no loot is dropped.

The portal to the left is the undead wing.  To my knowledge there are no quest objectives for the Alliance there, but there are several rare spawn bosses with interesting loot.

Good luck!

Come on, it's stated over and over above:

1. Talk to the Scarlet Emissary in the basement of the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind OR head straight to Nijel's Point in Desolace and talk to Brother Anton - the guy in SW only sends you to find the guy in Desolace anyway

2. Anton gives you a *mandatory* pre-quest, you need to head to south-east Desolace and kill 30 undead ravagers; these are lv37-38 mobs, easy to solo, watch out for the roaming lv40 necromancers though (soloed it on my lv36 priest, no problem). Head back to Nijel's Point to turn the quest in.

3. Head to Southshore in Hillbrad, talk to the guy on the second floor of the inn; after a little speech and burning a letter, he gives you this quest (In the name of the light); head to Scarlet Monastery, kill Houndmaster Loksey (Library wing), Herod (Armory wing), Mograine and Whitemane (Cathedral wing), head back to Southshore to turn this quest in and collect your blue reward.

This is not a difficult quest, but does require you to go through most of the sections of Scarlet Monastary, save for the graveyard. With a group of 5 38-40+ players, it is easily done in two to three hours, if you can move quickly. The rewards for this quest are very nice for rogues and warriors especially, as the Black Menace is a very nice dagger for rogues and the Bonebiter is a very good 2H Axe for warriors. The Sword isn't too bad, but not that great, while the Orb is pretty nice for mages I would think. So definitely a worthwhile quest and you can gain a decent amount of XP while doing it.

The hardest part is the Cathedral where Mograine and Whitemane hangs out. But all of the instances can be 3manned if you have a group of level 40-43 people, and doing it like that is a great way to get some exp around that level.

forever.body: I, lvl 40 Priest, did this quest with a 40 Hunter last night. The best way to find her is when you enter the cave stay to your right. You can bypass all the boss mobs (ie. Overlord, Deathspeaker). Keep on going until you hit serveral bridges. Be careful because there are a lot of mobs, including mobs that will hide. Eventually you'll find a cave with bats. In this cave go left until you see the bats. Then stay to your right. IGNORE THE FORCEFIELD. The crone is NOT there and the fight was quite tough. All that is there is a huge boar which dropped some lame pants. Keep on going right until you see a camp with some totemics. Patience, you're almost there. Kill those and walk out and keep going until you see the top of a tower. Buff up and prepare for battle. She wasn't to tough. She casts a lot of magic, never healed herself while we killed her though. She dropped the shield and the medallion.

mage solo guide for charlga

i did this quest at lvl 47 by myself just to get the shoulderpads cuz mine were really crappy. i went through killing stuff and ended up dying when i aggroed like 8 mobs. i went in again another time with everything respawned, and i walked past everything (the aggro radius is small cuz the mobs are 'grey' color) i didnt kill a single mob until i reached charlga. use blink to bypass mobs and especially patrols on bridge. blink has a 15s cooldown but if you time it right you can blink right past the patrols twice. worst comes to worst you might have to kill a few if you aggro by accident.

while fighting charlga, you'll notice she casts some shield on herself. dont use any mana; just use your dagger and hit her 2-3 times until it doesnt say 'immune' anymore. i guess the shield nullifies 2-3 of your attacks. its pretty easy. you might have to use a mana pot/jade and maybe a health pot too.

keep in mind, this is for solo. if you have a group its pretty straightforward :)

I was also able to find the crone and the directions above are quite good.  There is a long way to go through there in order to get to her, but if you find the cave with the bats, you're on the right track.  I attempted the crone as lvl 37 druid alone.  Didn't quite happen.  If you're going in you better be good at dps, cause there is a lot of healing that will go on and mana seems to replenish whenever the crone wills it to.  I think i had the crone down to half health 2x and 3/4 hp another 2x and each resulted in a full heal and me watching my mana disappear as i'm trying to keep alive.

Difficult part may have been that the crone was receiving heals from below... Tried to pull her outta the hut and onto the ledge, but she was very difficult to move.  Every time i backed out she immediately went to magic.  Gonna go back at lvl 39/40 or with a rogue and try again.

I solo'd this last night as a 44 hunter. Not too difficult at all, although my poor pet snuffed it 12 times. Sometimes you try to pull 1 and 5 come to the party ! Oops ! Time to 'Feign Death' and let the pet take one for the team.

I only died once - the bats surprised me and I let my guard down. Other than that, as long as you keep your pet happy (i.e. fed) it's very do-able. All it takes is some patience. Make sure you always set traps before you let loose with the pet and the arrows ! This is critical if the pet loses aggro and you have to melee.

The crone herself was surprisingly easy to take down, as I caught her all alone. Amazing ! Got some decent loot, including a decent mail helm off of one of the lesser bosses. As soon as I turn lvl 45 I plan to do the instance 'accross the street', Razorfen Downs, solo. Should take a bunch of hours, but I'll be packing tons of meat for the owl and health/mana potions for moi.

I've run this instance a few times as Horde, and while it's fun and I plan to go back, it's reasonably hard with a good level-appropriate group. I wouldn't count on soloing it like a couple posts above. 

Easier to find if you've played the other side and know the Barrens, but directions above are great. It really is easy to walk into the much-harder Razorfen Downs instead of Razorfen Kraul, right across the road from each other, if you don't already know the way. A bit hard getting an Alliance group to go in here, though. It's not a bad walk from Ratchet or even Theramore compared to getting to Scarlet Monastery from Southsore, but folks aren't as excited about going.

There are two Razorfen areas before the lift.  The one the Crone is Razorfen Kraul (to the west of the path). There are level 22 - 23 elites out the front (rather than level 32 - 33's out the front of the other Razorfen area).  

Also, when fighting the mistriss herself - note that she can regen ALL (yes all) her mana in one spell, so trying to keep her drained doesn't work too well.  She will also throw up a shield at the worst possible time.

This starts off from Lonebrow's Journal.
Note that this quest does not appear ! on the minimap, so you must find the dwarf body yourself. but it's simple. Go down the Great lift, take your right and go to the dead dwarf. Click the journal.
After you turned the quest in Thalnar(Feralas or w/e it's called), go back up the great lift. and RFK is very close to it.
Just stay to your right. There are boars below you at a certain point. Ignore these. Even if you/your group are planning to do the escort quest, it's much quicker to jump down after Charlga.
You'll soon come across an intersection with 3 other paths. The ones to your right/left lead to optional bosses. For the Medallion, keep going straight.
Once you reach the bat cave, killing the guards of the force field is just another optional boss. You might also come across a rare bat. Once you see more razorfen, keep going, Charlga Razorflank is hiding in a hut, so make sure you don't just charge up there unless you're a high lv.
She mainly casts Chain Bolts, so casters will want to stay back. When around 30% health, she will cast a shield, wiping all debuffs, and becoming immune. Once it's gone, continue and she'll be dead
Rewards 4650 xp post-2.3.

As a level 36 enhancement shaman (with BOA chest, shoulders and 2her) I was able to get to her and solo her. Keep to the right always, don't jump down, and cross the (3 or 4) rope bridges when you get to them. You should reach the cave full of bats, most of which are easy to dodge, then up into where Razorflank hangs out. The mobs I aggro'd were usually the quillboar champions in front of several passages which I could not get by without pulling. They were actually harder than the boss was. She isn't interruptable, but at my level many of her chain bolts missed. A single lesser healing wave healed me to full after the fight.

Again, the hardest part was getting to her.

I just finished soloing Galgann as a level 42 Protection Paladin, a few tips about how to get there and kill Galgann:
 
I used the back entrance wich is described by the comments above, the first mob you have to kill is a 7k giant. He isn't very hard and only needs a bit of AoE to kill the adds he makes. When you have killed him, the hardest part before Galgann is next. There are two digger and one geomancer. I suggest to kill the miners first. I killed one miner and died, and when I respawned there were only 2 left, so that was cake, you only need to die. When you've killed them, you have kinda made it to Galgann, there are only bats patrolling. You only need to watch out for the scorpids, they have low health but do very fast, constant damage if you dont AoE them down quickly. When you've killed them you do some pretty easy trash where Galgann is.

Galgann:

Galgann has two geomancer (thankfully not miners, that'd be a nightmare). when you are ready, pick one of the geomancer and DPS them down A.S.A.P. This is very hard, and it could be good to be running around killing the adds, since Galgann does Fire Nova wich is.. bad, but you can decrase the damage it deals by moving far away from him. When the add is dead, DPS the other one and be running around to avoid the Nova. When he is dead,  Galgann does not have much mana left, and just DPS him down, I needed one potion and a bubble. Note that he is immune to stun, so Fire Nova can't be interrupted

Clarification:

Both Horde and Alliance can get this quest.

Alliance can get in Darnassus BUT you don't have to go there first! Here's why --> Basically, the quest in Darnassus is to find the guy. You find him in BFD. The quest is completed. Done, done, done. He already has another quest, to kill the boss Kelris (which leads to your reward of the Gravestone Scepter or Artic Buckler). **Essentially, you do not have to go to Darnassus first.

To find the guy to get the quest (for BOTH Horde and Alliance), whose name is Argent Guard Thaelrid, you have to see where the turtle boss is (Ghamoo-ra) and check the nodes.

Check this link: https://www.wowhead.com/forever/zone=92 and look at where Thaelrid's name is.

You only need to kill Kelris. You can also have the person running you clear everything prior to Kelris. You just need to be there to loot the head.

(If the rewards were all you wanted, you do not have to light/gear the fires. It sends  aves for each fire lit and mobs come. That activates the door for the hydra boss. You can just leave after looting the head)

For Horde, it's at Elder Rise at Thunderbluff.

Look for yellow dot!

Have fun.

forever.body:
Location is 48,91

Okay, it took some time and clicking to actually locate a nice area, but here it is: 

After you enter the dungeon, travel along the tunel until your first T-junction. 

Take the LEFT path 

Go along until you come to what appears to be a dead-end ledge. There is actually a large green wine to your RIGHT, which is a bridge. 

Taking this bridge. 

The area directly at the end of this bridge is blueleaf tuber country. Once I summoned the snufflenose, I didn't even need to move. Just keep clicking on the command stick.
For those of you having trouble locating them, the crate, manual and control stick are beside mizzyrix. Outside the general store in Ratchet.

1. When you enter instance, go straight, if you see vines and hogs (called Raging Agam'ar's) you're in the right spot.
2. Kill a bunch of hogs
3. Stand on vine.
4. Click crate with holes, be careful you can only do this 5 times, so make sure you're on right spot (you can check if you're on the right spot if your snufflenose command stick works- that is, it keeps shining when you click it and it doesnt say failed)
5. Gophers. Once you see them, CLICK your snufflenose command stick ONCE. The gophers sniff around come up to you and turn into an HERB (looks like one)
6. Click on the herb and BAM you have collected a blueleaf tuber.

Such a confusing quest if ya don't know what you're doing, took me & my group a LONG time, lol.

if u still dont get it with the blueleaf tubers, read this. first, collect the crate of holes, snufflesnose manual book and the command stick, they r located just left of the quest giver. when inside the dungeon, take the path that goes to the left, and keep going until u meat the first bridge, and a lot of boars down below. summon the gopher and make him dig. do this a couple of times and ure finished.

Just finished this quest. Not sure how randomized the contents are, but what I got when I opened my A Small Container Of Gems follows:

1x Moss Agate
1x Iridescent Pearl
1x Jewelery Box (unique 6 slot container, soulbound)
2x Small Lustrous Pearl
2x Tigerseye

Equip the crate.  When you get up the branch, use the crate to make a snufflenose.  He's a level 1 critter.  As soon as he's summoned, use the Command stick and he'll dig for a minute and up will pop a Blueleaf Tuber plant.  Harvest and you're done.  For me I just stayed in one place, using the vine method.  I don't know how you'd get up there solo though, as I was already 33 when I finally figured this stuff out.

From the start of the instance, go left and go straight until you reach the ledge that has a green "bridge".
On that bridge click on the box, it should summon a hamster.
Then click on the stick and don't move for 5-8 seconds. The hamster will spawn the quest item beneath it.

Repeat until done.

As posted before, and confirmed.
Go to south in Barrens, just before Lift, west side.
Fight into the instance entry.
Then fight in instance, turning LEFT at the fork.
Most fights can be timed to pull one or two in the mobs.
You reach the bridge as you encounter the last two guards to either side of it. Kill them.
Once you are here Release the Hounds!
Oops, click the box to release the gopher.
As it wonders around, simply click the Stick.
The Gopher will smell around for a few seconds and then a tuber will appear. Harvest it and repeat.
I had no respawn in this area and no adds, so once you are there, it is easy. Just click the stick and wait for the tuber to appear, it might take a few seconds.

1. Enter Uldaman's front entrance.

2. Walk in and the screen will show you enter "Excavation Center", continue forward and go under tunnel.

3. Screen will show you back in "Uldaman". Continue forward and screen will show you in "Dig One". Upon entering "Dig One", follow the path left. Do not jump off the edge to the instance portal.

4. At the first fork in the road. Go left and screen will show you again in "Uldaman". As the word "Uldaman" pops up; you are again in a fork on the road. Left = Dwarves  -*-  Right = Troggs. Go right towards the Troggs.

5. Continue forward and the screen shows you enter "North Common Hall".
6. Go through the tiled hallway, and when you enter the room; go towards the far wall in-front of you. Then look towards the right, and the chest is there on the floor.

*Note: Standing on the box. I have these coordinates: 53,62.

*Note: I put a picture here showing the box location, and some tips for rogues looking to solo this quest.

~Lie

forever.body:
As has been noted, he spawns in Moonbrook, east of the fountain, just before the road turns north. He then walks along the Old Coast Road until he gets near the Gold Coast Quarry, then runs down the ravine into the Quarry to a spot fairly far in, but not the very back. This is one of the two times he runs, the other being when low on health. And yes, he hauls butt, even when critical.

Anyways, after that he walks back out and up the road to the Jangolode mine, and into the back of there and back out. Time spent in the Quarry is less than 2 minutes, in the Mine a bit upwards of 3. Assuming he hasn't died yet, he then ambles back south down the same route he took up, until a point somewhere between Moonbrook and the Quarry. At this point he seemed to just be travelling back and forth over a small section of road, until someone came up and killed him. I'd been tracking him for more spawns than I care to recall, so I stopped at that point. Oh, the respawn time is about 4 and a half minutes, usually.

He's fairly easy to kill, nothing special about him. But feel free to group with anyone else with the quest, everyone in the group that kills him will be able to loot the message. The respawn is short, but why waste the time?

Edit: Just occured to me, he won't attack you on sight. You can walk right next to him, and he'll ignore you. I'm pretty sure he won't even assist other Defias, but I could be wrong.

forever.body: The name "Pool of Tears" probably refers to the pool of tears from players as they scratch their eyes out from pure frustration over this quest. Don't let the screenshots fool you, the artifacts are small and harder to find than a clean spot on a troll.

There are quite a few of these artifacts around the shoreline and on the water shelf before it drops into the deepest part of the lake.

The artifacts are small and can be either bowls or something resembling a pyramid.

74,47
71,59
66.59
65,55
65,51
67.45
The artifacts are scattered under the water surrounding Sunken Temple (70, 53). Very easy but slightly time consuming.

First look around the entire pool by all the eygiptian looking walls and stones. Then look around the top ring of the pool thats close to the surface then look at the bottom of the pool. If you dont have all 10 rinse and repeat. I got all mine in 15 mins.
Disable ground clutter in System -> Graphics -> Ground Clutter, this helps a lot

This quest really shouldn't be marked as "(Elite)" any more.

In ages past, the dragonkin that patrolled the area were, indeed, Elites.  But as of ... what was it?  1.11?  1.12? ... these dragonkin aren't elite any more, and are easily soloable like any other world-mob of the same level.

In fact, you don't even have to fight them.  The artifacts are strewn around the area, including under water, and are usually a safe distance from the Wyrmkin and Scalebane mobs.

Just did this quest, and it was extremely frustrating.  I used Questie to figure out where the locations were.   Some notes about this quest:

[ol]
[li]It helps to turn down both Environment Detail and Ground Clutter to 1 (you can find both of these together in the System -> Graphics menu) [/li]
[li]Some of the artifacts are inside the temple.  Ignore these if you are solo (you can tell they are in the temple because you will switch areas from the Swamp of Sorrows to the Temple of Atal'Hakkar), as there are elite enemies inside the temple[/li]
[li]Like all gather quests, the artifacts themselves are not shareable.  So, I recommend you do this one solo.[/li]
[li]There are artifacts outside the temple.  A few are underwater, and a few are on the shoreline.  [b]For some of the ones on the shoreline, Questie is incorrect and will show the artifact being there when it's not.[/b][/li]
[li]The ones near the shoreline and underwater outside the temple do not have any elite enemies near them.  So even though the quest is elite, as long as you stay outside the temple you should be able to easily solo this around level 38-43 (just be able to kill the odd dragonscale that you aggro)[/li]
[/ol]

For anyone doing this quest on Forever during peak hours: don't waste all your time diving into the deep parts of the lake, especially when lots of players are competing for artifacts.

Artifacts also spawn on dry land along the shoreline and in very shallow water where you can simply walk instead of swimming.

I recommend checking those areas first. It can save you a lot of time and frustration.
Don't bother going underwater at all, look around the shallows and its a lot quicker. Got all mine in a couple of sweeps.

I followed the advice above I swept the shore and got 2, I swam round the shelf before it got deep and got 4 more, then I swam around and dived as I saw them, I don't know what everyone is talking about I thought they were quite easy to spot and had no issues, 15 minutes tops, easy xp.

[b]Confirmed in Classic.[/b] All information appears to be correct.

This quest starts in Stonard, Swamp of Sorrows, from  Fel'Zerul usptairs.

The fetish drop rate is low. You can farm the fetishes outside of the instance if need be.They also drop from elites inside as well.

This is a HORDE ONLY quest in the Sunken Temple. However, there is a similar chain for the alliance.

The reward isn't too bad.  I use it with my druid when I need to tank.  It'd be nice if the duration for the armor up was more like what you get with Mark of the Chosen, but it does come in handy.

The fetish drop rate was kinda low, however.  I ended up doing it solo by killing trolls outside the instance, and it took a long time to complete.  Later I did a 4-man ST run where one of the others in the party didn't have the quest.  Nevertheless, the two who were doing it had to kill trolls outside the instance after we were done to finish it.
These drop from the elite mobs inside so no worry =)

Don't let the trinket reward pull you in too much.

This quest is not to be done alone. I figured that as I am underleveled (46) I could still kill the trolls that drop these Fetishes, since they're the same level and I can kill them 1 by 1. The drop rate on the fetishes is 5%, which means that on average, you'll need to kill 400 trolls to get all 20.

On top of it taking insanely long to complete, going into the place where you find trolls takes time too because of all the Oozes and Nagas. You'll also have to dodge the patrolling NPCs while trying to figure out who to pull next.

Basically a TL;DR : Just get a dungeon group. Don't try to solo.

Rocs:  Fly to Gadgetzan (Tanaris) and run nearly straight south from the griffon area.  There you will find skeletal remains of great beasts--there were 2 very near the town--and Rocs/Fire Rocs and Hyenas.  I was able to get drops off both kinds of Rocs.  Also, I had to kill about 40 to get my 3 gizzards.

Ironfur Bears:  Fly to Feralas and go west.  You will run into the bears fairly quickly.  I killed 4 bears to get 3 livers.

Groddoc Apes:  Continue west after killing bears (but beware of the level 55 mobs east on the path from the griffon area!), just past the first mountain range, but before the High Wilderness area.  I killed 5 apes to get 3 livers.

- Elisabet

I just figured I'd mention this, since it wasn't obvious: Any time you gain reputation with any single alliance/horde faction (I.e. Orgrimmar, Darnassus, etc), you always automatically get a quarter of the reputation with each of the other factions as well. 

In this case, you'd not only get 125 rep with Exodar, but also with Darnassus, Stormwind and Gnomeregan as well.

Edit: It doesn't actually show it in your combat log - it only shows that you gained rep with the main faction involved. But if you actually look at your rep screen before and after turning in a quest, you'll see that they've increased. Also, this isn't the case for ALL quests... Just most of them. Runecloth turn-ins for instance, only give rep with one faction.

I just figured I'd mention this, since it wasn't obvious: Any time you gain reputation with any single alliance/horde faction (I.e. Orgrimmar, Darnassus, etc), you always automatically get a quarter of the reputation with each of the other factions as well. 

In this case, you'd not only get 125 rep with Exodar, but also with Darnassus, Stormwind and Gnomeregan as well.

Edit: It doesn't actually show it in your combat log - it only shows that you gained rep with the main faction involved. But if you actually look at your rep screen before and after turning in a quest, you'll see that they've increased. Also, this isn't the case for ALL quests... Just most of them. Runecloth turn-ins for instance, only give rep with one faction.

Since many people are trying out these low-level dungeons since the new dungeon tool appeared, perhaps for the first time, I thought it might be nice to make a summary of quests for WC for Alliance characters. Note that, for the Alliance, there isn't a quest for killing any of the bosses, although there is a quest triggered by a drop from the final boss.

I don't really know if coordinates will help, but some people will keep asking for them.

Go on top of the mountain.  There's many ways up.

Once you are on the top, go towards 46,33.  This is the leg that leads to the caverns.

As you descend off of that leg (south), you'll come to a giant granite slab.  This slab is basically WC.  As soon as you step on it, the map key will no longer give you coordinates, since it thinks you are in an instance.  45,36 is probably about the center of the slab.

As you continue to walk towards the front, you'll see there are a few drop offs.  The first drop off is easy, since there's only one ledge the whole way along.

The second drop off that you need to make is to the nose.  Look around until you find it, since if you miss, you will have to start over.

The third drop you have to make is into the west-most eye.  The face would tell you it was his right eye.  It looks like you might not find a footing to land on, but it isn't really all that hard.  Of course, if you go into the east eye, then you'll have to start over.  This drop off is about 45,38, but that won't help you much.

That's it!

You first need to finish a quest called Raptor Horns from the same quest giver to get this quest (for the horde at least; I don't know about alliance but WC isn't really an alliance dungeon).

[b]Alliance Quests for Wailing Caverns[/b]

Since many people are trying out these low-level dungeons since the new dungeon tool appeared, perhaps for the first time, I thought it might be nice to make a summary of quests for WC for Alliance characters. Note that, for the Alliance, there isn't a quest for killing any of the bosses, although there is a quest triggered by a drop from the final boss.

Also note that since the mobs in the entry area (outside of the actual instance) are not elite, three of the four quests can be completed without actually grouping or entering the instance, as long as you're a high enough level to handle these non-elite mobs. On the other hand, since many people will be zoning directly in to the instance using the new tool, it's important to note that three of the four can be completed in the instance itself.

There are no pre-requisites to getting this quest.[/li]
[li][url=http://www.wowhead.com/?quest=1486]Deviate Hides[/url] - Also obtained from the cave outside WC. This quest can be completed either inside or outside the instance. Again, there is no pre-requisite for this quest.[/li]

Soloing this as a 15 Priest was not an issue.  This quest is a lot easier to solo now that escort NPCs are not quite as pants-on-head retarded as they once were.

In ye olden days of yore, if enemies aggroed you, the escortee would gleefully disregard your plight and keep walking while you were trying to keep yourself alive.  Typically said escortee would then pull the next four mobs onto himself while you're still fighting the first one, die in roughly two seconds, and then you'd tend to join him shortly after.  But in this modern, glorious age, the escort AI will now stop and assist when [i]you[/i] are attacked.  Apparently Blizzard decided that the hunter/warlock pet defensive AI might be useful for these NPCs.  Knowing this mechanic, you can do some preemptive pulls and avoid getting shoved into a 6-on-2 fight.  Just note that merely [i]aggroing[/i] something will [i]not[/i] switch the escort to attack mode -- you must [i]take damage[/i] before the AI switches from walking to assisting.

Also, the Defias Traitor can be healed [i]and buffed[/i] with any means you may have, so [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?spell=1244]charge him up[/url] before you step into Moonbrook.

The Blackfathom deeps part was easy, except a lot of travel. You can go into the dungeon itself, or you can kill some lvl 22 elite nagas at the entrance. I did the first thing. REMEMBER to take the Gem quest from Darkshore, it's in the bulding to the left from the shipyard bridge coming from the ships.

The DM part is easy, just don't forget to loot.

The Lock Modan part was the easiest. The box is among some lvl 18 ogres which are easy to deal with. I walked among them at lvl 27.

All in all takes two or three dedicated evenings.

I'm a 25 Ret Pally (I was a twink at 19 so not everything will be just as easy for you), and i'm flying to IF to turn the quest in as I write this.  This is how you get each piece:

The first section, where you have to defend Daphne Stilwell from the Defias is not too hard, and not too easy.  It's really yourself that you have to look out, since she has a very good amount of hp, and regains it after each 'wave'.

For the Whitestone Oak Lumber in Deadmines, I can solo until the ogre, but since you need ranged to pull him, I suggest a group.  You just have to get to the goblins, and they should drop it the very first kill.

For the Jordan's Refined Ore Shipment, you have to go to Loch Modan, in Thelsamar, into the house with the Tailoring Supplies guy on the porch.  Talk to Bailor Stonehand, and take his quest.  Then go Northeast across the lake until you start seeing the ogre encampment.  Go in, and keep going until you reach a tree with the item you need under it.  Grab it and finish the quest for the shipment.

For the Smithing Hammer, Get to Southshore (Run there if you do not have the flightpaths), and then run east along the road until you reach Silverpine Forest.  Follow the road up the hill and into SFK.  You may need a group for this, but since you're a pally, you might have Turn Undead.

I did this quest at 23, which i think is the lowest you can be unless you are in a group and I think that a group would have helped sometimes.

The first one I did was the ore and it is by far the easiest. The ore is next to a tree in the middle of the ogre place, not in a cave.

The next one that I did was the lumber. I just got in a group for VC and got the lumber as we ran through the place.

After that I headed to Auberdine by way of boat and got the gem quest. I just ran down the coastline unill I got to the ruins. The place you go in is one of the first ones one the left if you are looking at it from the coast. I just went in and swam under the water to get to the entrance. I had to kill a few saytr's to get to the tide priestess but i just killed them one at a time untill i got to her. I killed her easily and got the gem. Then you just have to go back to Thundris.

Finally is the Shadowfang Keep part. This is possible to solo at 23. Once inside you go to the right and immediatly run into a wolf and a worgen thing. I couldnt ever kill both at once so I would just kill the worgen guy, run out of the instance, heal up, and head back in and fight the wolf(which will immediatly attack you when you zone in). Work your way up the winding stairs untill you come to an empty hallway. At the end to the right is the door that leads to the stables. Because it is closed you have to let lose a guy locked up in a jail cell. At the end of the hallway to the left is where you have to go

Grabbed the quest just outside Ironforge gates and headed to Deadmines. Farmed some exp there first, did the Deadmines part while doing normal dungeon runs at level 22, soloed the others at lvl24.

Dun Morogh part was really easy, just remember to take the quest from Thelsamar, go loot the item at the elite ogre area and return the quest. Very easy to avoid the ogres and loot it, though the ogres don't do much damage anyways.

BFD part was really easy too, just lots of running. Remember to take the quest from Darkshore here too. Quest item dropped from first elite I saw when heading to BFD, no need to enter dungeon or even go near the entrance. Grabbed Astranaar fp while in Ashenvale and flew back to Darkshore to deliver quest.

SFK part was soloable at 24 with sword&shield. Did the first packs (wolf + worgen) one by one focusing wolf first (dies faster), kept retri aura and blessing of wisdom on and it was np. First boss was just as easy with same tactics. Then cleared the left side of the next "inner yard" area. Had to pull couple worgens there at once but it was np at all, they do antimagic shield anyways so just switched to devotion aura. Just remember to heal up early. Looted the quest item next to the horses, absolutely no cooldowns needed here either.

Hearthstoned to Ironforge and returned the quest outside the gates. 875 exp from returning the first part and 2200 exp and AN AMAZING 2H MACE from the second part ^^

main.body:
There are the four items needed to complete this quest and two of those item will require an additional quest to be picked up.

Whitestone Oak Lumber:  This is dropped from the goblin woodworkers inside deadmines inside the mast making room.  Its the room with the large logs stacked around.

Jordans Refined Ore Shipment:  This will require an additional quest acuired from Bailor Stonehand inside Thelsamar.  http://www.wowhead.com/?npc=6241  Hes down stairs inside the house with the tailoring merchant outside.  Once you acuire the quest the ore can be found from a box at aproximetly 71,21
http://www.wowhead.com/?object=92420  Return the box to Stonehand and he will give you the refined Ore.

Jordans Smithing Hammer:  No additional quest is needed.  You will need to travel to Silverpine Forest to Shadowfang keep which is located just north of Pyrewood Village.  You will find the hammer inside the stables located in the courtyard of the instance.
http://atlasmod.com/Maps/ShadowfangKeep.jpg
The stablesare located just north of the letter B on the map.  If you are around lvl 20 you will either need a full group or a lvl 60 to get you to that area.

Purified Core Gem:  The final piece requires that you travel to Kalimador.  You will need to take the boat from menethil to Darnassus (Teldrassil).  Be sure to stop by the gryphon masters to acuire new flightpaths.  You will need to take the boat from Teldrassil to darkshore which is just on the otherside of the dock.  Once i

The smithing hammer is probably the hardest part of this quest due to difficulty in finding groups to Shadow Fang Keep. It is however soloable. I did this at level 22 solo so it is definetly doable. Some tips to doing this are that if you have to fight mobs in a group try pulling them near the entrance to the instance. Kill one of them and zone out. Eat + drink and come back in and repeat until you have cleared that pull. For the part where you free the guy from the cell, you can just jump down and free him and if you die he will still open the gate for you. In the couryard, work on clearing the left wall so that you have a clear path to the stables. If you get the debuff that periodically summons the spirits using concecration when they spawn quickly kill them.

Might want to pick up "Onward to Ashenvale" from Thundris Windreaver while you're there...  9 Silver and some XP to talk to somewhere in Astranaar, the inn-city in Ashenvale.  About a 2 minute run (non-speed-increase) from the top of the zone, and also where the flighpath is.

Regarding soloing SFK....

I did it on my level 20 retri pala with green items apart from the Cruel Barb from the deadmines, would recommend a few health pots too.

To reiterate what one of the other posters said about SFK, it is advisable to pull multiple mobs back to the entrance, or if too far away just kill one and try to run out as fast as you can, for the gate I just used Divine Protection and quickly talked to the NPC, death is a given here. 

One thing I found out is that when up the second set of stairs I think it was (There will be a raised platform to your left with a wolf and a worgen on it) you can aggro the worgen from the lower platform and the wolf doesn't come after you along with him, maybe a fluke, worth testing though, but also worth hanging a right whilst getting rid of the other two mobs so you don't agro him too soon.

When in the courtyard it is fairly easy to get along the left side, there is only one double pull and I found it best to get rid of one of the wolves and one the ghosts to make sure I didn't get agro problems. The worgen do put on an anti-magic shield but it has a short duration and shouldn't cause too much bother.

Once you have killed the mobs on the left by the wall you can get into the stables just enough to get the quest item without agroing anyone inside.

Hope this helps someone, and as this is my first post to wowhead I hope I didn't make any community nonos.

Just soloed the entire quest at level 22.  It CAN be done.

The Ore Shipment is cake since Blizz nerfed the ogres in Loch Modan.  The Kor Gem is just a lot of running to get to BFD.  You have to go underwater and into the cave, but you don't need to enter the actual instance. 

The tricky part starts with the smithing hammer.  The pulls in SFK are all 2 at a time, if done right, and very easily managed (I didn't need to exit the portal, but I suppose you could do that if you're not burning pots/scrolls/elixirs).  As said above, the one death in the jail cell area is unavoidable - that boss simply cannot be taken down alone at that level.  All I did was jump down, bubble, open the cell and talk to the NPC, and then died.  As long as you don't release until the dude gets the door open, you can run back and finish up with minimal effort.

In Deadmines, Rhak'zor is very soloable with the right consumables up, and even easier if you spend a little money on a Clefthide Armor Kit for your pants.  After that, it's a cakewalk to the mast room.  Watch out for the pat after Rhak'zor, then just pull the first goblin in the room and get your lumber.  

Personally, I think doing it all solo is a good way to hone your skill and challenge your wits a bit - plus the XP is a little better. :-)  I picked up the quest after I dinged 22, and was nearly 23 before I turned it in, doing no other questing in the interim.

Started this quest at level 21, finished at level 22. Getting the gem and ore were easy, just took some travel time. I died once getting the wood. The sub boss was a long, but easy fight, bring a good healing potion with you, and take your time, he's not to hard to beat. Watch the goblins when entering the ship building room, only pull the one, and stay close to the door, else you'll get mobbed. The hammer took the longest. When traveling, stick to the center of the road so you don't pull agro. I died once in the dungeon, at the cells, pull carefully. When you get to the court yard, like the others said, stick to the left side, against the wall. You'll deal with groups of 2 while being attacked by minor lower level spirits. Once you make it to the stables grab the hammer and hearth out.

Soloed the entire quest at Level 21, with no twink gear at all, all quest gear and stuff that dropped for me. Loch Modan and BFD are easy. Just take it slow in SFK, and you shouldn't have too much of a problem, just kite packs of two to the instance portal and zone out immediately after killing one. When you get close to Rethilgore, strip naked, use Hand of Protection, and talk to the mage who opens the courtyard door before the mobs kill you. At that point you can resume your slow crawl towards Jordan's hammer. The only truly difficult part is Rhahk'Zor in the Deadmines. To beat him, I had to use Divine Protection, a Healing Potion, Lay on Hands, and Lifeblood (rank 2). I don't think I could have done it without Lifeblood.

Vancleef isn't too hard if done well. You'll have encountered harder bosses and areas in the instance, such as the large tauren captain who stuns, and the upper deck with Cookie and his friends. Apart from the rogues, he isn't too hard to kill. Just be prepared.
A mage can polymorph one, a rogue can sap one. Make sure your party is on the deck, as standing below can mean you can't cast as your target is not in view. The tank should attack Vancleef, with DPS backup. Perhaps get one party member to run around, with the 2 bodyguards following, while the other 4 bring down the boss. When VC is dead, it is easy to mop up the others.
A party of about level 20+ should not find killing this too difficult, provided your party is well-balanced (tank, healer, DPS) and can co-operate well.

Vancleef drops some really good loot, such as the famed Cruel Barb, a green polearm, and other good loot. He also drops a letter, starting a very large quest series which leads onto a reward - The Seal of Wrynn, a ring which will last you until about level 50!

Shouldn't take your group more than an hour and a half to do this entire instance.  I'll lay out some working strategies as best I can.

In the corridors, which is most of the zone, you just need to watch what/how you pull.  I've pulled the entire dungeon as a level 22 Hunter and never gotten more than one add.  You really need someone with a ranged attack to pull.  If it's a caster who shouldn't be tanking, they need to use their lowest level spell to pull with, so they don't cause much initial aggro.  If it HAS to be a paladin or druid, then they need to pull the mob and back up quite a bit.  Runners in here will get you adds, which cause wipes.

The first boss is an ogre.  He walks up and down a path.  If you've never done this before, watch him a couple times, and pull him when he's farthest from the door to avoid adds.  There is a patrol after him, which will need to be neutralized before going through teh door.

The next boss is the Shredder, and it's pilot (Sneed?).  This is fairly simple, as the shredder also has a set path.  Pull him just as he begins walking up the hill, but make sure all the goblins around the wood are dead.  The second and final patrol is here.

Next, you go down another corridor and into the Foundry.  This is where most groups wipe.  It is IMPERATIVE that your puller pay attention to the pathing of the goblins. Hopefully you didn't skip through the quest text throughout this quest chain. It was, and still is, a simple but marvellous story in which it is ponderous if the adventurers truly were the heroes for slaying VanCleef, despite his trespasses. Here's a rundown of what transpired throughout the quest chain:

Gryan Stoutmantle of Westfall learns that a faction calling themselves the Defias Brotherhood is responsible for driving the people of Westfall from their homes. He tasks the player to seek the aid of Wiley the Black in Lakeshire - a rogue who owes Stoutmantle a favor.

Wiley complies with the request for information, and has the player return a note to Stoutmantle. The note states that the Brotherhood is larger than previously thought, and that the Kobolds and Gnolls of Westfall are also part of the conspiracy. They have hired Goblins to produce the mechanical harvest golems seen throughout Westfall. The note also states that they have an underground network from Booty Bay as far as Stormwind Keep, and that they are working on a weapon of mass destruction. It also mentions the name "Stonemasons."

Upon returning the note to Stoutmantle, he ponders if Wiley mentioning the Stonemasons was a slip of tongue, and perhaps they are connected to the Brotherhood. He asks the player to speak to Matthias Shaw of SI:7 for more information.

On my level 22 rogue (who's a completionist and didn't want to leave this quest behind), I was able to solo this guy. The regular guys at the beginning you can kind of single pull and fight on their own to get the miner cards, that's not hard (as long as you pull 1 or 2 at a time, with having to use cooldowns to down 2 at once), but Thistlenettle has a bunch of guys around him so even if you stealth to him and blow your cooldowns, you'll be fighting him along with 2 or 3 other undead, so here's how I did it:

If you stealth ALL the way to the end, get as far into the corner as you can and range-pull the 1 or 2 undead there and down them, then you will have more room to work with from the end of that cave to Thistlenettle. Wait for your CD's to come back, then down any leftover undead between you and Thistlenettle. For me, it was possible to pull Thistlenettle eventually without pulling anyone else, although there was another undead close by that CAN aggro if you pull Thistlenettle while they are standing closer to each other.

Get your badge for the quest (and probably a green as well) and stealth out of there. Done.

Some tips for Alliance:
Pick up Retrieval for Mauren (https://www.wowhead.com/forever/quest=1078/retrieval-for-mauren 6 crystallized scales, as you may be killing these Basilisks that get in your way). You pass by about 4-5 before you get to the vale, might as well start killing them.

While going thru Windshear Crag, follow the west side and you'll find a hut with a goblin.  Get the quest Super Reaper 6000 (https://www.wowhead.com/forever/quest=1093/super-reaper-6000) and go back to the big stationary machine, climb up and kill the Operators, they should drop the plans. https://www.wowhead.com/forever/search=fire+hardened

There are the full rewards for this quest. They are fairly impressive, but you might need quite a bit of help for completing the quest in the first place. The Hauberk is especially impressive, but a Shining Silver Breastplate can be used if you'd rather not brave the dangers of collecting those items. =)

So, I hear a lot of "this armor sucks" and such. Basically, it's the mirror of a Shining Silver Breastplate (The Str and Stam values are flipped). The pro to this is the 1/hour 30 Rage, which, if you're fighting a boss or a small group of enemies, can be very nice. Also, it doesn't use your potion cooldown, so you can still use a healing potion.

This isn't the only item you get for being a 20+ Warrior, though. And I think people fail to see it. After you complete this quest, you talk to Grimand Elmore and he gives you a quest that nets you a Fire Hardened Coif, with (I think) +7 Strength and +8 Stamina (Somewhere in that ballpark). This was the first helmet I got and far better than the other one I saw (Which was +6 Spirit/Stamina, not too useful for a Warrior aside from the Stam). Then, after completing that quest, there's a guy in Ironforge in the Gnome area (Where you get all the Gnomer quests) who gives you a third quest which nets you new gloves with +6 Str/Stam. All in all, just from the quests (Not counting all the kills from mobs/etc) I think I got 15 or 20k in XP for doing all 3 quests, not to mention far better gear than I had before.

This is for those who have Cosmos' Atlas.

Enter the instance and immediately turn right.  Work your way around to point 1 on the atlas, where "Deathstalker Adamant" and "Sorcerer Ashcrombe Rethilgore".  Release the prisoner and he'll open the door to the courtyard.

[b]None of the mobs in the couryard drop the Large Soran'ruk Fragment.[/b]  Only the Shadowfang Darksouls do.  So work your way through the courtyard and up a ramp that curves to the left leading to point 2 on the atlas where Razorclaw the Butcher is.

My fragment dropped with the first Shadowfang Darksoul I killed.

Happy Hunting!

The Three small shards in Black Fathom Deeps:

Ashenvale coordinates 14:15
Follow the cave all the way back to the instance, then you will have to get to the last stage right before you kill the nasty hydra boss. Special note: dont click on the alter if you decide to go ahead and kill the hydra for drops.... it will kill you and send you back outside the instance to the beginning where you drop down to go into the caves.

The Large Shard in Silverpine:

Silverpine coordinates 45:68
Entering instance, turn right, free the prisoner and enter the courtyard. The large shard should drop from a haunted survivor or one of the shadowfangs that are near the ramp area. 

Since I play alliance, and it was difficult for me to find silverpine to begin with... from Iron forge, go north into the wetlands, from there, into arathi to south shore. from south shore, go north towards hillbrad and into silverpine... 90% of the mobs along this quest are elite. bring a party, or go at a higher level (I completed this at level 33, when it was green)

The armor from this quest is good and [b]will[/b] be an upgrade for you, unless you're wearing the strength side-grade [item=2870] (which is a bit expensive to craft).

Sadly, it gets replaced almost immediately by [item=7688] (SM:GY), [item=7759] (SM trash), or [item=10328] (SM: Cath trash). If you somehow fail to get any of these three, then you will upgrade it with [item=10775] (RFD), which you should farm as it's a big upgrade.

The pieces from all of the follow-up quests are [b]NOT[/b] worth your time - [b]IGNORE THEM[/b]. The [item=7130] is sub-par to the [item=3836] (blacksmithing) and the [item=6686] (RFK), the [item=7129] are weaker than the [item=16978] (Ashenvale, Horde Q) / [item=6906] (BFD), and the [item=7132] are weaker than [item=15470] (1k Needles, Horde Q) / [item=3842] (blacksmithing).

If you link the chest piece in your hotbar and click on it, you will increase your rage by 30 but it has a 60 min cool down.  Which isn't really all that useful since the rage disappears or is used within moments.

You are given a scroll when you get the quest.  It reads:

<Name>, below are the items needed to create your armor:
Smokey Iron Ingots from the Windshear kobolds in the Windshear Mine in the Stonetalon Mountains.
Powdered Azurite from the Hillsbrad miners in Hillsbrad.
Iron bars from miners, or from iron deposits if you are a miner.
Vial of Phlogiston from a quillboar named Roogug in the Razerfen Kraul.

I have to say that the rewards from this quest, and the next ones in the chain ([item=7130], [item=7129], [item=7132]), are very underwhelming for the level when you get them.

Since you have to run RFK for the [item=6841] part, meaning level 29-31, you will likely have much better gear once you see the rewards.
As for the on-use effect on the chest you get from this quest ([item=7133]), it's great but the 1h cooldown makes even that very limited.
[i]*Edit: And a simple [item=5631] can be used every 2 minutes.[/i]

All in all a tad disappointing :/

Just got through reading everybody's comments above, and wish someone had summarized it all. So here's my shot at it. Did I miss anything?

[b]The Obsidian Power Source drops from the Obsidian Sentinel inside Uldaman.[/b]

The back entrance to Uldaman is at [b]67,44 in the Badlands[/b] in some island of rocks next to some ravine with elite dragons. Or if you don't use Cosmos, like me, then it's about 2/3 of the way across the map and a bit north of the equator. (Or if you're OCD, it's 67/100ths of the way across from the left edge of the map and 44/100ths of the way down from the top edge.)

[b]1. He reflects all "targeted" spells.[/b]

This means:
* Use ONLY melee, wand and AoE spells (and, duh, Frost Nova and Mana Shields)
* If you use fire attacks, make sure to use a fire ward (dunno if you need one otherwise...)

This also means you only need to bring along one friend if you choose the right class:
* A shaman or priest can remove any of those reflected magical effects if needed (and, duh, heal you...)
* A tank can melee without worrying about all that reflection crud
* If you pick someone who is at least level 45 (preferrably higher), then you probably won't wipe at all.

[b]2. He spawns "mini-me" adds, but gets weaker each time he does it.[/b]

This means you'll have an easier time of it if you:
* Kill each new (lower level) add before returning to the boss.
* Kill the boss after he has weakened himself by spawning a handful of adds. (Didn't see a specific number, but it

How to solo in WoW classic.

So  every comments covers some aspect, I thought I'd specifically explain how you'll solo this at any level. Enter at the back entrance, it's in a small cave in a mountain on the mid-east side of the badlands. He's the first you'll see (once opening the door) and has no adds around him.

Basically the golem will spawn adds every 20% health (aka 4 times). When they spawn they will cause the boss to deal less damage (60 dmg less per hit) but they make him immune to targeted spells.

In order to solo him just keep resetting him at 75% because while he regains his health, he keeps the (stacking) debuff meaning he will after a few resets, do next to no damage anymore. He can't gain more than 4 debuffs but that's 240 less auto attack damage and he basically hits between 5-20 at that point.

After you've reset him 4 times and engage him all you have to do is wand him down with a shield up. ocasionally you can nova / blizzard to kill the add without any reflection shenanigans or wand that down too.

note: He doesn't seem to reflect 100% of the spells either. so you could still fire some at him, but not all will stick.

You can use Detect Magic on him to see how many stacks he currently has to make sure he's dealing less damage.m
You can get the Power Source from killing the Obsidian Sentinel right at the Uldaman Backdoor(67,44)
As soon as you enter the back instance of Uldaman, he is behind the closed doors.  The back of Uldaman is at 67,44 in Badlands.

A couple of points that I don't think were very clear from everything above.  But great information from everyone...

1. AoE spells will not be reflected back at you, but the EFFECTS (stuns, slows) that proc off those spells might be reflected.  So if I hit him with a Flamestrike, I won't take any damage because I'm not in the AoE, but I MIGHT be stunned if I have that Talent and it procs.  Same with Blizzard and slowing. That being said, I've never seen him reflect Frost Nova.

2. Reflection happens about 50% of the time, but only on aimed spells.  CoC can't be reflected, however the damage from Blastwave CAN.  These are just my observations, feel free to contradict me, but I have combat logs to back this up.

3. The Guardians that splinter from the Sentinel ALSO have the spell reflection property.  They are level 35, non-elite, and go down pretty quickly. The Obsidian Sentinel is lvl 42 Elite.

4. Sometimes when you leave the instance and return, the Sentinel and his splinter will not have gone back, they will be right there.  Make sure you go in with Mana shield up, and Frost Nova ready.

5. THE MOST IMPORTANT PART
After he splinters about 4 times, and you have done the run in, run out to heal and mana up, you will now have the long fight in front of you.  If you have to leave at this point of the fight, you will be resetting all the damage you have done.
With him splintered so many times, he is very small, and does very little damag

I have always run into problems with finding Uldaman groups in general. When I did find a group that wanted to do it, they never wanted to swing by the area with the obsidian sentinel so I had pretty much given up on this quest.

I am now a level 49 frost mage, and decided to try to solo it. I followed the comments on this page and mixed some of the suggestions. Here's how I did it. (you can get all of this from above - I'm just being very specific.)

1. Make sure you have your mana gem ready to go.
2. Start off by putting up mana shield. (I also used ice barrier to save mana; it worked very well for me)
3. Drink up to full mana.
4. Frost nova the sentinel.
5. Start wanding him. Continue until your shield breaks from his damage. Cast mana shield again and keep wanding.
6. Continue to frost nova whenever the cooldown is ready.
7. When he splinters and gets a guardian, leave the instance.
8. Food and drink up outside.
9. Go back in - the sentinel and his buddy will be standing in the original place.
10. Repeat the same process, but wand the buddy first.
11. Once the buddy is dead, you can leave the instance again if necesssary to heal, but I never had to.
12. Keep repeating this, and you'll eventually end up with a dead sentinel. :)

I only used one superior healing potion, and I didn't really even have to; I was just doing it to be safe. Good luck.

I did this when I was only [i]42[/i], with a [i]47[/i] Shaman (who didnt purge unfort. but did heal some) and I found a way that made it easy.  If I relied on the Mage's abilities to regain Mana + Used Powerful Mana Potions I probably could have done it without the Shaman (Though even for just piece of mind I recomend one.)

Things I used:
[b]Gnomish Universal Remote[/b]  [u](If you cant make one, find someone who can!)[/u]

First, go in and fight the Darn guy until he spits out the Mini-Me's.
I suggest using Fireshield and then Only Fire based attack spells.  Once he has spit out a few Mini-Me's retreat from the instance.
Head back in and use your remote on the boss, then use him to attack the Mini-Me's He will kill them all and they will weaken him down quite a bit.  Once the remote wears off, fight him again using Fire Shield + Fire attacks.  Once he gets down and has Mini-Me's out (if you can't yet beat him) retreat and repeat.  After 3 or 4 tries at this He is so small and weak that it actually does not take long or much effort to take him out, only time and smooth rythem.  The key is doing enough damage to hurt him without doing so much that you blow your fire shield away before you can be ready to recast it.  Mana Shield does help a lot here but you will burn through mana fast so if you use mana shield have potions and any other means you can for mana regen.

Having done this at level 50 due to a lack of Uldaman-interested parties, I can broadly confirm the tactics recommended by previous posters.

Initially, even though I had ten levels on him, Mr Golem does a fair amount of damage. If solo at 50 or below you'll likely need a superior healing potion for the initial fight, before he spawns any guardians. I used a few small mana potions/gems in later stages.

The advice regarding leaving the instance each time he spawns a friend is spot on. Eat and drink outside, roll yourself a new mana gem, and get back in there. I didn't stay outside longer than about 2 minutes.

When you return, I recommend chaining him and his guardian with Arcane Explosion. He doesn't reflect them, it'll only take a few to take down his guardian, and it damages him too.

As soon as he shrinks to being veery small, and the guardian he spawns is much bigger than him, then you have to stick it out. At this point he does indeed do a teensy amount of damage. AoE his guardians when they show up and keep wanding. I had about 4 more guardian spawns during this last phase before he went down.

1. The split-off mobs are also 42 elites.

Don't waste mana nuking him or trying to strip his spell reflection buff - just beat on him or his split-offs (Thought about this later: if you're a solo mage you have to cast at him - use your fire,  frost or mana shields to absorb some of the damage he reflects back on you.)

The splits can make 1 or 2 adds - never saw a split make more than 2 adds, for a total of 3 with the original mob.
5. I think a group in the low 40's could handle this mob and the split-offs, as long as they focussed melee on the main guy, with off-tanks for the split-off mobs, who died

There are at least three troll hangouts. They form a sort of triangular region in the central part of SV, east of the road. 

1. the Ziata'jai Ruins (42,35) are along the road, to the east (right) of the road, between the Arena to the south and Lake to the north.  Here, the road runs almost straight and almost due north-south.  There is a Temple icon for these ruins on the Map.  This place is mostly populated with lvl 39-40 Axe Thrower and HeadSplitters.  I found only a couple Mystics or WDs nearby. 

2. the Ruins of Zul'Mamwe (46,41) lies to the SE of Ziata'jai.  There is a Temple icon on the map for this location too.  As I hunter, I used Humanoids tracking to 'scout' the area and found near zero Mystics or WDs, but saw large groupings of Warriors and others.    

3. The most promising spot I found is north and east of Ziata'Jai in the Balia'Mah Ruins (43,41).  The are about where the letter 'o' in ogre for the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound appears on the map.  I found good numbers of Mystics around here. 

It's worth noting that there are patrols, usually 3 of mixed types, patrolling the paths between these three sites.  You are warned. 

I definitely found that most Troll types were dropping Tusks (for the other quest).  But, the Fetishes are only found on the WDs and Mystics

Overall, I found the drop rate to be okay.  :-|

Good hunting!

This is a small straightfoward guide that doesn't use locs.

---
There are 4 tablets. These are interactable objects on the ground in the troll ruins. You get a gear when you pass over them even through walls so you will be able to tell when you're close.
- #1 is in Bal'lal Ruins which are just east of the basalisks on the coast and south of Zul'Kunda. The tablet is in the southwest corner of thse ruins. The easiest way here is just to clear your way to it as best you can.

- #2 is in the Vile Reef, filled with elite murlocks. Scary huh! Well, it's almost due west of Bal'lal. Swim out until you see a ruin. It'll be on the north edge of the northeast corner on the outside. Swim down from the outer edge and no murlocs will even notice you.

The 3rd & 4th Tablets are in the Ruins of Zul'Kunda in the northwest most corner of STV.
 
- #3 you can reach by going to the beach on the west side of the ruins and going up a path in the back. It is in the corner behind a wall from that angle. Going in through the front, it is in the SW most corner of Zul'Kunda. There are alot of closely-packed mobs near it so unless you're a powerhouse I'd bring friends.

- #4 is on the north side of Zul'Kunda. It is the hardest part to reach. I did it by clearing my way down the middle of the ruins, where it makes something like a road. You will reach a hairpin turn. Get up onto the divider and clear the mobs at the top of the second path where you're walking back towards the front of the ruins. After th

You can solo all of these if you're careful. I did it on my lvl 37 warrior. 

The first two are easily done. With some thought you won't have any trouble at all.

The third one is the hardest to solo in my opinion. There are a lot of closely packed mobs around it (it's at the soutwest corner of the Zul'Kunda ruins, btw). Approaching from the south I was able to clear a path to the legend with some delicate pulls. Just take your time and don't be afraid to run off if you aggro too many mobs. 

#4 can be gotten pretty easily if you know where to sneak. As you go into the Zul'kunda ruins from the east, go up the big hill to the right of the main entrance. Follow that hill north until it gets close enough to let you jump onto (not over) the outer wall. Hop on that wall and follow it all the way north. Then follow the wall west to the upper level of the waterfall. To your left you should see the legend. Pull the mobs closest to it carefull and you'll get it no problem.

These aren't drops, lest there be confusion.  There are big stone tablets leaning up against the walls in the ruins, that you can interact with.  You right-click on 'em, and it gives you a loot box, and voila! :)

Soloed with a 33 Hunter. WooHoo! People who say this is tedious are wrong. It's a challenge and fun. The only really tricky tablets were the two in Zul'Kunda:

For all you Cosmos-haters (like me!):

One of tablets is at the southwest corner of Zul'Kunda. At this corner there is a fort, then just north of that is another fort. It is in this fort at its northwest corner where you find the tablet. You can take the mobs 1 or 2 at a time if you're patient and keep your eyes open.

The second one is tougher. You can approach the east entrance to Zul'Kunda, but don't go inside. Instead, climb up the hills and walk north along the wall until you reach the steep slopes. From here, you should be able to see a small water fall inside the ruin.

Get close to the wall and you will aggro 1-2 mobs  through the wall who will somehow chase you onto the hills. Kill them (of course). Then, you can run up the steep slope near the wall and if you time it right, jump onto the wall. From there you can walk west along a very narrow ledge over the water to the waterfall (as stated above - good post). The tablet is right next to the waterfall guarded by several mobs.

If you have a pet :), send them into the mobs and loot the tablet at your liesure.

Track Humanoids, Eagle Eye, and Feign Death were awesome for this mission.

The basic idea of this quest is simple: Go to various ruins filled with baddies and interact with a stone tabled in each - usually surrounded by several mobs at once. Good things to have: Superior Healing Potion, Elixir of Water Breathing (superior or lesser- any will do).

1st Tablet - From Nessingwary's Expidition camp, head Southwest towards Kal'ai ruins.  Bypass this on the right side by climbing over a few foothills. Continue going Southwest until you find Bal'lal Ruins. Inside the Ruins there is a campfire surrounded by 9-10 mobs. And in there is the stone tablet you have to interact with. Kill the mobs (expect to fight 2 at once) until they are dead and then click the tablet. This is pretty much waht you will be doing for the all the rest of the tablets you have to interact with.

2nd Tablet - After you've gotten the first tablet, go immediately southwest from Bal'lal Ruins and into the sea. This one is a pain because the tablet is in ruins that are underwater - about midway between the island and the shoreline of the mainland. If you are a melee - that underwater breathing potion would come in handy here since the ruins are very deep. Once you get to the location, look down and see the ruins beneath you. They are inhabited by level 35-37 elite Murlocks. They are relatively close to the tablet so you may want to bring a friend for this. If you have a pet though, just send it in to draw aggro while you get to the tablet.

My group wiped twice on this before we hit on this strategy, maybe this advice will help you.  Remember, you need at least 3 people to channel the altar before you can wake the big boss (or the one in the room before this).

At first, the big boss is relatively easy to control.  Main tank can keep aggro, one or two DDers add boss damage, one or two DDers/offtanks take down the adds as they spawn, and a healer keeps everyone standing.  (The adds show as level 44 but they are easy to kill.)  Then the Stone Golem add spawns and all h*** breaks loose.  The Stone Golem is very hard to kill, plus the big boss is liable to toss a knockdown attack starting around this time which does huge damage.

My advice: Take your time and keep your powder dry (mana levels high etc.) until the Stone Golem spawns.  You should have no trouble killing the adds and whittling down the big boss before then.  When the Golem spawns, forget about him and concentrate on taking down the Big Boss immediately, using everything you have (the boss should be at low health by then).  You won't be able to kill the Stone Golem before the next Golem spawns, and pretty soon you'll be in a crowd of adds plus the boss and then you wipe.

I've done uldaman numerous times. 

I've done with several chars and several other times with lvl 43-49s in many various groups.

Lots of different strategies, most important part is:

1. Have 1/5 heal, make sure to keep agro off healer, peel adds quickly from healer if he gets the agro
2. Have 3/5 focus on Arcahedas (sunder armor and dps)
3. Have 1/5 focus on all the minions or adds (hunter or rogue do this well)
4. When the 4 elites come out, have a tank pull agro quickly and everyone just focus on archaedas.
