As was said above, the Treasure is to be found outside the actual instance. While the Alliance version of the quest item is found in the North Common Hall, you need to go to the South Common Hall for the Horde item.

Here is how you get there:

After entering the front entrance, go forward until you enter the "Excavation Center". There is a sort of tunnel there - or rather, a bridge that you can walk underneath. You need to go underneath that bridge. Moving forward, you will enter "Dig One" after a bit. Down in the dig, you will see the instance portal to your right. 
Jump down into the dig and keep the instance portal to your right. Go to the tunnel you see before you (there are two dwaves' tents to the right of the tunnel mouth.)
Walking through the tunnel will get you to a tiled hallway, the "South Common Hall". Turn left, go up the three stairs into the Hall, and the chest with the treasure is right ahead of you at the back wall, partially obscured by a pillar.

Standing directly on the box, the coordinates are 51,79 / 64,00.
Does not count toward the Loremaster Achievement. 12/8/08
Also note that the South Common Hall is north of the North Common Hall

This one is tougher than it sounds. I just finished it as my lvl 43 hunter, with a lvl 43 cat pet (turtle or bear might be a better choice for this one).

The room is not "just on the left as you enter the instance." You have to fight your way through a lot of lvl 36/37 elites ... you do keep going left ... but it's a ways to travel. I died three times. There are quite a number of self-healing lvl 37 Elite Oracles to get by, and they generally have company. Make liberal use of combustion, freezing and frost traps ... it helps. Also use Viper Sting on the Oracles so you have the mana to keep healing your pet (if you have one) or yourself if you have the ability (sadly, Hunters do not ... you have 1 healing pot per "event"). And watch out for healing totems ... the Oracles put out a lot of them in addition to casting self-heal on themselves.

With a group this would be much easier ... you can be dealing with up to 4 mobs at a time. For this 43 Hunter it was a real challenge, and I've done a lot of crowded cave and dungeon work. Don't even think about soloing the sequel quest - I did - used eyes of the beast to check it out. ha hah ... bring some friends.

If you want to avoid those elites, you can actually jump up onto the ledge and make your way completely around the left as mentioned. If you fall off, hopefully it won't be next to one, but get to one of the urns in the corner, jump on it and onto the ledge. Once I got to the dirt room, I found a stealthed trogg at the entrance, so watch out for a few of those. The rest was fairly easy. Then just exit the same way you came in on the ledge (although I did have a little more difficulty staying on due to the change in angle). I was able to make the run on my lvl 55 shadow priest.

1. I would never have found this place without the map screenshot and the description of the big red banners outside. This was my first trip to Desolace, and I would not have expected to go ALL the way south from the quest text.

2. The only way I could do this as a level 37 mage, without dying, was by keeping close to the entrance and away from the patrollers. The respawn rate really is fast enough to take on one at a time at a reasonable pace, with time to regenerate health and mana (sometimes down to half, sometimes pretty intact, depending on whether an opening frostbolt froze them in place or whether their attacks on my mage froze them in place, or whether they got to get close and hit enough to stun - they hit hard. My spec and style, best I could do was frostbolt, uninterruptable arcane missiles, frost nova, back up, repeat, unable to repeat frost nova until they were killed by more arcane missiles, fireblasts, and the occasional fireball - but they interrupted the fireball a LOT in close quarters). 

3. The other posts are SO right about avoiding the patrollers. My one death was when I went in too far and a patroller found me at half health. I used counterspell when they started casting, and oops - if you play a mage, save counterspell to block their summoning another mob. Struggling to find [npc=11561]s to kill?

If you're comfortable tanking them for a bit, pull an [npc=11559] or [npc=253272] and allow it to cast [spell=18166] or [spell=1263343]. These summoned Ravagers are identical to the naturally spawning ones, and count towards this quest's credit!

There are several "fen-type" creates in Wetlands. To complete this quest you have to kill 12 [url=https://www.wowhead.com/forever/npc=1040/fen-creeper]Fen Creepers[/url]. Unfortunately, they are invisible but you can use a macro that will help you finding them:

[code]
/cleartarget
/target Fen Creeper
/cleartarget [dead]
/run if (UnitExists("target")) then SetRaidTarget("target",8) end
[/code]

You bind this macro to a button. Clicking the button will target any nearby Fen Creeper that is alive and put a skull on it. I'm not an expert in macros and targeting so there might be a way to clean the macro up a bit. However, it works as advertised.

Since these things are invisible, thought I would help give some of the locations of the Fen Creepers that I found. If you have Cosmos you can use these  coordinates. (20,28), (20,24), (48,37), (47,32) (46,34),(47,36), (54,37), (56,46), (55,46), (51,32), (37,33). Hope this helps and good luck hunting.

Too few of these are available, especially now that the area is really crowded. I used a macro, making sure to not miss one, while running along the rivers and puddles.

/cleartarget
/targetexact Fen Creeper
/stopmacro [target=target,noexists]
/stopmacro [@target, dead]
/ping [@target] Mob Found
/cast Arcane Shot(Rank 1)

Replace Arcane Shot(Rank 1) with any instant ranged ability of your choice.

forever.body:
I've completed this 3 times this week with my level 43 priest (all shadow). The first group, we had a pally who helped with the healing. The last 2 groups, I was the only healer in the group. In addition to the already excellent comments regarding going PvP, etc, I think there are a couple of things you need to do to succeed.

Our last group had two level 50 warriors, a 49 hunter, a 47 lock and me.

1st - Gather everybody b4 you start to buff. Fort buff and shadow resist should be recast on everybody in the group. Everybody stay at or very near the TOP of the stairs UNTIL Bly and his crew start moving down. No need to move down until then. Let the mobs come to you. The main benefit to the priest is that everybody stays in your LOS (line of sight) so you can heal. I mention those 2 things in my groups. Stay at the TOP and in my LOS, that is, IF you wanna be healed, hehe. 

2nd - Use your spells wisely. I primarily use Flash Heal, PW:S and Renew. Using that as a combo is enough to get a tank through for a few seconds while you help somebody else. Flash Heal is my primary healing spell. It heals enough without generating huge amounts of agro. (I've also started using Prayer of Healing more when you notice that everybody is down about the same amount of health. Works pretty well.) Also, bounce your heals around. Don't heal the same toon 5 times in a row unless absolutely necessary. Doing that will certainly bring the agro on you. 

3rd - you have to take the opportunity in betwee

To start the quest event you have to kill the Sandfury Executioner at the top of the Temple and use the key he drops to free Sergeant Bly from his cage. 

After freeing Bly several waves of level 42-45 trolls spawn at the bottom of the steps (some but not all elite). It is best to wait at the top of the steps and kill each wave of spawns as they come to you, because if you go down the steps you may agro additional trolls. If you toggle pvp on you will get heals from the orc npc priest, but they won't usually save you from dying. After fighting several waves of trolls Bly leads you down the steps and you fight the two bosses. Neither are particularly difficult, though you do fight both at once so make sure to off-tank one of them. 

Once the bosses are killed you can talk to the goblin who will blow up the gates to Chief Ukorz Sandscalp. Do not talk to Bly until everybody is ready, because doing so causes Bly and his group to agro and attack you. Kill off the priest and lock first, then the rogue and finally Bly himself. Loot his body for the divino-matic rod and the quest is complete. 

To do this quest your group needs to be slightly higher than it does for most of the instance. Most of the members should be around level 50. Good healing and Dps is probably more important on this encounter than healing.

You do NOT need to PvP flag for the NPC to heal you.  I know this from personal experience.

I have soloed the event numerous times with my lvl 60 hunter.  At this point my success rate is about 80%.  Key to survival is protecting the weaker NPCs.  They deal significant DPS.  I discovered it's suicidal to use AOE except at the very end of attack waves.  Another lesson: its inefficient to rely on ranged weapons, due to recurring line of sight issues.  Best bet is to assume aspect of the monkey, and just dive right in, backing off occasionally if you need to bandage.

NPCs in order of priority

1) Orc Warlock
He is usually the first NPC to die.  If you protect him he will continue to cast rain of fire and put DOTs on incoming trolls.  He is an aggro magnet.  Melee attacks disrupt his rain of fire and seriously reduce his dps.  If you keep him aggro free, the trolls die quickly and your odds improve greatly.  Toward the end of each wave he will run out of mana, and jump into melee combat.  

2) Dwarf Priest
She is the only NPC who heals, making her very important.  Mostly she struggles to keep the rogue NPC alive.  But she will also shield or heal you, if she has the mana.  Healing causes her to draw aggro from every loose mob running up the stairs.  She is more robust than the warlock, presumably because she can shield herself.  When she runs out of mana she will jump into melee.  If

There is an easy way to take out Bly and his crew after you've finished off all the spawns.
(after you have the Demolition guy blow up the door to the last boss that is)
Wait for them to begin to Hearthstone (yes if you wait long enough Bly and his gang will begin to hearth away).
Then talk to Bly at the last second and his teammates will continue to hearth and leave.... leaving only Bly to kill.

You get this AFTER the fight with Sergeant Bly. Make sure you don't talk to him until your group is full on mana and health. He and the rest of the group you saved (except the Goblin) will attack you.

Once he's dead, you can loot the Divine-o-Matic Rod off of him.
Whatever you do, do NOT wait too long to talk to the guys at the bottom b/c these mofrakee's will hearth out. Some sick joke the devs put in the game i guess...

"But the summoning of Gahz'rilla is a well-kept secret of the trolls. To face him, you must first wrest the secret from them."

 Head over to the Hinterlands and find Qiaga the Keeper (https://www.wowhead.com/forever/npc=7996), she should drop a Sacred Mallet (https://www.wowhead.com/forever/item=9241).

Take the mallet to the Jintha'Alor altar located at 59, 77. When used on the altar you'll end up with the Mallet of Zul'Farrak (https://www.wowhead.com/forever/item=9240).

Use that to ring the gong at the end of Zul'Farrak. This will summon Gahz'rilla. Good luck!

Once you are in Zul'Farrak, you can find Gahz'rilla's room by heading left when you can.  His room has a large pool with a gong at one end.  Before you summon him, take time to clear out some of the mobs in the room, particularly the patrols.  There are single patrols as well as multiples, including at least one trio of two hunters and basilisk.  Take special note of the mobs in the corners, as they can be hard to spot.  You don't have to get rid of them if you don't need/want them, but you need to be aware that they are there.  Also watch for patrols that come from the adjoining hallways.  You likely took out the patrols from one of the hallways on your way in, but the narrow hall on the east side of the room has one or two mobs that patrol into the big room.  Their patrol route is long, so you might not see them unless you know to wait for them.

Hydromancer Velratha is also in this room, and is worth taking down even if you don't have the Tiara From The Deep quest.  She is a bit tougher than the usual mobs and would be a nasty add if you don't take care of her before you summon Gahz'rilla.

If you don't want to clear the entire room, you need to take out Velratha and all patrols, then clear the static mobs closest to the pool.  Depending on how long you take, watch the hallways for the patrols to respawn.  They often come right up to the pool, and that will almost surely make for a wipe.

Once you are ready, have a party member with the enchanted mallet use the gong

Since there is some confusion on how to obtain the mallet.

Well first of all you obviously get the quest from the guy in the Shimmering Flats (Thousand Needles), Wizzle Brassbolts at 77,77.

Then you go to the Hinterlands. At the altar of Zul at 48,68, on top of that (small) altar there is a woman called Qiaga. When you try to kill her the other mobs agro you, but I was able to solo it all with a lvl 60 lock.
She drops the uncharged mallet.

Then you go to the east. When you arrive at Jintha'Alor don't bother killing any of the mobs there. Just stay on your mount and follow the path and the stairs until you get close to 57,78.
There you will see a (very) small altar guarded by a few elites, a few wolves and a priestess. Also there is some horde guy lying on his back.
The only thing you need to do is stand on that altar and right click the mallet in your inventory to charge it. You can choose to kill the mobs but you don't have to.

Then you scroll up and look for the first yellow post for further instructions :)

Jintha'Alor is a very boring and bland area and it is pretty hard to find a group willing to escort you to the top to get your mallet enchanted. You can naked corpse run (or feign death/vanish) your way up there and if timed correctly (the Priestess enters the cave every now and then), you can approach the altar and charge your mallet without waking the guy sleeping there, then hearth out.

I took the wolf to the left and then the elite beside the altar once the priestess was back in her cave. These guys hit you with their sheild and stun you for a few seconds so best to pull them singularly if solo'ing like me. 

Watch for the priestess to return and dont be like me and not see her until it was too late. She's pretty tough for a lvl 51 Druid although I wasn't 100% health at the time. She heals herself when she gets down to 50% and 25% so make sure you use some sort of stun to interupt it. She also uses a bit of shadow magic and can turn you into an amphibian which is no problem for me because I can shapeshift out of it. It is best just to avoid her altogether and apply your hammer onto the altar when it is safe. (and Im not talking about your manhood here)

Make sure you leave the guy sleeping on the altar, you dont have to wake him up if you dont want to. If you do he's not that hard to kill, takes a while but he doesn't have a weapon and tries to punch you to death! Poor fella.

main.body:
"But the summoning of Gahz'rilla is a well-kept secret of the trolls. To face him, you must first wrest the secret from them."

 Head over to the Hinterlands and find Qiaga the Keeper (http://www.wowhead.com/?npc=7996), she should drop a Sacred Mallet (http://www.wowhead.com/?item=9241).

Take the mallet to the Jintha'Alor altar located at 59, 77. When used on the altar you'll end up with the Mallet of Zul'Farrak (http://www.wowhead.com/?item=9240).

Use that to ring the gong at the end of Zul'Farrak. This will summon Gahz'rilla. Good luck!

Once you are in Zul'Farrak, you can find Gahz'rilla's room by heading left when you can.  His room has a large pool with a gong at one end.  Before you summon him, take time to clear out some of the mobs in the room, particularly the patrols.  There are single patrols as well as multiples, including at least one trio of two hunters and basilisk.  Take special note of the mobs in the corners, as they can be hard to spot.  You don't have to get rid of them if you don't need/want them, but you need to be aware that they are there.  Also watch for patrols that come from the adjoining hallways.  You likely took out the patrols from one of the hallways on your way in, but the narrow hall on the east side of the room has one or two mobs that patrol into the big room.  Their patrol route is long, so you might not see them unless you know to wait for them.

Hydromancer Velratha is also in this room, and is worth taking down even if you don't have the Tiara From The Deep quest.  She is a bit tougher than the usual mobs and would be a nasty add if you don't take care of her before you summon Gahz'rilla.

If you don't want to clear the entire room, you need to take out Velratha and all patrols, then clear the static mobs closest to the pool.  Depending on how long you take, watch the hallways for the patrols to respawn.  They often come right up to the pool, and that will almost surely make for a wipe.

Once you are ready, have a party member with the enchanted mallet use the gong
As of patch 3.0.8, you no longer require the Mallet to hit the gong to summon Gahz'rilla. You can just walk up and use the gong.

Jintha'Alor is a very boring and bland area and it is pretty hard to find a group willing to escort you to the top to get your mallet enchanted. Easy way to battle Gah'Zrilla:

Step 1: If you're entering his area via the narrow pass, clear the mobs in front of the pass or patrolling in front of it. NO need to clear the mobs adjacent to the path.
Step2: Make sure to kill the named troll priestess that paths around the pool. She fears people so get her as far in to the pass as possible before dps'ing her.
Step 3: The tank has to go straigh to the edge of the pool and pull the mobs near the gong to him and run back to the group waiting for him at the entrance of the pass..Clear that group.
Step 4: Whoever has the mallet, go stright to the edge of the pool and then turn left to the gong (This is to not aggro the other mobs) and hit the gong and run back the same way to the group.
Step 5: The tank goes straigh to the pool and pulls Gah'Zrilla to him and when the boss is closing in on him, he runs back to the group.
Step 6: Tank the boss in such a way that only his head is inside the pass but the rest of his body is outside. This way only the tank will get punted. If and when the tank gets punted, he will land on top of the arch above the entrance and can jump down on the boss. To reduce damage, when the tank gets punted, shift to berserker stance and intercept him and switch to def stance.
Step 7: Kill him. 

This way, you don't have to clear the entire room, just enough to summon the boss.

Cheers.

Stay away from the edge of any ledge.  If you fight on the edge, you'll pull dozens of elites by accident.

You can kill mines from the dwarves, but they have a lot of health.  The best option is to back up when a mine is laid.

This task is actually really easy...... Once you're in the instance (the main enterance, not thru the door) go straight, then right.  You will come to a dead end... jump off (make sure u got a healer or someone that has first aid for this). Then, folow the wall you are on until you see an opening wit gnomers on birdthings. Go thru this hallway, and once ur out, kill the gnome humanoids and go right... killing every mob in the way. About 3/4 the way around, there will be a ramp that prings you up to a bot, kill it, and get the key. Now, go back down the ramp and jump down to the lower part. Continue to circle the lower part until you find a hallway with dark iron dwarves. If this hallway, you can go in the middle or to the left... take the path on the left. Walk straight down this entire hallway and eventually you will see a big door. Open it wit your key and kill the gnomes and machines guarding the boss. You will see the boss in the middle, so kill him and take the combination. Now that you have the combination, go straight and jump up to a walkway a little bit higher than the part you were standing on. Just make a circle around the thing you are on until you find a box. Use the combo to open it and you will get the blueprints... you have just completed rig wars :)

forever.body:
There has been some confusion on where Tabetha is. Let me first say this:

[b] Calm down, relax, and take a deep breath. [/b]

Okay. Now. It isn't that hard. First, take the path from Theramore. It is a long mount ride/run through the Marsh. Follow the path until just before the Barrens. Then run SE until you are North of the Stonemaul Ruins. The Ruins are SW of Theramore on the map. 

Her house has a dock in front of it extending into the water. It is a one-story with a garden and haybales to the side. Go inside, and /cheer, because you've found her!

Now, for all you who love adds, and have coordinates... [b](46, 57)[/b] is standing right next to her.

If you do not have a coordinate system, which (46,57) is, I highly recommend installing Titan. It's not that hard, and most people can tell you how. Google.com- search "Titan".

I hope you have thoroughly enjoyed my mini-guide to finding Tabetha in Dustwallow Marsh. For more info, find me on Argent Dawn. 

-Kaydaa, level 42 Warrior, Boanbimo Goonies-

Hydromancer Velratha is in the same room as Gahz'rilla.  She patrols near the pool in the middle of the room.  Take out the other patrols first as they pass the south end of the pool.  Once they are all gone, clear the static mobs down one side of the room, working your way north to the area Velratha patrols.

Velratha is not much more difficult than the other magic users in Zul'Farrak.  Her only edge is the ability to use a totem called "Wrath of Zum'rah" which summons skeletons.  You can counter this by assigning someone with fast attack speed to watch for totems, and have them attack the totem as soon as it appears.  However, it is possible to do enough damage to Velratha that she will wind up focusing on healing herself, thus never casting the totem.

BTW druids, shamans, rogues and hunters should not pass up this quest even though the rewards are useless to them.  You get both of the items and 65s.  Selling both items should yield well over 2g, bringing the monetary reward close to 3g.
Tabetha - Dustwallow Marsh (46,57)

Others might have noticed that this takes place in "Dustwallow marsh" and not in the Swamp of Sorrows. I on the otherhand spent 15 minutes running around 45;57 in the swamp of sorrows (which isn't really that interesting) trying to find her.

Just wanted to emphasize the "Dustwallow marsh part..

A mage can solo this quest.  I did it at level 48, but I'm sure it can be done earlier.  First you will want to shield up, mount up, and ride past the enemies at the start of the dungeon.  I went through the graveyard and past the stairs.  There are several reset spots in ZF, so if you get low on health or mana, you can use one to drop out of combat.  One reset spot I found that may be helpful is near the stairs, next to the closed door that leads to Chief Ukorz.  There are a couple of boxes and a small pillar by the wall.  Jump on the first box, then the pillar and enemies will stop attacking you.

Next you should clear the long corridor between the stairs and the pool where the Hydromancer spawns.  There are two or three enemies to kill.  They are elite, but can be pulled one at a time and kited.  Then you can pull Velratha by herself.  You can pull her back to the corridor and use the wall to block line of sight so she will run to you.  I found it best to fight her at close range.  Be ready to counterspell her, and be sure to wand down her totem as soon as she places it so you don't get swarmed by skeletons.  Otherwise, your shields and damage output should be plenty to bring her down.
Correct cords are 45,57

You'll find Velratha walking around the fountain/pool where Mahz'rilla comes out. She's a level 45 elite plus there are a LOT of other elites and non-elites nearby; so, you'll need a group with you.

**Potential quest conflict / workaround (WoW Forever)**

If Brother Sarno in Stormwind isn't offering Tinkmaster Overspark (#2923), check whether you currently have **Save Techbot's Brain! (#2922)** in your quest log.

In my experience, having Save Techbot's Brain! active prevents Tinkmaster Overspark from appearing, even though I met the level and faction requirements and had not completed either quest.

**The fix:** Abandon Save Techbot's Brain! (#2922), then speak to Brother Sarno again. Tinkmaster Overspark immediately became available for me.

Hopefully this saves someone else some time running around Stormwind trying to figure out why the quest isn't showing up!

*Tested on WoW Forever, Alliance, level 29.*

1850 XP at level 37, when the quest is green.

These are pretty easy to find in large, gray ... refrigerator-sized (for lack of a better description) robotic boxes. You'll find them easily along your path. The biggest concern is finding enough of them to complete the quest for an entire party needing them.

Some notes about this quest:
[ul]
[li]
The highest concentration I found were the loop around [npc=6235] and [npc=6229]. Most groups don't fully clear those loops.
[/li]
[li]If everyone in your group has this quest, merely clearing enough trash to kill the bosses is not going to let you complete the quest. You'll need multiple runs or to clear extra trash.[/li]
[li]
Going through the side/back entrance (where mobs are lv 30+) is faster, but those packs can be hard to kill without a good group.
[/li]
[li]
You won't encounter many of these until you get deeper into the instance. I found only 2 in the area where the green oozes are, then another 8 in the "Hall of Gears" that connects to the ooze area.
[/li]
[li]After killing literally everything from the entrance up to the dark iron dwarf hallway (which leads to last boss), all 5 of my group members had their quest complete. We didn't clear that hall because it was all orange to us.[/li]

[/ul]

forever.body:
A few general tips to keep in mind during a Gnomeregan run:

You might consider making a macro like

/target Mobile Alert System
/cast Earth Shock(Rank 4)

or whatever rank of whatever instant-cast damage spell you might have. Moonfire, Arcane Shot, Fire Blast, you get the idea. If you're not all about macros, just keep your eyes peeled and make sure your sound is on so you can catch them, otherwise they spawn a pair of elites. Alone, this isn't that bad, but when they come in the middle of a fight already in progress, you're probably going to wipe unless you're slightly overleveled or have a really good and organized group.

A major chokepoint for many Gnomeregan groups is the tunnel with all the Dark Iron Agents. The first pull with 4 Dark Irons is just really tough, make sure you kill mines before they're armed. A little further along, there's a group of 3 Dark Irons and one Arcane Nullifier who seem like they're a linked pull. If you wait for the Arcane Nullifier to path over near you, you can pull it and one of the Dark Irons, splitting it up into two pulls of two instead of another group of 4 that can now reflect spells.  As for Thermaplugg himself, just keep DPSing, have someone run around and push the buttons of the statues with open mouths to prevent being nuked with tons of bombs, and if you have a good mage, Thermaplugg can be kited with Blink and some clever maneuvering.

The thing about Gnomeregan seems to be that it's the first instance that actually requires some thinking and coordination.

Other low level instance you just run around and beat up everyone you see, and you'll be fine as long as the tank keeps aggro and the healer heals.

Gnomeregan requires fast reaction to dropped mines and alarm bots, timing to avoid large patrols, mobs that become immune to magic damage and finally some button pressing at the last boss. Sometimes this seems like it's just too much for inexperienced players (and noobs who just refuse to learn) whom until now have been able to survive by just doing dps.

In the end it comes to us experienced players *snicker* to explain to the newbies how to act, and get past certain areas. Unfortunately some people suck horribly at explaining, and rather resort to yelling insults and leaving the group, and others (noobs) just refuse to listen.

Okay so I have a new rogue, level 20ish.  I wanted the Triprunner Dungarees for her (naturally).  Came here to check out how to get em.  I see a bunch of comments pretty much saying ,

"zOMG its soo hard!"
"I had 2 60's help and we all died! zoh noez!"

I went to Gnomer with my main (level 60 druid).  Nothing aggroed me, but I felt like testing it out anyway.  So I aggroed 3 or 4 groups of mobs (normal and elite mixed) and aoe'd.  Mind you, I am 51-point restoration spec for raiding.  So I have no talents in Balance (spell dps) or Feral (melee dps).  I killed the 3-4 groups of mobs with 1 aoe.

I stealthed to Thermaplugg's room, opened the door, went inside.  Buffed with Mark of the Wild only, I killed him in under 30 seconds in cat form.  The bombs did about 100dmg to me, or at least it felt like it.

So in conclusion, don't listen to people who blow this quest out of proportion.  It's not that hard to get to him and kill him.

Now yes, I understand I am level 60, and a group of 30s would have a harder time.  But here's the thing, designate 1-2 people to hit the bomb switches and you will be fine.  For the mobs before Thermaplugg, just your basic tank, heal, and dps.  If you can't get by those you will never make it in BWL/Naxx.

But seriously.  If you want this quest done, and dont want to waste time on trash mobs or the new LFG feature, just find a level 60 pal (or try and pay someone) to kill Therm

You receive the first card from the wandering elite mobs in the upper level outside of the instance. 

Place that card in the card reader outside of the instance.  (Run over to the west and get Techbot's brain while you're here).

Each card reader gives you the card needed for the next reader.

The remaining card readers are located inside the instance. 

These are all of the translated messages from the five punch cards as well as all the machines:

*Avril - you can get the plans if you are horde, read on.*

Loot the White Punch Card from the NPCs in Gnomeregan, inside or outside the instance.

Take the White Punch Card to the Matrix Punchograph 3005-A that is located to the north of both the elevator or the transporter.

You will get the Yellow Punch Card.

Take the Yellow Punch Card to the Matrix Punchograph 3005-B that is located in the bottom of the Dormitories.

You will get a Blue Punch Card.
If you are an Engineer and managed to get a 'Security BETA Access Card' to drop, you will also get the 'Plans: Minor Discombobulator'.

Take the Blue Punch Card to the Matrix Punchograph 3005-C that is located at the top of the Launch Bay on the platform.

You will get a Red Punch Card.

Take the Red Punch Card to the Matrix Punchograph 3005-D that is located at the bottom of the platform in the Engineering Labs.

You will get a Prismatic Punch Card.
If you are an Engineer and managed to get a 'Security DELTA Access Card' to drop, you will also get the 'Plans: Discombobulator Ray'.

Take the cards back to Ironforge to complete the quest.

The punch card will drop off of any of the elite or non-elite spawns outside the instance. Low drop rate.

Run into Gnomeregan, take the elevator down, follow the tunnel until it turns north, and follow the tunnel north until it opens into a large, open room:

[code]/way Dun Morogh 21.8 33.5 Entrance to the First Key Card Room[/code]

Kill the addled lepers until you get your White Punch Card, and take it to the north side of the room to the Punchograph 3005-A there so that you don't have to fight through elite troggs to get your Yellow Punch Card.

[code]/way Dun Morogh 22.03 30.96 Easy Access 3005-A Punchograph[/code]

The white punch card (the first one) drops off the Addled Lepers (non-elite) that are outside the instance, by Techbot.  They do NOT drop off the elite mobs (Caverndeep Invaders, etc).  I know because I have been killing those elite mobs for the past hour for experience and such.

On a side note, Robo-mechanical guts DO drop off those elite mobs outside the instance.  Not a great drop rate, but good to know if you like to solo quests as much as possible like me.

It seems like a lot of you don't really understand probability.

See, there's a chance every time kill a spider that it will drop the item in question.  Let's say that chance is 5%, or 1/20.

Now, it's probable that you'll get the drop within the first 20 times you do the quest -- probable, because you receive 20 chances to roll the 1/20.  And the average of all people doing the quest will average out to about 20 kills.

That doesn't mean you'll get it within 20, though.  On that 21st try, regardless of the fact that you've already killed 20 spiders to no avail, the chance is still only 5%.  And on that 22nd try, it's STILL only 5%.  It's not impossible that you'd kill 100 or more spiders, still never having hit that percentage.  Call it luck if you like, but extended periods of "improbable" missing are to be expected.

All you can do is keep trying.  It's not Blizzard's fault that the computer rolled you up a long streak of &*!@ty numbers.  And keep in mind: it's that same random number generator that just might you a sweet blue weapon drop from a worthless quillboar.

The randomness makes the game, and you gotta take the bad with the good.

Theka the Martyr patrols a large room in the western part of Zul'Farrak.  The room is full of scarabs, but they are neutral beasts.  Just be sure to avoid using AOE attacks and they'll leave you alone.

Theka himself is fairly easy to start.  Just blow him away like you would any other mob.  However, when he gets to about 30% health, he will become immune to all physical damage and all Shadow magic.  This means that you need to have a mage, priest, druid or shaman in your party (or a warlock willing to use only fire spells).  I believe paladins can also use damaging judgements.  I originally tried this quest with a party consisting of hunter, rogue, paladin and two warriors.  Beating Theka was not easy with that group :).  If you have a mage, it might be a good idea for them to not pour on DPS until Theka hits 30%.

Once you've killed him, you can read the tablet in the middle of the scarab room.  It's leaning against one corner of the crumbling structure there.

Confirm soloed by a level 45 Hunter!  I was a little nervous that I wouldn't be able to pull it off, but here's my advice for Hunters to do it as well...

Bring plenty of your pet's favorite food type, at level 45-level.  That's the only thing you need to bring beforehand -- no special/invisibility potions.

Put on Track Humanoid and make sure you're handy at firing off Feign Death.  Also, go into Aspect of the Cheetah (not Pack, you'll want to make sure your pet is able to run as far as it can).

It also helps if your pet has Dash or Dive trained, so it can move quickly.

What you'll want to do is run as far as you can with your pet running ahead, aggroing as many groups as possible before it dies and the mobs turn it's attention to you... then Feign Death in a 'safe spot'.  There are [b]many[/b] places in the grounds of Zul'Farrak where you can stand still and be safe from patrols so you can rez/heal/feed your pet between these pulls.  I know many of them because of having run the instance many times before on my other alts -- I might come back here and mark a few places on a map where I Feigned Death and recovered.  I will note, though, that the first main hallway where there are Shadowcasters channeling against the wall, there will always be a few patrols going up and down the way... but there'll be a good 1-2 minute break where you can stand safely against the [b]left wall[/b] where you can prepare for your next charge.

Ok, i will clarify this quest for you all. 

The Grime-Encrusted Ring is a semi-rare random drop by the Dark Iron Dwarves in Gnomeregan. If you right click on the ring it will begin a quest called The Grime-Encrusted Ring.

The first part of the quest requests that you find some way to clean it. Go to the sparklematic machines located in the dormitory area of Gnomeregan, the GOOD gnomish exiles are standing around, a good indication you are in the right place. 

Find the correct sparklematic machine, the one i used is on the far side of the staircase, near the door to the left. Click on it and do your quest business.

Next post continues...

The follow-up quest, after cleaning your new shiny ring is to decide whether to return the ring to its owner... or not.

The initials 'TDK' are engraved in the ring. You can find our little gnome 'Telvash del Kissel in the Mystic Ward, right in the north east side, co-ordinates : 35,4.

He gives you a new quest, if you choose to accept, which will spruce up your ring to new Heightened Levels of POWER! 

Anyway, next quest to follow.

Well, this follow on quest is pretty straightforward, read the instructions.

Bring the Ring
Bring a Silver Bar
Bring a Moss Agate
Bring 30 Silver Coins

..to TDK.

And bring your brain along too, this quest wasn't hard! why are you reading this!

Only kidding, i had this in my quest log for a long time annoying the living .... outa me.

Non-Relevant information to the above, regarding the Grime-Encrusted Objects to follow, below.

Just for your information. The Grime-Encrusted Objects allow you to activate the sparklematic machines to give you gifts, in the form of little red and white presents. Right click on your presents to open them and recieve your gift. 

You can use the sparklematic to recieve as many presents equivelant to the number of Grime-Encrusted Objects you have, unfortunately they have painstakingly only allowed you to use one at a time, and the machines is not exactly fast. 

We should definitely talk to the Gnomish exiles about this.

N.B - You can only clean the Grime-Encrusted Ring once you get rid of your Grime-Encrusted Objects, or as far as i can remember anyway.

Enjoy!

- Elerethal

This q is an easy 5K XP that most should be able to solo by lvl 31 (which is when I did it with a holy priest). If you also have a grime encrusted object, its a bonus 2.5K XP as well.

As you enter the instance you will see the 1st mob. If you can solo him you should be fine.
Watch out for the non elite solo patrol, he can agro the second mob thats to the left of the first 1.

Once you have disposed of the 1st 2 elite mobs look over the ledge. There is an enormous nut on the floor of the HALL OF GEARS below, and beyond the nut is a doorway to the DORMITORY which is your destination.
Jump so that you land on the nut and then pick your moment to creep towards the doorway.
Once through the doorway watch for a solo elite patrol who will run away at low health.
Head to the right. There is an elite duo blocking your way. My priest was able to hug the wall and get past without agroing, my paladin wasn't.
If you do agro, run up the stairs to the right into the 'friendly' area, which will help if you have to fear the mobs.

Alternatively, asking a group to kill the extra 3 or 4 mobs to allow you to hand in the quest, will add 2 mins at most.

I did this on my lv 48 warrior without having to fight the elites. Using the advice in other comments I looked for the left side access. It's v. easy to spot once there (to find the area without coordinates: it's at the south west end of Tanaris, past the ogre ruins). To the left of the gates is a hill area seperate from the mountians. The space between the mountians and this hill is the pass through other comments refer to. If you follow that you will see the a pillar beside the gate and next to it the round platform you need to click on (wait until the NPC has vanished, which takes 10 min from when he was last talked to). 

There are 4 elites I saw in the area around the platform. 3 stationary and one that wanders. Wait for him to make a loop past the platform and for him to be a decent distance away before approaching the platform. What I did was stay nearer to the pillar then the giants, with the view angled on them as best as possible, and got just close enough to the platform to click on it. You click that, then talk to the guy who appears (I recomend having the 'slow scrolling of quest text' setting turned off for this), ensuring to click on each cartoon chat bubble after his text until he tells you to get some other disc (you don't need to go anywhere, just keep clicking stuff). Click on platform again. Here my memory gets a bit foggy about this quest. Just click on the platform or the guy until you get the quest to return to IF. All this clicking takes less then a mi

Dodging these giants is really wasn't too bad. There are six spawns, all elite, from 48 to 50. At the time I was 47 and they have a fairly small aggro radius but incredible HPs and DPS. They also move pretty slow so with super patience, you can get in there like Shoxy says. Just stay on the left and hop around the blocking pillars. In fact, there's even a trail East of the doors that you can take for maximum safety. I was able to complete this while within spitting distance of the giants.

One thing I wanted to emphasize. When I see a door, I expect to open it. You don't. The little pedestal thingy is in front the door on the left side.

Bring back the miniature platnium discs to the gates of Uldum in Tanaris..the loc of the Uldum pedastal is 38,82. There are level 48-49 elites near there that hit me for 200 per swing and took away about 2000hps before I could bring them down so bring along some guildmates and such before attempting to finish this.

If the guy disappears with your disks still inside the pedestal, here's what you do.  First, don't go anywhere.  Without leaving, abandon the "Stone Guardian" quest.  Then, click the pedestal again, it should give you the quest again.  After that, just restart your conversation with the guy.

Indeed, you see small path at the left hand of Uldum. Walk first around the mountains (behind  Southmoon Ruins) until you're at 39,78. Walk to small path and you see already ghosty statue at left side.
Look out for walking giant. When he's walking away, step safetly further until you're in click range. Click first the down part for discs, then talk to upper part, then down part, then upper part, make sure you receive finally quest for Ironforge and check for disc in your inventory. If you cannot talk more to the ghost and down part is not more clickable, you can go to IF.

Much XP indeed! No aggro at level 53 mage.

The easiest way to do this quest is to approach the pedestal in a counter-clockwise manner.  Hug the  wall until you see a crevice in the wall.  You can force your way through it with your mount.  Continue to hug the wall and you can access the pedestal without fighting the elite mobs.

(summary)
Four things:
1.) Hug wall
2.) go counterclockwise
3.) watch out for the one patrol
4.) be high enough level to not aggro the mobs.

It leads to blue rewards and lots of exp--well worth it!
Note: this quest is in/near [b]Uldum[/b] in Tanaris,  not Uldaman.

This is one of those weird legacy quests that just hasn't aged well. [url="http://www.wowhead.com/item=9538"]Talvash's Golden Ring[/url] isn't a [i]bad[/i] item, but it's not worth the cost of admission. The fact that you need to run an instance and make a trek to Ironforge just to start this quest is one thing, but then you're required to shell out the cash for a silver bar and a moss agate, with 30 silver on top? 

On my server, I ended up paying 5 gold for the silver bar and 10 gold for the moss agate. If you're a miner, you might already have these items, but using them for the quest means you can't use them to craft or sell, so you're losing just as much on the deal as anyone else.

In the grand scheme of things, this isn't a lot of money to spend, but the ring itself isn't very useful compared to other rings at this level, and you can only vendor it for [i]64 silver![/i]

Full text of dialogue with The Stone Watcher of Norgannon:

Watcher: [quote]Salutations. I am a guardian of entry. Unless you have the plates of Uldum already integrated into your disc set, I will not allow for entry into the Uldum compound.[/quote]

Player: [quote]What function do you serve?[/quote]

Watcher: [quote]My purpose is to regulate access to the Uldum compound for the Creators. I allow entry into the compound only when the solicitor exhibits for access the proper sequencing discs.

Your disc set currently does not include the Plates of Uldum, the primary prerequisite for entry. Access is not granted unless the Plates of Uldum are present.[/quote]

Player:[quote]What are the Plates of Uldum?[/quote]

Watcher: [quote]The Plates of Uldum are discs synthesized by the Creators that allow access into the Uldum compound. These discs house and store specific data related to the Creators' activities here. 

Physically, they are nearly identical in circumference to the disc set you currently possess. Their markings, however, are directly related to information on Uldum as opposed to the Uldaman complex.[/quote]

Player: [quote]Where are the plates of Uldum?[/quote]

Watcher: [quote]Several sets of the Plates of Uldum have been synthesized by the Creators for their expressed use. The Creators control the distribution of said discs for all complexes on this world. As such, Azeroth has been rescheduled for visitation, and therefore future discs may enter circulation at that tim

The joke is from one of the greatest skits in Saturday Night Live history, Christopher Walken playing the record producer for '70's gray-beard metal band Blue Oyster Cult, as they are recording the song, "Don't Fear The Reaper". Will Ferrell plays the member of the band whose sole purpose is to hit the cowbell, in 4/4 time. He starts playing quietly while every fifteen seconds or so, Walken charges into the studio and states how there needs to be EVEN MORE cowbell, eventually stating the funniest thing I, personally, have ever heard on television: "I've...I've got a... a fever, a fever for cowbell, and the only, the only cure... Is more cowbell." Easily one of the funniest skits in the show's history, Ferrell eventually banging on the cowbell so hard he drowns out the rest of the band, FYI, "Don't Fear The Reaper" is considered one of the finest examples of what NOT to do when recording a song, as the cowbell drowns out the guitar, singer and even the DRUMS occasionally. Go to Wal-Mart, pay five bucks (it's in the budget bin) and get the Christopher Walken SNL disc. It has this skit and shows why, as well as Alec Baldwin, he can say at any time that he wants to host, and he gets to.

Therefore I believe that Uldum is a homage to the Developers who created this great game.

The quest line to obtain these rewards can be confusing, so here is a quick rundown on how to get to the end....on the Horde side. The Alliance side is almost exactly the same except it involves chatting up NPCs in Ironforge instead of Thunderbluff.
[ol]
[li]You can't start this quest line until you are level 40. The lineage is in 2 parts and the second part has a minimum level of 45. This is where a lot of folks get messed up......so start it at 40 and come back at 45 to finish it.[/li]
[li]The first thing that has to be done is for the last boss in Uldaman ([url=/?npc=2748]Archaedas[/url]) to be killed by any group whether you are in it or not. It takes a minimum of 3 folks to summon him so don't get a single high level friend to run you through. 3 have to click on an altar to summon him and then he can be killed.[/li]
[li]Once he dies a set of doors behind him open up into a closed room. Here is where the quest line will start. At this point, anyone in this group's instance level 40 or above can start the quest line. So if you have a level 40 alt you can log off your high level main, log on your alt, get invited to the group by its leader, and come in and start the quest line without having to have killed anything in the instance.[/li]
[li]In the room is a pile of discs which you will click on. These are the [url=/?object=131474]Discs of Norgannon[/url] and you will click on them and take the quest offered.[/li]

[b]Location:[/b]  The Hinterlands; Aerie Peak; 9.44 (To recieve and complete the quest).  The Altar of Zul; 49.68  

[b]Description:[/b]  Although you could mount up and run up the altar to touch the platform and complete the quest, it would be smart to find a group and kill the mobs.  The reason being that you can also obtain the "Sacred Mallet" which is used to create the "Mallet of Zul'Farrak" which is used to summon Gahz'rilla in the Zul'Farrak instance.  The trolls and wolves around the altar are levels 46-47.  However, once you reach the top, you will find two level 50 elites.  I brought a level 60 hunter with me to do things the easy way.  I sheeped the front elite and from there we successfully cleared the altar.  Everyone in the party will be able to loot the mallet from the elites.

Sorry, but I just can't.

Yeah, it's Classic. Hurr durr, you gotta earn stuff. I get it. But this quest is so unbelievably #$%^.

The level of hostility baked into some aspects of Classic's design is genuinely baffling. It's almost as if the developers were giggling to themselves while coming up with the most mean-spirited, unnecessarily annoying quest they could possibly devise.

The dwarves are overtuned to $%^&, with way too much HP and damage compared to other elites of their level. On top of that, they're packed ridiculously close together, so good luck trying to pull them individually without aggroing half the camp.

And, of course, we have Blizzard's favourite design philosophy: "Kill 5 of X, but there are only 5 of them on the entire map."

But here's the best part: this quest is unironically harder than Stockades, the whole reason you're picking it up in the first place.

At some point, there's a difference between making players earn something and making an experience unnecessarily miserable. &*!@ whoever tuned this.

Read the other reviews, but decided there had to be a better way to get Demo's without having to pry them out from the camps...

Go to the Inn at the end of Dun Modr (left hand side at the end of the valley).  There are two Demo's in the back room and another one below.... and no escorts..... plus you have to get through 3-4 tunnelers as well so you can get rid 50% of the req

...can be found in the second building on the left as you enter, which is a half-tunneled inn in the dwarven plan.  There are a few tunnelers in here, and a merchant (!), and three demolitionists.  I was able at 38 to take each without aggroing the rest, except the two in front of the merchant, where I had to vanish (as a rogue).  There's plenty of room to bandage or eat in here without further aggro, though.  There are three demolitionists in here as of today; I'm waiting while I type for them to respawn so I don't have to go elsewhere for the last 2 on the list. :)

Definitely do this quest in conjunction with the Grim Task quest - saves you the hassle of having to fight your way through the mobs a second time.  I'm a 27 pally and I grouped with a 34 lock/vw, a rogue, and a shaman.  The VW and I tanked and it worked out pretty well.  For the Demos, I would go to the camp to the east - less crowded.  

Finished in about an hour - woot!

Either wait till you ramp up quite a few levels over the quest, or get a full party of 5 to take this one on.  If you're level-appropriate, you'll likely pull 5 of them at once, so you'll need some serious crowd-control, or enough players to go 1-on-1.

The demolition dwarves are in camps to the east of Dun Modr and are the toughest to get because they are surrounded by at least 6 other dwarves.  Even if you work on picking off their bodyguards one at a time, the respawn rate is so fast that you don't have much time to heal and drink.

I found that doing this quest solo with a pet is significantly easier than without, or even in a party. I preferred staying mostly in the front area of the instance, that entry room before the first hall which opens to the big one with the monolith in the middle. I can barely handle one or two at a time, much less three, so obviously it was difficult when most mobs were at max 3 (if they didn't run and attract more).

Sending my Void to tank, I'd focus all my energy on killing the Witch Doctor in the group first, being they can Flash Heal or summon a Healing Ward, then, I'd run out of the instance. Don't worry about your tanking pet, they'll be right next to you outside the instance. Afterwards I'd run back in and finish the other two much more easily, or if you can't handle that just do one by one, running in and out. It's not as tedious as it sounds. I prefer killing in this order: Witch Doctor, Blood Drinker, Shadowcaster. Shadowcasters die very easily and don't have a very high DPS, while Blood Drinkers have a higher defense and DPS. It all depends on your priority, and what you can handle.

There's one patroller, that goes halfway into the front room you'll be in and then patrols back. Be sure to time attacks just right, and minimize fearing with maximized DPS. Concussive Shot will really help you out when they start to run, or if you're a Lock cast Curse of Recklessness right before their health gets seriously low. Chances are your pet may die, so don't forget to bring

Marvon Rivetseeker is found at a sand-buried temple ruin not too too far south of Gadgetzan.  After speaking with him, you will have to travel to the Sunken Temple, located in the Swampasaurus area (Swamp of Sorrows).  It is the large lake, the Pool of Tears east of Stonard.  There are many lvl 42-45 drangonkin elite that wander the land that surrounds the temple, but do not fear what is outside, you can easily sneak by them and swim out to the temple inthe center of the lake.

After you arrive at the temple, enter and descend.  Inside it is best to have a party of 3 or more (5 is best) lvl 45 or higher, but I suggest minimum 3 players lvl 50 or higher.

I did this as mage lvl 52, with orc shaman lvl 50 and troll hunter lvl 50 (hunter counts as 2 in my books cause his pet Julian is a good asset) and it was challenging and fun.  A priest would be darn handy!

Happy hunting. BOF

There is understandably a lot of confusion surrounding the [url=https://www.wowhead.com/forever/quest=3446/into-the-depths]Into the Depths[/url] and [url=https://www.wowhead.com/forever/quest=3447/secret-of-the-circle]Secret of the Circle[/url] quests. This is understandable because Blizzard seems to have gone out of their way to make both the quests and the instance the quests are in as confusing as possible. I'm going to post this on both quest pages.

On the bottom of the Sunken Temple is the Altar of Hakkar. You will need to use this Altar to complete both of these quests, however before you can complete them you need to activate the statues on the level above in the correct order to set the next part of the quest in motion and summon the boss [url=https://www.wowhead.com/forever/npc=8580/atalalarion]Atal'alarion[/url]. In theory you're supposed to go down here first to click the alter and learn the order to activate the statues, but I'm going to give you the order to do them so don't worry about that yet.

Upon entering the Sunken Temple you'll be able to choose one of four directions. If you turn 90 degrees to the immediate left and right of the entrance there will be spiral stairs going up and down respectively. The right stairs lead down to the altar but ignore them for now. In front of you there will be a fork, take the left side which should be guarded by an Atal'ai Witch Doctor and a Unliving Atal'ai or  some other combination. Take them out, step around the corner

A rogue can manage this quest solo but expect to die if you make a mistake.

Enter the instance, take the right hand path down to the Pit of Refuse.  The Altar of Hakkar is right there.

When you click on it of course you lose stealth and if a lurker attacks, all those little maggots also attack.  So you have to try and do it fast then flash away.

I did it on an exporation mission at lvl 49.  Other areas here look like a lot of fun in later levels!

[code]Click Order:

          NORTH

          SOUTH
[/code]

1.) I recommend you take the rightmost path down the stairwell and clear out the enemies in the pit (these are oozes/snakes/maggots, lvl 48-50).  This will make it easier to kill the mini-boss that spawns after you activate the statues.

2.) Go back up the the main hall.  Now take the path 2nd from the right.

3.) When you come to the stairwells, take the stairwells down.  You will now be in a circle area where the balconies are.

4.) Clear everything out.

5.) Activate the statues in the correct order (see top post) and then a lvl 50 elite mini-boss will spawn in the pit below (the pit you should have cleared).

6.) Jump down, kill the mini-boss.

7.) Click on the giant snake statue in the middle (appears after activating statues) in order to complete the quest and get your three rewards.

8.) Breakdance.

OK, this might make things a little easier for those who are confused. The cobra idols you need to activate are on a level called Hall of Serpents. There are six. Best way (in my opinion) is to run around the outer hallway and clear all the junk (monsters) before you begin. There are hallways to get down to each of the statues from the main circular one. 

If your bearings are as bad as mine, start clicking on ANY of the statues. If it's wrong it will say "miss". If it's right it will light up with a green glow. The first one that lights will be SOUTH. From there follow this order until all six are lit up.

S, N, SW, SE, NW, NE

OK cool, you lit up everything but you're not done yet. The end of the quest is a giant statue one floor below and there are of course guardians. Don't jump down there unless you have "slow fall" or its equivalent. Walk down the stairs if you're a mere mortal. Kill the guardians, click on the statue, complete your quest and get the hell out.

have done this myself, so I can say with 100% confidence that this quest CAN be done by all of the people in your party at once. 

The setup for this quest is just plain dumb, and desperately needs to be reworked. Basically the way this quest works is you have to talk to Belnistrasz a couple of times (at least twice), and he eventually will offer you the quest Extinguishing the Idol, when you accept this final quest from him, the escort process begins. At this point, everyone in your party that talked to Belnistrasz up until the point where he was offering them the chance to accept the Extinguishing the Idol quest (but have not actually accepted the quest) will be given the typical "X has started an escort quest would you like to join? Yes or No" option. Anyone who has not, will not get credit for the quest. 

What typically happens when playing through RFD is that someone in your party will click through all of the dialogue boxes with Belnistraz before anyone else has had a chance to talk with him, the quest will begin, and they will be the only one to earn credit for it. The short version:  Enter the temple, take the first hall to the left, this twists around and around and up.

Keep totally right until you find a room with a gate on either side and a skelly in a ring in the center.  Four fires burn on the corners.  Clear everything.

Use the egg, this spawns the event, kill everything you can as fast as you can, focus on the flying snakes, take their blood and put out the four fires.

This will spawn the God Hakkar's avatar, defeat him and take your prize.

Notes: We did this with 1 shaman, 1 hunter, 3 rogues from level 49 to 60.  We all but wiped and the gates opened back up (one rogue vanished).  We came back in and aggro'd the mess, pulling it outside the caged area and locking one rogue inside.  We defeated him anyhow.  The hard part is the endurance match!

actually need to make a correction, seemed like a good tip before I did the encounter, then when we went to start it, realized this was not true. You need to use the egg in the room where the skeleton of the avatar is in order to start the encounter, and then the mobs start spawning. Unless it was meant that you need to clear all the mobs around the area. 

This encounter is VERY hectic if you aren't well organized, so make sure you brief everyone before using the egg. 
Change the loot to free for all(thanks to the second post) and make sure one person is in charge of getting the blood and extinguishing the torches. The blood drops from wyvern looking creatures called Hakkari Bloodkeepers(https://www.wowhead.com/forever/npc=8438) that spawn one at a time. there are also several non elite venom spitters running around, that will quickly target your priest/healer, so have at least one person assigned to pull these off of them. Also, during the encounter before Hakkar is summoned by putting out the four torches, there are elite dragonkin called Nightmare Suppressor's (https://www.wowhead.com/forever/npc=8497#00Rzc) that spawn and try to prevent you from summoning the avatar, they also start a "drain soul" like animation on the Avatar, but I didn't really notice if it was doing anything with all the other mobs around, sorry. But if you see them doing the drain, a quick attack is all that is needed to break the action and have them target you, then it is just a regular elite fi

Once you use the egg in the room with hakkar's skeleton, the ghost of hakkar comes out with a few non-elite snakes.  Also spawning is an elite flying snake.  Kill the elite flying snake, and loot his blood.  Use the blood to put out one of the fires.

When you put out a fire, an elite summoner will spawn and start walking in.  Kill the elite summoner.  If you let him go, he will start shooting beams at the ghost of hakkar.  You do not want this to happen.  If you let them shoot the beams too long, hakkar will not summon and you have to reset the instance to do it again.

When you kill the summoner, another flying elite snake will spawn, which you have to kill to loot the blood.  Again use the blood on one of the fires, and repeat the same process.  Casters, you should drink in between fights to regen mana.  If you clear the two hallways leading to the room, its safe for a priest to use psychic scream if things get hairy.

When all four fires are out, hakkar will spawn, and then you kill him.  Loot the essence of hakkar off the body and use it from your inventory to complete the quest.  Turn in the quest back in steamwheedle.
Set your looting to "Free for All" to have 1 person gather the Bloods needed for the encounter. Once Hakkar is summoned, change it back to Master-Looter.

Ok here's how it works this is a more detailed description of the encounter than what the quest description says:

When someone has the egg they can use it in the Temple instance to "summon" Hakkar and start up the little event to summon him. When someone starts it both gates will close off the room, and Hakkar will spawn, but he's unkillable and he won't attack yet.

A couple non-elite snakes will spawn periodically throughout this event. They can easily be "round-up" by someone and then be killed by Area Effect spells. A few elite dragons will spawn also but again they're easily taken out if you have a good tank.

The important mobs you need to pay attention to is the Hakkar'i Bloodkeeper mobs that spawn. Once they're killed they drop "Hakkar'i Blood" regardless of what loot your group is set too someone needs to loot the blood and use it on one of the 4 "eternal flames" torches on 4 corners of the room. Once all 4 flames are put out the Avatar of Hakkar will spawn and you can attack him. Overall he's a pushover compared to the other bosses in this instance.

There is a belief pause between non-elite snakes and Hakkar'i Bloodkeeper so your casters can drink up and get mana back. Try to conserve mana.

Hope all this clears it up.

Easiest way in and out if you're only here to do this quest:

After entering the instance, head to your immediate left and climb a spiral stair.  This will take you up to a level with green drake type enemies.  Northwest and southwest lead to a rectangular room where the event takes place.  Use the egg you were provided to start the event.  You're locked in, so make sure all group members are inside before the event starts.

During the event, loot the blood from the bigger elite add with 'blood' in the name, then put out the torches, total of 4.  They'll spawn periodically.  Otherwise it's 'kill the infinite adds' kind of fight.

After the 4th torch is put out, the adds stop spawning, but anything remaining will not despawn.  Kill the remaining adds, then just tank and spank.

The boss drops an item that you right click to actually complete the quest objective.

To leave, go back out to the main room with the green drake type enemies and leave via the north entrance, this will take you right back to the exit again.

After you turned in the quest and talk to the NPC again, you can optional take another item.

We did this quest with 2 Paladins (L46) and 2 Rogues (L41 and L44) and found it to be fairly easy.

The boss at the end is alone at first, but will summon a bunch of undead when he's about half dead.  Just keep on him and they will all disappear when he dies.  We killed him in about 15-20 seconds.  Maybe less.

When you enter the instance there are two paths:

The left path leads to a sub-boss and a sub-quest further on. To fight the spider sub-boss, bang the gong 3 times.

The right path leads to the main boss (Coldbringer - lvl 41). Expect undead elites in the range of 38-41 before you get to the boss. The boss is alone at first, but he will summon elites as the fight progresses. 

Not a bad place for mid-range rares. Good luck.

main.body:
((Spoiler alert!))

[b]The Story of Thaurissan[/b]:
Hundreds of years ago, the great city of Thaurissan stood proudly in a lush expanse of land that is now the dilapidated Burning Steppes.

Thaurissan was home to the nation of Dark Iron dwarves and at the time, in the midst of a civil war among the dwarven nation at large.

You see, that area of the world was at one point in time part of the Redridge Mountains - until the day that Thaurissan was consumed by a gigantic explosion. The city lay in ruin, the surrounding areas reduced to an ashy wasteland.

[i]That is tragic. How did this happen?[/i]

We do not know.

The Dark Irons that did survive made their way into the mountain and began rebuilding their city.

From the ashes of Thaurissan then rose Blackrock Spire and the new Dark Iron nation. Additional fortifications were made within the Searing Gorge, in the area known as the Cauldron.

Stories of an ancient evil that controlled the kingdom of Dark Irons began to circulate.

[i]Interesting, continue please.[/i]

Recently, the Dark Irons have been seen on the surface world with greater regularity. Fortresses have been built in the Badlands. Massive exploratory forces have been sent into the depths of Uldaman in search of ancient lore. They have even invaded our own homeland, striking at our dam near the loch.

[i]Unbelievable! How dare they??[/i]

We need adventurers to assist us, <player>. Will you help?

[i]Of course I will help![/i]
She stands next to the King of Ironforge

"Listen to Royal Historian Archesonus [b]recant[/b] the history of Thaurissan"

[u]Recant:[/u] to withdraw or renounce (beliefs, statements, etc. formerly held), esp. in a formal or public manner.

Sheesh!

This chain has a few eerie (and completely coincidental) parallels to Dan Brown's [i]The Lost Symbol[/i]. I say they are coincidental because Dan Brown's novel was written [i]after[/i] the quest (late 2009).

[i]The Lost Symbol[/i] is about the Masons (a secret society that had goals to improve the infrastructure of the United States).
An Unsent Letter is about the Stonemasons (a secret society that had plans to rebuild the city after the war).

The name of the antagonist in [i]The Lost Symbol[/i] is Mal'ahk, although he has many other names.
The name of the assassin in An Unsent Letter is Marzon, aka Maelik.

In [i]The Lost Symbol[/i] the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) becomes heavily involved in capturing Mal'ahk.
In An Unsent Letter the Stormwind Intelligence (SI:7) becomes heavily involved in capturing Maelik.

There are probably others, if you really want to stretch it, but these are the obvious ones.

forever.body: You have to kill Dextren Ward. He is at the far end of the left wing in Stockade. At least he was when i killed him, might be somewhere else considering its such a small instance....

Stockades is an instanced zone within Stormwind City.  It's in the fort-looking building that's just NW of the trade district as you come into the city. (directly north of the enchanter's shop if you are familiar with that or just ask a guard)

Stockades is populated with 23/24ish and up elites.  The bosses are 27/28ish elites.

The zone is essentially a T shape.  As you come in you are at the bottom of the T.

Along each hallway there are several rooms that lead off to the sides.  These are populated with 3 or 4 elite mobs each.  

Be aware that runners will often turn into these rooms as they flee.  So be sure to either A) stop all runners, B) be high enough to not care about the 3 adds or C) clear all rooms as you pass them.

Dextren Ward can be found by heading straight in, and taking the first hallway turn to the left.  Be aware that theer is a respawning wanderer that paths between the two branches of the T and could be comming up behind you at any given point.

Down the Left hallway you go, until it opens into a larger room at the end.  This larger room has 3 smaller rooms off of it.  The large room will have 3 to 4 elites in it.  Each smaller room will have approximately 3 elites in them.

As you come into the large room Dextren Ward can be found in the smaller room off to the right.  In there you'll almost always find 3 elites plus Dextren Ward.  He's dressed as a caster but does not seem to cast when I fight him.  

Generally spekaing, Stockades is a very short zone

If you enter from Searing Gorge, the first chain to the left has a rock ramp that you can use to get on the chain.  Once on, run across the chain to the building. main.body: You can only grab this quest if you are in ghost form (dead) or someone that already has it shares it with you. You can find Franclorn Forgewright outside the instance. He is actually in the center of the big lava pit as you start running down the chains to head to BRD. He will be standing on top of a tomb.

You don't have to res at the GY (and get the 10-minute Resurrection Sickness debuff) if you kill yourself in the lava. What I did was this:

1. Strip naked (and dismiss pet if you're a hunter / lock)
2. Go to the narrow platform at the bottom of the second chain bridge leading to BRD, near where the blood elf Lothos Riftwalker is. (You can pick up the MC attunement quest from him while you're there)
3. Fall off the platform near Lothos, so you land in the lava right next to the platform.
4. Die, release and run back to Franclorn Forgewright on the way back to BRD. Get the quest from him.
5. Go back down to Lothos - you'll be able to recover your corpse standing on the platform, since you died right next to it.
6. Get dressed again, and continue into BRD to finish the quest.

Shadowforge Key Walkthrough:

I will assume that you have the Dark Iron Legacy quest already.

1. As you enter BRD, go northeast into the first area and clear it.  This area doesn't have a name that I know of, but has 6 large exits off of it.  The key direction you want to go in here is East-Northeast (ENE) into the tunnel.

2. Ring of Law - A little ways into the ENE tunnel, you will find the Ring of Law on the left side.  Make sure all of your party members enter at the same time as the gate will shut behind you.  Defeat the 2 events inside the ring and exit through the western gate.

3. East Garrison - You'll will come out of the Ring of Law into the East Garrison.   Immediately to your right is a large set of stairs that go east to the upper section of the Ring of Law.

4. Ring of Law (spectator area) - Proceed through this area to the Shrine of Thaurissan.

5. Shrine of Thaurissan - Head to the left (north) across the bridge.  Note that you'll come back here later once you have the drop off of Fineous Darkvire.

6. The Domicile - Head through here to the exit, which is down the stairs in the north corner of the room.  This leads to the eastern side of Shadowforge City.

7. Shadowforge City (east) - The Black Vault is here on the right side, but is optional.  Go all the way to the north end and down into the Hall of Crafting.

Here's how you get to Fineous:

1) Go into BRD (duh).

2) Go straight, clear your way to the path directly in front of you- this is the path that runs almost perfectly east/west along the southern side of the Arena.

3) Go into the Arena and do the event. This will make the spectators at the top of the Arena (you'll be there in a second) passive. 

4) Go out the arena exit, it's to your left as you walk into the arena. You'll find yourself in a room with some DI Dwarves and some fire elementals. 

5) On the right there will be stairs/a ramp leading up to the spectator area of the arena. Walk to the other side of the arena, DO NOT ATTACK THE SPECTATORS.

6) At the other end of the arena go down the ramp. Going right will take you to the statue you turn Ironfel in at. Head left to get to Fineous after crossing through a few rooms first. He's in the room with the large stone golems and the non-elite dwarves. He pats up and down the ramp. 

7) After you kill him head back the way you came, go past the entrance to the arena and continue on to the statue that is just around the corner.

1) Go into BRD (duh).

All of the previous comments were very helpful in allowing me to get this done - but it might be easier to summarise it all here:

Assuming you're looking for the Shadowforge Key, the first step is to die, and pick up the quest from Franclorn Forgewright.  Dying within the Blackrock Mountain, preferably near the entrance to BRD is easy - on the run back, pick up the quest, and ressurect at your corpse.

Enter BRD itself, and continue straight forward, past the initial 2 guards visible upon zoning in, and continue straight across the circular room you find yourself in (minimap reads "Detention Block"), and enter the tunnel directly opposite your entry point.  Continue up this tunnel until the first pack of mobs on the right hand side, on your left will be a tunnel.  Take this, and you will enter "Ring of the Law".  

Stand on the grate in the middle of the room to engage the event, but make careful note of your entry point to this room.  You will get 2 waves of scorpid like adds, and after this, a random (thank you Narinae!) boss will enter.  Kill him, and this will open a gate to the left of the point where you entered the room.  This gate will reveal a ramp leading up, take this (you will see "East Garrison" on your minimap), and at the end of the ramp you will enter a room.  

Perform an immediate U-turn (About turn in USA) to your right, and take the ramp up to the spectator room.  Minimap will change to read "Ring of the Law" again.  Without attacking any spectato

This quest is a bit intriguing. I don't think the background is arbitrary.

Consider that Targorr is a Blackrock orc. Now, who do they serve? That's right, Nefarian. While I doubt he gets personally involved here, let's assume that some Blackrock authority does. Okay, exactly by what means could they intervene?

Why, Nefarian's sister Onyxia, in the guise of Lady Katrana Prestor, is very much a noble... :)

It's also noteworthy that - okay, I know trash mobs are always at peace with each other - the Defias and Targorr are actually inhabiting the same cell. If you do any Defias related quests in Dustwallow marsh, you will see connections between the Defias Brotherhood and Onyxia, that she perhaps even leads it. Check the "Allies and leadership" paragraph of http://www.wowwiki.com/Defias_Brotherhood

There's a couple of ways you can reach Lord Incendius, both ways are as difficult however the 2nd guide is recommended for a solid party since the mobs are more higher level:

1a) Go up to the Ring of Law and defeat the boss there, then exit to the west into the room with the dwarfs and fire elementals.

1d) Work your way down out of the small maze of rooms to an upper semi-circular area with more groups of humanoids you'll need to battle through at the entrance.
1e) Drop down to the level below you where you'll need to fight a couple of elementals before proceeding engaging Lord Incendius in the middle of the circular room to the north-east.
