forever.body:
After opening the cell of Commander Gor'shak, you will be able to turn in the previous quest in this chain. The commander will then offer you this quest.

DO NOT ACCEPT IT until everyone in your group has had a chance to turn in the previous step.

Accepting this quest will cause eight low-50 elites tospawn in the hallway, rush into the cell and begin to kill the unarmed and unarmored Commander Gor'shak, which makes you fail the quest. The best way to stop them from doing this is to never let them into the cell at all, so turn in the first quest and then go back out of the cell.

Only one person has to be in the cell to activate this quest, everyone nearby will get an accept box stating "So-and-so is starting "What is going on?, would you like to as well?". Everyone accept, and the person who triggered it steps outside to rejoin the party.

The Elites will spawn in the hallway and begin rushing towards the cell. Have your warrior do an AE taunt, then pile on the area effect spells. A frost mage who can kite and Ice block is invaluable here, as you have a long hallway that has been recently cleared to play in.

Ice traps outside the cell are needed if you choose to attempt the crowd control and tank it out route, but the sheer number of attackers makes it difficult for your 5 man group. Remember to keep Gor'shak alive and you'll be ok.

This is a tough fight.  We tried to win this 4 times previously trying to fight _in_ the cell.  Due to close quarters, and the cleaves that all the elites use, Gor'Shak dies in seconds. 

Our plan was to use fears to break up the attacks. We cleared the hallway top to bottom to prevent adds. Then, our warlock started the script while the rest of us waited outside the cell. I Intimidating Shouted them first and we DPSed the 1st target. Fortunately Gor'Shak focused on this target.  By the time the rest returned, we were ready.  The warlock feared them, and Gor'Shak (thankfully), went after a lone runner. We caught up with them and DPS'ed that target quickly. Our priest then feared the group, and once again, Gor'Shak goes after a lone runner.  Once that target was down, I simply tanked 3 while the rest of the party DPS'ed the remainder.  They then peeled targets off of me 1 at a time until the encounter was over.  At no point during this fight did Gor'Shak ever go below 3/4 hit points.

forever.body: Some people will insist that you can't do any sort of damage to the princess at all, but this isn't true. So long as she isn't dead when the Emperor dies it'll complete the quest. It's possible to offtank her in order to keep her from wailing on your healer.

This is a working tactic for all to free Princess Moira Bronzebeard:

1. Get a Priest in your group.
2. Clear the whole Throneroom, except Thaurissan and Princess.
3. When the group attacks the King let the Priest heal as much as he/she can.
4. As soon as Priest draws aggroe from the PRINCESS, let healer offtank her and only heal him-/herself.
5. IMPORTANT: The priest must NOT hit the princess with ANYTHING.
6. Without the Princess healing Thaurissan he goes down quickly. No big deal.
7. As soon as King goes down, the Princess turns friendly, although she suffers from Stockholm-Hostage-Sydrome.

Worked peachy for us.

Hardest part is resisting the urge to $%^& it up for you and your group.  "Well if we CCed her it would be so easy." 

This is what you do: you pretend like she's not even there,  you don't sheep her, you do not sap her, you do not seduce her, you don't even try, if she is beating on your priest just kill the emperor faster.  

With a tank, a priest, and 3 DPSers,  it's cake.  If she goes for one that just nuked the emperor, just let him die.

But don't really pretend that she isn't there;  dispel thorns and fireshield, put pets to passive, use timeworn mace instead of your thunderfury, no naglering you just won, yes I know you disenchanted your other ring and you're just a druid so you probably wont aggro her, but just put it away.  Oh your shield has a mithril spike does it, well you're about to use protection stance with your ice barbed spear.

And just to be on the safe side don't use any challenging shout or demoralizing roar or whatever those tank tricks are. Don't use ice armor or touch of weakness.  And no fears please.  Think you can handle it?

Good luck. 
Have fun. 
Die with dignity.

I had 60-days played between my two 60's before I ever bothered to kill Bael'Gar.  He's simply not on the way to anything, is a pain to get to with a group, is impossible to solo without uber gear, and would be moderately hard even with a stealth group, they're not the right classes for killing him ... well maybe with 2 druids (tank + healer) and a rogue it would work.

If you do want to kill Bael'Gar here's my experience:

My priest friend and my hunter duo him all the time for shards, but the priest has difficulty getting to him without aggroing things so he's not even worth farming for shards.  Probably a hunter + druid(healer) would be the best duo for this guy.  The hunter has to pick up the adds that spawn though.  The druid just has to keep the pet alive.

If you run to the wall behind him when you first aggro him, you wont have to fight any of the pats or mobs in the area.  That makes killing him a lot faster because the packs of 5 elites that roam around are much harder than BaelGar.

For a level 50-something quest that makes you run all around and kill stuff that noone ever kills (Bael'Gar) the rewards for this quest aren't worth the inventory nor quest space they take up.  

To think I've had the molt in my inventory for a couple of months thinking I was saving it for something good.  What a waste.

For anyone who doesn't know how to find Bael'gar:

After entering the instance, head through the locked door on your left (using the [url=?item=11000]Shadowforge Key[/url], or a skilled Rogue) and kill the fire elemental that patrols the hallway. Continue in this direction to the Dark Iron Highway, and turn left. Bael'gar is the gigantic dude at the end of the highway. Added: Oct 14th, 2004

Objectives:

Venture to Blackrock Depths and destroy the vile aggressors!

Warlord Goretooth wants you to kill 10 Anvilrage Medics, 10 Anvilrage Soldiers and 10 Anvilrage Officers. Return to him once your task is complete.
Game Description:

By order of Warlord Goretooth, commander of the Kargath Expeditionary Force:

Head of the K.E.F. reconnaissance division, Grandmaster Lexlort, has returned with news of the whereabouts of high ranking Dark Iron officials. Through locked gate, near the heart of the city, they train their forces to snuff out our men. Travel to Blackrock Depths and destroy them!

Completion of this mission will result in a tribute.

main.body:
This quest is the prereq:
http://www.wowhead.com/?quest=4081
To get this quest, you'll have to do first the KILL ON SIGHT: Dark Iron Dwarves quest.
Picked up from the Wanted sign outside the Kargath inn (in case this quest is low level to you).

You can find the most of the Medics and Soldiers in The Domicile (between the Vault and Shadowforge City, or accessible via the Upper ring of Law)
The Officers (grouped with Soldiers and Medics) can be found on the Upper ring of Law (spectators) and in the Detention Block (from the entrance left though the gate, you'll need a key)

It does not count towards Loremaster

If you have a shadowforge key, go left from the entrance and through the gate onto the Dark Iron Highway. Every group here has one officer and a mix of medics and soldiers, and there are enough officers to fulfill the quest requirements.

I would recommend having a couple of people trailblaze - preferably those don't have the quest - and kill orcs (non-elite, level ~55) in and around the fortress, so that those with the quest can stay close to Grark and can walk him out safely.

Stay back from him, where possible. When he stops, and spawns the ambushes, if you're on top of him, it's easy to panic and get over-run, especially if you're training adds (i.e. there's a squad of orcs still chasing you). If you hold back, you can send in a sap/sheep/MC and deal with the first batch pretty easily.

If you die and release, you fail. I imagine you can be ressed safely, but since I'm the priest, and they pooped on me, I can't be sure.

The second batch are, as mentioned, a pack of dragonkin. He'll try to walk straight through the encampment, but as mentioned, just skirt it, keep him in range, and they won't get involved. This is the best quest in WoW, [i]ever[/i]. Truly an epic adventure. I don't know whether my favourite part was waiting around for him to spawn, waiting for him to start walking or following him as he walked incredibly slowly to his destination. All of it was so exciting.

And if anyone is wondering how long this little trip takes (that is, after he's done the appropriate amount of stretching, said his goodbyes, gone to the toilet, turned everything off, and checked he's remembered everything he'll need to take with him) expect a trek around the ten minute mark.

This quest is quite tedious.  You actually DO escort him all the way from Blackrock Stronghold to inside of Blackrock Mountain.  And yes, the guy you escort walks as fast as you do when you walk slowly.  Along the way, you'll be ambushed.  The first time, 4 non-elite orcs, the second is 3 non-elite orcs and 2 elite dragonkin, the third is 3 Searing Drakes, and right before the end I saw another drake spawn, but he despawned immediately, so not sure about that.

1. Clear the room first - careful there's an elite in there that looks like the rest of him.

Okay, finally got it to work this way, used the shackles on him about 7 times, and him just standing there, after 5 minutes he would just disapear... so finally I abandoned the quest, lost the shackles, but then he offered the quest again and immediatly followed. If you've been bugged and waited like quite a few 5 minutes for him to walk, try this one, seems like not everybody is affected by this bugged quest in the same way.

During the escort, there will be 3 waves of ambush. The first wave appears just as you leave the fortress area and walk up into the rocky landscape, consisting of 2 non-elite and 2 elite orcs. The second wave appears just at the foot of the bridge up to blackrock mountain, consisting of 2 non-elite dragons and 2 elite orcs. The third wave will appear on the middle of the bridge, consisting of 3 non-elite dragons.

You will fail the escort if you get out of a certain range. Death does not fail you, but releasing to a graveyard beyond the range will. Surprisingly, if you die at the first ambush you will not fail the quest as the graveyard is close enough.

A good strategy to deal with the ambushes is to stay mounted and far behind the escort. The mobs will not target you, merely surround the escort. If you are far enough behind, you will not aggro them initially and the escort will just stand and wait until the mobs have been defeated. The advantage in this is that you can split the mob into two by pulling. The first wave is linked two and two, elite and non-elite. The second wave is linked two and two as well, but opposite (non-elite + non-elite and elite + elite). The third wave is not linked at all, however the dragons come at a periodic rate so if you are fast to pull you can separate them anyway.

The most difficult part of the quest is getting out of the fort. You should clear the way before engaging the escort in combat, as once he begins to walk he will not wait e
as of 3.3, you still have to wait for 3-5 min.

Make sure to kill every mob in the ambushes (Or at least, the first ambush.).

It also seems that, if, for whatever reason you need to move away from your computer while the escort is in progress, you can 'pause' it by quickly moving out of aggro range of the ambushes before they occur (Grark speaks shortly before the ambushes occur.). I'm not sure for how long you can do this, but I still think it would be handy for any emergencies.

Get Grark down to 25% health or so and he submits to you. Then start the next quest to escort him to Blackrock Mountain. He walks through tons of NPC camps, but you can just ignore them and walk around and he'll be fine. He calls 2 elites and 2 non elites, and if you stand far enough back they don't aggro and he stands still. Then you can pick them off one by one with sap/sheep/charm/etc. and he starts walking again. Then he gets to the bottom of the Blackrock Mountain ramp and calls 2 elites humanoids and 2 elite dragonkin. Again, stand far back and you can take your time. About 200 feet up the ramp he summons 3 56-57 dragons, but they seem to have low HP or something because they went down pretty fast. Then when you get into the mountain, he laughs and a few seconds later about 10 or so non-elites run at you from around the corner. If you have a rogue/druid, you can have them stealth along with Grark and have the rest of the party wait. Grark will go up alittle bit farther, and call 3 humanoid elites and a 58 dragon. Wait for a bit and the 10 non elites will despawn and your party can catch up with you. Then sap/sheep/etc. and once you beat the last guys some green Horde NPCs come out and chop off his head. Good luck!

Grark Lorkrub is not located inside BRD - he is inside the Blackrock Stronghold (40,34) in Burning Steppes (just to your left as you exit Blackrock Mountain).

Be warned that when you use the Thorium Shackles on him to turn him hostile he hits quite hard - harder than most 58elites in the game, he also takes a bit of work to get his health down. Once he is around 30% you use the Thorium Shackles again to begin an escort quest. This involves him walking from Blackrock Stronghold around up into Blackrock Mountain and through to the other side. Along the way he will stop three times and spawn a npcs. 

The first time is four Blackrock orcs, the second is two orcs and two elite Black Dragonspawn and the final time is three Searing Drakes.

Once at the other side you will be told to go to Kargath to collect your reward. If your quest was bugged like mine and you lost your shackles you can still complete the escort then talk to the quest giver to get another Thorium Shackle before turning it in.

There are a few tricks to make this quest easier for you and your group. First, clear the trash mobs out of the yard in front of Grark's stronghold FIRST, then get in there and defeat him fast. They will not have respawned by the time you bring him out.

When you are walking with him towards the mountain, do not walk directly on top of him, stay somewhat to his [b]left[/b]. By doing this, you will be able to avoid the unrelated camps of mobs he will walk through. This isn't an ordinary escort quest; he WON'T aggro non-quest mobs if your party doesn't come in their range. He's one of the bad guys, he's friends with all these mobs! The only mobs you have to fight are the ones that he spawns himself.

The first few groups he spawns are easy if you have a full party, because he stands still for them. But when you get up on the ramp, for the last couple of groups he will continue walking. You must pay attention to this and continue moving with him even as you're fighting the mobs. Don't get distracted. If he gets too far ahead of you, the quest will fail.

If you're having a hard time and you play on a PvE server, try doing the quest during peak time when many people are hanging around the mountain. The mobs aren't particular about who they attack, and several times while we were doing the quest some of them got trained away by people trying to help, or just innocent bystanders. This will help you, not hurt you (though it will hurt the people who get jumped by the elites!).

As most people know, this quest is the beginning of a short chain which ends with a Sunken Temple quest.  Keep in mind that Sunken Temple is intended for characters from their mid-40s to early 50s.

There are a couple problems with what should have been a simple collect quest:

1)  Seems like the only Bloodpetal that drops the quest items at a DECENT droprate are Bloodpetal Trappers.  There aren't many of them.

2)  The Trappers that [i]are[/i] around, are sprinkled in heavily packed zones.  You pretty much have to watch your back at all times to make sure some random Ooze or Pterodox doesn't jump you.  This slows the process of collecting them.  I was killing more of these things just to get to the 1 or 2 Trappers I saw.

3)  And just when you thought it was difficult enough, there are numerous level 56-60 Elite T-Rex that roam the very same area as the Bloodpetal Trappers.  I'd understand if there was 1 T-Rex terrorizing the area, but thus far, I've counted nearly 4.  Not to mention, if you go south of the Trappers, toward the Lake, there are more elite mobs with pets.

All in all, this quest is a !@#$%.  But it's something you should do, if you need the ST quest [b]Haze of Evil[/b].

Good luck!

Go to the Sunken Temple in Swamp of Sorrows. You actually have to GO INSIDE THE INSTANCE. To clarify.

Once you are actually inside the instance, head down the path infront of you that leads to the right, the wall with the masks on it. Follow that and you will come to a room with two sets of stairs: one going up, one going down. Watch out for the pat here. It's two trolls and two imps. If you stay kinda angled in the room before the stairs to just where you can see the stairs, you want to wait for those guys to go upstairs at least, that's what I did. I imagine it is a long pat cause once they go up those stairs, we weren't bothered by them fora while. 

When they have passed, go down. You should be in The Hall of Serpents...or Snakes...same thing, right? The stuff drops off of the giant worms and elemental thingies within this hall. But, YOU NEED TO KILL AS MANY MAGGOTS AS YOU CAN since they will all aggro when you aim for the worms of elemental thingies. They also aggro when you kill one of thier own. Least...that's what happened to us. 

Since you act ually have to go into the instance, I recommend bringing a healer with you. A full party might be best...it's up to you. 

Hope this helps.

I also have feral gear on for when I solo.

Basically, I enter the instance, take the spiral stairs on my right going down. Stealth in. Now the trick is DO NOT TRY TO FIGHT THE OOZES! They are extremely hard when near death as they spawn oozelings which will pretty much make you unable to cast healing spells except the instants. The pats are random spawns. They can be either an ooze, murk worms or the lurkers. Kill murks and lurkers only, but not the ones with the grubs. I'd usually Ravage opening, get 5 combo points then Rip. Cast a Regrowth and Rejuvenation and then Bear form, and finish it off.

I fight the pat on the spiral steps, skip the next group of mobs with the grubs. Kill the pat in the hallway, and the other one that's alone after the pat. 3 Elites to kill. After you kill the three, go back upstairs and reset the instance, repeat. Took me 3 resets.

Good luck.

The quest isn't too hard to solo as a level 60 rogue. I think any other class would need a full party. 

I used nightscape boots to help with the stealth, I highly recommend them for this trip. Also, you'll want to have 300 lockpicking (though I don't know if you need it at 300, that's what I had) 

From the entrance, go straight between the two guards and into the courtyard. Be very careful, there are patrols with dogs doing circles. The guards won't see you, but if you're not careful the dogs will. The place you want to head is at your 2 o'clock position. As you get closer, you'll see the little jail cages suspended from chains. 

Follow the corrodor, avoiding dogs and patrols. Your minimap will show Windsor up as the little yellow dot we've all come to know and love. It should lead you to a cell that is guarded by three dwarves and a dog. 

Here's the tricky part. You have to get rid of the guards to pick the lock on the door to get to Windsor. The way I did it was to sap one of the guards, kill the dog and vanish. Wait for cooldowns, sap a guard, kill the other two guards (thank you blade flurry) and vanish again. Finally kill the last guard. The guards run, so use crippling poison. 

I had some epics in my gear which made life easier; I suspect though it could be managed with just blues, just brind blinding powder and maybe a healing potion or two. 

When you leave the instance, make sure you don't reset it. Once you turn in the quest, the chain will continue

As soon as you enter the instance, go straight into the first room.  It splits off into many paths.  Go to the right.  The three right passages all lead to the same place.  Right, left, and to the middle.  The two side passages circle around and join each other, the middle path has square rooms.  The high interrogator is what drops the key.  That mob is in the last room of the middle path.  You can get there from any of the paths.  I don't know about the random cell location.  Bring a hunter :)
You can find him if you take the first passage on the right from the entrance.
When you get near the correct cell you'll hear him scream to let him out.

The quest seems to end like *poof*, nothing to be done next, BUT if u continue with some little darkiron dwarves farming u might get " a crumpled up note" from them, thats your next path. Give that to Marshal and you shall continue. I dont know the %drop but i do know u can farm the Slaves outside instance too, there's where i got mine.

Good day.

To quote someone that wrote it up so nicely at the END of the quest listings, I thought I would move it up to the front, so that anyone printing out the steps, could save some paper.

--------------------------------------------------
By revoluti0n, Alliance Drakefire Amulet quest chain

To enter Onyxia's Lair, you must endure these steps:

1) Dragonkin Menace (Elite) from Halrendis in Morgan's Vigil, Burning Steppes.
2) Talk to Marshal Maxwell in Morgan's Vigil.
3) Talk to Magistrate Solomon in Lakeshire.
4) Talk to Highlord Bolvar Fordragon in Stormwind.
5) Talk to Magistrate Solomon in Lakeshire.
6) Talk to Marshal Maxwell in Morgan's Vigil.
7) Find Marshal Windsor in Blackrock Depths jail.
8) Return to Maxwell.
9) Find a random "A Crumpled Up Note" drop from a random dwarf in Blackrock Depths.
10) Take said note to Marshal Windsor.
11) Retrieve Marshal Windsor's Lost Information from General Angerforge and Golem Lord Argelmach (two pieces).
12) Escort Marshal Windsor out of Blackrock Depths jail.
13) Meet Marshal Windsor at gates of Stormwind.
14) Escort Marshal Windsor to Stormwind Keep to unveil who Lady Katrana Prestor really is. (Spoiler: Onyxia)
15) Stand way the hell back while Bolvar fights the elite dragons.
16) Travel to Winterspring to find Haleh. Find lots of elite blue dragons and run to the back of the cave, where you'll see a rune on the floor. It's hard to see, so you will die a few times.
17) Haleh tells you to go kill Drakkisath in Upper Blackrock Spire.

After you turn this quest at Marshal Maxwell, he doesn't give you a follow-up quest. Instead you have to return to Blackrock Depths and kill mobs until you find [url=?item=11446]A Crumpled Up Note[/url], which [url=?quest=4264]continues the chain[/url].

After each time I killed the pair. The note finally dropped. That is the easiest way to solo it, although someone said youc could farm the slaves outside the instance. I decided to go in to make sure I didn't waste my effort. 

Of course, if you go with a group to do BRD, you should get the note fast and be able to do the rest of the quest. I did it solo because my guild was busy and I wanted to get it done.

Although it doesn't state it here, you get a choice of 3 items in addition to the XP.  Conservator Helm, Windshear Leggings, Shieldplate Sabatons.  If you aren't going to use any of them, the Windshear Leggings sell for the most at 1 Gold 44 Silver 46 Copper.

main.body:
He's easily soloable as a 53 Frost mage with a little ingenuity; ended the fight at full health and half mana, didn't have to pot or gem at all.

At the start, throw up Ice Barrier and Fire Ward, summon your Elemental, and let the pet aggro.  Stand as far back as possible, pop Icy Veins, and go to town on him until you pull aggro off the elemental.  Keep nuking until your Fire Ward and Ice Barrier are both down, then Ice Block.  Pyron will run back to the elemental; when he's far enough away, click off Ice Block and finish him off.

Same strategy works for pretty much every elite that's immune to snares for Frost mages, so keep it in mind once you get to Outland.

- Make sure that everybody in your group turns in the quest prior to that *before* starting Jail Break.  If they do and some other members haven't turned in yet, they won't get credit and be rightfully mad ad you.

It is very annoying to get a group together and plow through the long, hard and tedious escort only to discover that you haven't received credit for it at the end and have to do it all over again. So, here are some warnings:

1. [b]Make sure EVERYONE has talked to Windsor and completed "A Shred of Hope" before ANYONE accepts "Jail Break!"[/b]. This means you all need to be standing in range of Windsor and see a "!" over his head. Then, when someone (anyone) accepts the quest, a dialog box should pop up on everyone else's screen saying "x has started Jail Break! Would you like to accep the quest too?" or something similar. If Windsor starts moving and you don't have "Jail Break!" in your quest log, it's time to reset the instance.

2. [b]Do not release your spirit.[/b] If you release your spirit, you will be de-linked from the quest and won't receive (Complete) credit at the end, even if you're revived by a party member before you zone in. It won't be marked (Failed) either, so it can be very misleading. The GMs won't help you out either so this is your warning. The second you release your spirit, it's time to reset the instance.

3. [b]Don't let Windsor die or go out of sight.[/b] Just like any escort quest if Windsor dies or goes out of visible range the quest will be marked "Failed" and it's time to reset the instance.

When you inter the BRD instance, go to the right. There are multiple cells and he is in one of them. He pops up on your minimap when you are close to him, so it isn't too hard to find him.

The Royal Historian Archesonus, who stands next to the King of IF, gives the prerequisite quest for this quest

https://www.wowhead.com/forever/quest=3702

Walking straight up the ramp from the entrance, Kharan's cell can be found in the third side-tunnel entrance to the right off the large, circular main "lobby" area. It's fairly easy to tell if you're near the cell, because Kharan will show up as a quest objective on your map. You'll need a key to gain entrance to his cell, which is dropped off the mobs in the immediate area (the key is dropped only once, and only one party member may pick it up), or a rogue can lockpick his or her way in. Don't forget to talk to Kharan and listen to his story, then grab the followup quest that brings you back to King Magni Bronzebeard!

Solo'ing isn't a matter of friends/no friends, it is just another way to play the game.  IMHO, a much more fun way to play the game because: (1) you only have to worry about what the mobs are going to do, even the ones named Leroy, (2) it is a greater challenge to take on a place that seems to be designed for a party and try to solve the puzzle / instance / dungeon on your own, (3) when solo'ing, I rarely if ever have to quibble about the loot, bicker about who skins, listen to tank wannabees whine about poor healing, worry about where the youngest herbalist/miner has wandered off to, figure out a time when everyone can play (or wonder who these people are if it is a pickup group), etc.

Oh, and the loot.  Then more loot and, if there is any left, all the rest of the loot.  But that's just me, a greedy little nightelf :)  Sure, I may not get every instance and maybe some dungeons cannot be solo'd (we'll see) but there's plenty of space in the game for both types of players, even in dungeons.

Vilkasmanga
Guildmaster, Soloists Guild

I've done this quest and helped people do it succesfully both hurting the princess and not hurting the princess.

Twice when I've done it she hasn't become friendly and both times it was because the princess either wasn't in line of sight or wasn't in range of the emperor.

The princess doesn't have to be within healing range of the emp - I've found about half way across the room from him is ideal - but much further than that and you risk her not turning friendly.  Other than that, you need to make sure the princess has a clear line of sight on the emp when he dies; you can't have him around a corner from her or up by the throne when he's down below.

Anyway, I hope this post helps clear up some of the confusion and myths surrounding this quest.

It's not true that you will fail if the princess takes damage. If she doesn't turn friendly when the emp dies then you hit a bug or something.

What we did was had the warrior tank the emp, and had the pally offtank the princess far enough away from the emp so she couldn't heal the emperor. Very easy this way, just put your healer(s) between the tanks.

The pally was obviously chopping away at the princess during this time, as soon as the emperor died she truned friendly. It makes no difference whether she takes damage or not for her to change faction for you. By far the simplest way to complete this quest is just to keep her away from the emperor.

I do emp runs all the time now for loot and shard farming; every single time this is the way we do it. Usually the princess has about half hp by the time the emperor is dead and her health goes back to full right when he dies and she changes faction. In my opinion if you try to do this without hurting her at all (meaning that she will heal the emperor), you are just asking for a very difficult fight.

Did this as a level 80 H priest for Loremaster. You would need Shadowforge Key, and health pots, fire shields, or something to keep you viable through lava:

1. Take the easy way to the boss: Enter instance, go left, unlock door. Take the tunnel to the Dark Iron Highway, and pass the mobs (or kill them, whatever) to the opened doors at the end of the Highway. 
2. You'll see Lord Incendus. Kill him, or avoid him (whatever) and jump off the left side of the platform into the lava. Since I'm a priest, I used bubble and renew and I was just fine. 
3. Swim North-East in the lava until you see a bidge to your right. Swim just under the bridge, there is a ramp out of the lava on the east side. 
4. Enter the hallway, kill Magmus, enter torch room.
5. Kill the "red guys" in the torch room- they are the only mobs that are RED and move, so they're easy to ID. Kill 2, loot the torches, and set the blazier afire. The door behind you will open.
6. To be safe, kill the mobs in the room with Thaurissan- while an 80 plate wearer might be able to tank the boss, and the senators (and other adds) it's just easier to clear the room first.
7. Blow the boss up, and when he's dead, Moira goes green. Turn in quest, and presto!

Once you get behind the Inn, kill the guild between the Inn and the house on the right. Watch for wandering guards and kill 1-2 of them if you can. Once inside the Inn, there is a caster just inside. Freeze or Polymorph him and then run upstair and end the 3rd furthest to the right. You'll see hairy Apothecary Bernard in the room. Once you come back, rez all the way in the back of the room, so none of the guards outside or in the other rooms with aggro you. Heal immediately with a potion and when Bernard attacks, Polymorph his ass into a sheep and then take Benard's Journal from his book shelf. Then Hearthstone back to U.C. I did this mission solo with a level 14 undead rogue, and I'll tell you how!
Make sure you have:
- stealth skill
- ranged weapon (I prefer crossbows)
- a decent weapon (the best is dualwield with two swords with minimum 8.5 DPS, I have two scimitars - bought from the armorer in Undercity for 34s80c)
- a few restoring potions in case you mess things up
The trick:
First activate stealth, then follow the wooden citywall behind the houses till you find the big inn-like house (look at the map), when you stand at the angle behind the house shoot the guard from a distance that blocks the way when he is alone (he will notice you if you go around him), kill him and restore sitting or taking a potion. When you are in full strength activate stealth again and walk into the house. You will have to go upstairs, but the guy in the center blocks the way and will not move! Jump from the table to the stairs and go up (make sure this is all done in stealth mode!). When you are upstairs the quest-room is behind you, BUT DO NOT GO IN THERE, first take out the guards in the other two rooms (stay in the room while you fight them) so they will not come help the boss. Then shoot from a distance the last guard to lure him to you and kill him. Restore in one of the rooms and enter Berards room. Now you can fight Berard without him getting helped by his annoying guards, when you kill him, he may give you a nice item. Take his journal and leave the house like you entered

Put the device on a hotbar for easy access.  The device doesn't have a long range, so you'll have to be fairly close to activate it, so you might  aggro the whelp by proximity alone.  You will defintitely aggro it when you activate the device.  

The device acts as a short channeled cast (~2 seconds).  If the whelp is already aggroed, its attack could interrupt your device use and force you to repeat it.  As such, melee users should use the device to start the fight.  

For ranged users, you can attack at range so long as you remember to close the distance to activate the device before you kill the whelp.  This shouldn't be a problem for hunters/warlocks who can tank the whelp with a pet.  As a mage, I cast fire ward and ice barrier, attacked from range a few times, and then counterspelled one of the whelp's fireballs.  The whelp would close to melee range and I'd frost nova it.  Then I could use the device without interruption and then hit it with an instant cast or two to kill it.  

This quest can easily be soloed since the whelps are all single pulls.  Most of the mobs in the area patrol short distances, so just be aware of your surroundings to avoid unwanted adds, particularly the 52+ drakes.

[url=http://birdfall.blogspot.com/2008/10/pup-and-spider-or-crap-im-still-lost.html]My detailed directions.[/url]

[b]Get into Lower Black Rock Spire (Quick Summary):[/b]
Head upward to the Meeting stone, enter the passage behind, go up and bear right the whole way.

[b]Get to the Spiders (Quick Summary):[/b]
Enter instance, go up onto the bridge, turn right, and jump down.  Just before the first wooden bridge, head right and look down (should see two red tents below you).  Jump.  Head right and wind your way through the mobs and tents until you see the spiders up an incline.  (Watch for patrols in packed areas if alone.)

[b]Get to the Worg Pups (Quick Summary):[/b]
After the spider area, keep moving forward.  You'll see ogres.  Bypass them by dashing around the corner (there's also an area you can jump up on to avoid running around the corner, but I can't remember where).  Head straight (avoid the Spire Scorpids on your right) through the doorway, then turn right.  Pups by the boss in the room at the end.
One thing to be careful of when doing this at 80, the mobs die fast. I had to try this twice as the first time I ended up AOE killing all the pups before I realized they were the quest mob.

One thing to keep in mind is you can use the pup cage even if you're in combat.  On several occasions in LBRS, the pups have aggroed the groups I was with while fighting that orc pack near their niche.  If that happens and you're on this quest, just target one of the pups and activate the cage.  You'll take out an add and complete your quest all in one go.

Here is the short story...

Go into the cave and find Emberstrife (https://www.wowhead.com/forever/npc=10321).  He is all alone so don't worry about ads. I just did this last night, successfuly, and figured a better walkthrough of the entire event would've helped me not waste a few hours of my life. Enjoy.

1. The very first step of creating the UBRS keys is to gather these 4 items from LBRS
- Unadorned Seal of Ascension: random drop from mobs in LBRS
- Gemstone of Spirestone: random drop from Highlord Omokk
- Gemstone of Smolderthorn: random drop from War Master Voone
- Gemstone of Bloodaxe: random drop from Overlord Wyrthmalak

2. Once you have these 4 items, you must turn them into Vaelan in LBRS. He's located at the top of the slope that is right before the first wooden bridge. If you go to the very top of that slope, look left, you'll see a single orc at the very end of that flat area. That's Vaelan in disguise. He will transform back to his normal self when you get close. Speak with him. He says a few things and eventually lets you complete the 4 item Seal of Ascension quest. You now should get another Seal of Ascension quest which sends you to Dustwallow Marsh. Vaelan gives you a box containing (1) Orb of Draconic Energy and (1) Unforged Seal of Ascension. Both of these items have 5 charges which equates to 5 chances at getting your Unforged Seal, Forged. If you fail all 5 times you will have to go Gem hunting again.

3. Get a group of 5 or so capable people and head to Dustwallow Marsh. The quest, Seal of Ascension, describes how you must find the ancient drake known as Emberstrife and use him to forge your seal. The c

In current Classic, this quest can't be done for several people at once. Even if you (and other group members) will place more than one seal, after using special ability, you'll get only one "forged seal", that can be looted (with gear icon on mouseover). The dragon has a 3-hour cooldown on his first ability after successful seal forging, so you'll need to kill him anyway and wait for 3-5 minutes to respawn, to forge the seal for the next group member.
Tested more than 5 times.

If multiple people are doing this quest at the same time, they can all place their unforged seals on the ground. Only one person has to mind-control Emberstrife and use the correct spell to forge them. Since the attack must hit all of the seals, it is recommended that you place them all together.

If by some chance you miss one of them, someone else can mind-control him and try again. When I did this quest, it appeared that the attack you need to use in the pet bar (the left-most one) was usable once per mind-control, rather than having a cooldown.

Emberstrife is located in a cave in the far SE corner of Dustwallow Marsh.  He's further SE than Onyxia's Lair.  Lots of 41+ dragonkin in the area, but they should all be grey to you if you're high enough to get this quest.  

You'll need a party, but if you've just finished LBRS, you should have plenty available.  A 5-man group of anyone in their high 50s should be sufficient.  You'll need a tank and a healer would be very helpful, but otherwise any class type will do.  It's preferable to have the quest-holder (whoever has the Unforged Seal) not be the main tank.  

Emberstrife is the only thing in the cave.  A shallow lake (about waist-deep on a gnome) surrrounds the rocky peninsula on which he stands.  You can circle around to where you can climb up the peninsula and attack him there, but don't.  We did once and his proximity to the cave's ceiling caused sporadic "Target is not in line of sight" errors for our ranged-attackers.

Instead, face Emberstrife head-on.  Vaelon will have given whoever has this quest 5 charges of something.  (I didn't have it, but so I don't know the official name, but you'll have 5 charges of it.)  The quest-holder will also have an Orb.  The quest-holder should set the Orb up in his/her inventory so that he/she can easily use it when the time comes.  

When everyone is ready, have the quest-holder throw down one of the 5 charges in the water in front of Emberstrife.  Doesn't have to be right up next to him; anywhere between your shore and Embers
Dragon can be found 54,84 in a cave on Dustwallow march

After several attempts buggered due to various reasons, and no comments here with instructions I thought I'd try.

When you're in his cave, stay on the bottom in the water. If you fight up top there are a bunch of LOS bugs as stated previously. Just pull it down and it'll work it's way around to you.

When the fight begins, cast your seal on the ground in front of it. Do your thing until it's almost dead and it lets you use your seal. Make sure your party knows to stop attacking it when it goes "blue" and is your minion.

For those who have no experience with mind control or summoned pets, there will be a channeling thing on your screen. This does not mean that he's doing the task he's supposed to, that is the time left on how long you will be in control.

Above your hotkey bar you will see some new spell icons. There should be 4 on the right side. The first one is something along the lines of "Dragonflight." That is what you want. Use that on the seal and it should drop control from the dragon after.

Finish the mob off and then loot the now "Forged" seal from the ground.

I hope this helps out.

This hasn't yet been described well, so here goes.

Enter the BRS instance, kill mobs in the first room so you can go *right*.  It doesn't matter if you use the drop or go directly below, you end up in the same place.

Now you have a slope upwards to your right (you're facing south), and more mobs ahead.  Kill these, and the patrol that comes from the tunnel ahead/left, and go through that tunnlel (eastwards, with a wiggle).

Now you're where you can hug right and do a couple of drops to be at the left/right choice for Mother Smolderweb or the way to the troll area.

That's what you don't do, instead you kill the two groups of mobs in front of you.  Now look up and left, you should see a lone 'Scareshield Infiltrator', this is actually Vaelan in disguise. Now to get to him....

You'll probably have to kill the next set of mobs just on the slope ahead, so do that. Now look LEFT and go into the dark and up the slope there, and hook around to jump up to where Vaelan is.  He'll lose his disguise as you approach.

Just FYI, only one person at a time can do this quest.

Once a person MC's the dragon and uses the ability ("Flames of the Black Flight") the ability goes on a 3h cd. You have to kill the dragon to use the ability again.

If by any chance you run out of charges, you can use other people's charges. I ran out of unforged seals, so a party member dropped his, another MC'd and I was able to loot the forged seal. Also forgot to mention ember can resist your mc, it happened to me once.

I hope this helps!

When MC'ing Emberstrife, you will actually have *two* abilities that involve the breathing of fire.  One of them, the second from the left, has an icon with a flame on it and is called "Breath of Flame", "Flame Breath", or something similar.  This is NOT the one you want to use, as it does not convert an Unforged Seal of Ascension into a forged one.

The other fire breathing ability, which is the first from the left, is actually called "Flame of the Black Dragonflight" and is the one you want to use.  Its icon is a yellow inscription of some sort that looks nothing like a flame.

The reason I mention this is because when I did the quest, either something in my UI obscured the FotBD icon or I didn't see it in all the clutter, so the only relevant ability I saw was Emberstrife's standard flame breath attack.  Needless to say, I was frustrated when I used up three of my Orb of Draconic Energy's charges and the ability didn't forge the seal.  After researching more online and disabling all my addons to ensure that the FotBD icon would be visible, I tried again and it worked.

It should also be noted that the Orb of Draconic Energy and the Unforged Seal of Ascension both have 5 charges each. I just completed the quest after 3.0.3 patch, with a level 70 pally tank, and just wanted clear up a few things.

Right from the start to find Vaelan you need to go into LBRS, thru the entrance and down to the right, follow around to the left and as you start to go down again there is a slope on your left. Follow it up to the top and get onto the ledge. Over in the back lefthand corner is an Orc which when you chat to him turns into Vaelan. So now the quest begins. 

I received all four items from the boss with 100% drop rate, but you have to roll for it if in a group. Collected the item and chatted to Vaelan and in my inventory was a gift box that contained the unforged seal and mind control orb. Then I went on my merry way to Duskwallow Marsh.

[b]How to solo it:[/b]
I manage it on lvl 46 with mage 1400hp

Steps:
1: Look on the map, you can see there 2 small lakes 1 cave and 3 building marks and one long road with many serpentines.
2: CAVE on the map is the fake one, do not go there (our cave is not marked on map)
3: Look on the map on the name of the place: Called JINTHA ALOR
4: You need to get on letter N on the map. (do not take a turn on letter T it is next turn)
5: If you are alone then just run with the horse then respawn in a safe place and run again, takes me 1 death. 
6: As soon as you are on the bottom of letter N you suppose to see small amphitheatre with an altar in middle and 2 big waterfalls in behind.
7: The cave is right in the middle of waterfalls, like 20 meters from altar.
8: Run to cave if you die just rerun, Egg is in the last room, exactly on coordinates from wowhead. You really can't miss it
9: Now it's a hardest part, takes me 3 deaths to figure out how to do it. The 3 mobs which are patrol around an egg have a phase when they stop for a second, now you need to stand on another side of the egg release and take the egg, if you do it properly you will finish the looting before they attack you. Thanks to Muddbog for his useful comment. You can start looting from the bottom of the rock.

Reach the cave by whatever means. You can mount all the way if you want. Right up to the entrance.

The important part... at the end of the cave, the egg is in the center. 3 patrols circle it. The first 2 (in my spawns) were chicks. The last one was a guy.

I'll label it A - 1st chick, B - 2nd chick, C - 3rd chick.

After trying to retrieve the egg in my first time (and dying before i can... they interrupted me..) I observed in spirit form and noticed that...

In the room, towards the WALL, looking ACROSS, chick B walks awfully close to the egg.. but then later moves TOWARDS (sorta looks like they're merging) with chick A. So when chick B moves AWAY  from the egg and TOWARDS chick A, thats when you can accept your corpse, or release stealth, and click on the egg. By the time they find out and run towards you, you've already have gotten the egg.

BTW, this can be easily done with distract it seems.. but the tip was for non-rogues.

The map shows A cave in Jin'Thara but it's not the right cave.  The one you want is located behind the altar that you use for the enchanted mallet quest. The cave that's shown in the map is where the missing gryphon is. 

Anyway, it's a long zig-zag trail through the city to get to this point, full of level 47 elite through level 50 elite trolls. Some are easier to avoid than others. 

You don't have to kill the guys standing at the altar to get to the cave.. just sneak around behind them. 

Once inside the cave, all three paths lead to the egg; HOWEVER, there are a LOT of enemies in here. 

If you have more than one person doing the quest, you have to wait for the egg to reappear once one person gets it (roughly a 15 second wait). 

Once you get the egg, exit the cave, make a clear enough area to get on your horse, and hightail it out of there. If you follow the stone path to the stairs and DO NOT STOP, you should be fine. 

The regeneration rate in that city is ridiculously fast.

If you're gonna go to this place, it's recommendable that you do the other quests here too:

Saving Sharpbeak. Given from the guy in the aviari behind the Alliance FP in The Hinterlands. It's a detective quest that ends in Jintha'Alor with your freeing Sharpbeak, a cute baby gryphon.

The Mallet of Zul'Farak - not actually a quest. You have to kill some easy elite priests at one of the other temples in the Hinterlands to get the Sacred Mallet. Then you go to the Altar of Jintha'Alor - right in front of the cave with the ancient egg - and right click the mallet, and voila, you've got The Mallet of Zul'Farak - which is needed to summon Gahz'Rilla in ZF.
There's a quest in Shimmering Flats where you need to summon and kill Gahz'Rilla to get one of his scales, to get a carot on a stick (+3% mount speed). You need the Mallet of Zul'Farak to summon Gahz'Rilla. Annoying part: The carrot on a stick quest is level 42.

Sorry guys, this may seem not obvious to some people, like me. But the egg, to be clearer, is located in a cave. (As stated ^^) Heres how to get there. (Bring a fiend, suggested)

1. Enter Jintha'Alor, you'll notice it's full of nasty troll elites.
2. Work your way to the top of the "temple" (i suppose you can call it.) This isn't hard, just follow the roads and go up every set of stairs you come across.
3. Keep gonig up until you see a the cave that is marked on your map. This is not the right cave, but it is close to it.
4. Facing the cave, turn left. It is the very left route. You will enter a very opened - spaced, what you might call, ritual area. It is guarded by elite dogs, elite guards, and a named NPC. 
5. You will see also there is an altar in the middle of this place, with a horde troll on it, in a dead position. This marks the entry to the cave. The cave entrance is around where the troll is.
6. Work your way through the cave. This may require some naked suicidal runs to save repair bills, and lots of corpse runs, which thankfully, are around the horde base, so it isn't too far.

main.body:
[url=http://birdfall.blogspot.com/2008/10/pup-and-spider-or-crap-im-still-lost.html]My detailed directions.[/url]

[b]Get into Lower Black Rock Spire (Quick Summary):[/b]
Head upward to the Meeting stone, enter the passage behind, go up and bear right the whole way.

[b]Get to the Spiders (Quick Summary):[/b]
Enter instance, go up onto the bridge, turn right, and jump down.  Just before the first wooden bridge, head right and look down (should see two red tents below you).  Jump.  Head right and wind your way through the mobs and tents until you see the spiders up an incline.  (Watch for patrols in packed areas if alone.)

[b]Get to the Worg Pups (Quick Summary):[/b]
After the spider area, keep moving forward.  You'll see ogres.  Bypass them by dashing around the corner (there's also an area you can jump up on to avoid running around the corner, but I can't remember where).  Head straight (avoid the Spire Scorpids on your right) through the doorway, then turn right.  Pups by the boss in the room at the end.

If you are a tailor, I recommend that you not turn in this quest when complete! Just throw the eggs out so that you can continue to loot them. 

Each egg that you collect has a chance to spawn several spiders. Each spider has a chance to drop Ironweb Spider Silk and various other silks used in tailoring. The drop rate is good and because the eggs respawn, you can probably collect close to a hundred silk in an hour.

In short, the pet may be fun but the profit you could gain is very nice (especially if you disenchant items made with the silk).

The best drop you get from the spiders is the Ironweb Spider Silk. This stuff sells at the auction for a lot of gold. You can sell under 10 for over 50g or more.  The spiderlings that may attack as you are getting the eggs can be difficult, but the Ironweb is more than worth it.

As a rogue you can solo this, but not easily. There are 2 ways. Start by getting to Mother Smolderweb and engage her alone in combat. Put on evasion and let her whack at you until she poisons you. When she does, either:

1. Blind her and hearthstone right away, maybe make a macro to do it quickly since they both have the same exact time length.

2. Sprint up past the other spiders up towards the ogres and jump off the ramp onto a thin support beam above the orcs at the bottom. No enemies can get to you on this beam and they go into Evade mode and leave eventually. From here you can safely hearth.

Then make the annoying trip back to Burning Steppes to turn in the quest and get your worthless trinket reward. But at least you didn't waste an hour getting a 5 man group to this spider only to hearth and waste the rest of the instance.

You *do* have to leave the instance to get the quest done. You would pretty much have to set up a group specifically for this quest. Have the mage make a portal to IF, then head to Burning Steppes and complete it. Otherwise, no one else is really going to want to hang around and wait while someone heads to Steppes unless everyone is there to do the quest. The little spiders also drop an item that clears the "snare" effect.

Make sure, as a Druid, you do not have thorns on. I died 5 times trying to do this because she kept breaking hibernation as it registered her attack, and thusly my return damage from thorns, after I had allready cast hibernation and slept her.

Did it easily after that. I would start in Bear form and pull her with Faerie Fire, and then use Demoralizing Roar to try and help minimize her damage. I'd use demoralizing roar to heal up any missed health and then shift out and wait. At about half or 3/4 health I would hibernate her and heal. In my case I got the poison right before I hibernated her, but if not then I could redo it again after breaking her hibernation to let her attack again.

Solo'd this as a druid without using potions, I did use a scroll of protection IV and a scroll of stamina IV though, and it turns out I needed both.

Stealth to her, stand in the corner behind her. Regrowth yourself, rejuv yourself, and pull her. Then continue to heal yourself, but be aware that she interrupts sometimes. I used innervate early on just to be sure i didn't run out of mana, and nature's swiftness when i was interrupted. Once you have the poison, run as fast as you can across the big metal bar. At the very end of the bar, turn left, and jump off. There is a tiny little ledge that you can land on if you're careful. I made it to the ledge with 400 health to spare. ;)

It isn't impossible, but it'll likely take a couple of attempts, and a bit of luck. Gear for intellect, not stamina, as she'll force you to heal quite a bit.

The dungeon finder system added in patch 3.3 has made this quest extremely easy. Just go to Ragged John at Flame Watch, get the quest, join the queue for LBRS, and start the dungeon. After your group kills Mother Smolderweb, hit the "Teleport out of dungeon" button. Talk to John, have him "milk" you to complete the quest, and teleport back to the dungeon. Two minutes, tops.

Obviously, this only works if you're doing the quest at the appropriate level. And if queue times are long on your server, you might not want to sit in one place and wait for the LBRS queue to let you in, especially if you're dps. But if you want to get this quest done and waiting isn't a problem (if you're a tank or healer, or if you have a bunch of quests to do in the Burning Steppes while you wait, or if you just don't mind) then this quest is now much easier than it ever was.

This quest is actually soloable as a Rogue - that's how I did it back in the day.  The key is to get to a position where you *only* aggro Mother Smolderweb (as you're coming up the first ramp, the very far right corner should work I think), then have her attack and poison you.  If you are lucky enough, you can do this before she kills you (evasion might help here, I assume you can't dodge the poison effect).  Pop a vanish, get to safety, then hearth the heck out of there.  (setting your hearthstone up near Burning Steppes helps)

A Druid can also probably do this if they can hibernate her after they get poisoned. 

It's been a LONG time since I've done this (basically not long after the game came out), but I can't see how it wouldn't still be possible.
Keep in mind that you have to ask Ragged John to milk you in order to turn in the quest.

Theres been talk about getting people their onyxia key. Heres the steps in order.  The level requirement is the same as UBRS which I think is 58+. These are not all the quests just the major steps. There are also some short or easy quests in between I'm not bothering with since they can be solo'd. 

1) Warlord's Command - Picked up at Kargath. Have to kill 3 bosses in LBRS and find the document's there that randomly spawn at one of them. Has to be done in a 5 man party. Quest NPC then gives you rewards and sends you to speak with Trall's Advisor in Ogrimmer who gives you another quest to Speak to Thrall. 

2) For The Horde! - Given by Thrall in Ogrimmer. He sends you to UBRS to kill Rend. Can and should be done in a 15 man raid. Take Rends head back to Thrall for the next quest, a city wide buff, and some pretty nice rewards. 

3) The Champion of the Horde - Thrall will babble at you for a bit then send you to find Rexxar. This is more irritating than hard and can easily be accomplished solo. I only mention this step because he wanders and sometimes takes a bit to locate. Here's his path: Desolace, Feralas 
He sends you to a NPC in western plaugelands who is fairly easy to find - Myranda the Hag 

4) Ocullus Illusions - Myranda the Hag in WP sends you to UBRS to collect 20 dragon eyes. They drop from the dragon spawn there and can be collected in a raid. Once bring the eyes to her, she'll send you to emberstrife in dustwallow marsh with a amulet. 

5) The dragons - You'l

[ul]

I just found another reazlly useful thing for rogues to do in this quest.  Once you've downed every boss (we did wyrm, then omokk, then voone), at least 1 and hopefully 2 members have the documents.  With the group standing in voone's room, have the rogue stealth through the instance looking for the docs.  Once he takes them, go find them again (they take about 5-10 seconds to resapwn, so stick around as they might respawn at the same place!).  When you find them, destroy your docs and pick up the ones in front of you.  This will make them respawn somewhere else, hopefully in voone's room where you party is waiting!  We got our whole party's docs in one run by doing this, it was extremely easy.

BTW there are actually 4 possible document locations: Behind Wyrmthalak, to the left of Voone, behind Omokk, AND in that area with the ogres right after all the  spiders.  The first three areas are really easy for the rogue to stealth to and take docs (the boss guarding them is dead), but the last one may have ogres left (if you didnt kill them).  If the rogue has improved sap, he can sap the ogre closest to the docs and then grab them.  Since he has imp sap, the ogre wont ever agro and he can just restealth and walk away.  Quest done :)

Tired of having every group I run LRBS skip Bijou's belongings by doing the candle jump in [npc=9236]. I decided to solo it as a level 60 warrior.

It took me three [item=3823] and 20 minutes to get her belongings.

The first potion gets you from the instance portal, up the stairs, trough the doorway to the right and than jump down.

As you jump down you have a pack of three orcs + another pack of one orc and two worgs infront of you, This is the path you usually take. I instead go up to the stairs to the right, as there's a patrol of two legionary orcs paroling by. Standing on the stairs are safe.

With the next potion I run past the packs of orcs and worgs previously mentioned, trough the doorway and when I come into the open area I jump down to the right landing on a ledge going above the lava river.

Run along the ledge, take a left and run along another left. You are now overlooking the massive encampment of orcs at the bottom of the dungeon. Take note of where the patrols are and when it is safe jump down, run along the lava river, and than take a left into a corner. You'll be safe from patrols.

With the third potion you run towards the troll area, past the remaining orc camps, when you come the part where the stones have collapsed (pathway between troll and orc area) Bijou's belongings are tucked in along the walls.

Land on her belongings, loot them and either die or HS out.

It should be noted that there's no guarantee that the belongings are there, wowhead comments

First you have to get to Zul'Mashar which is in EPL in the NE corner. I just mounted and ran through all the trolls along the way to the altar. I did this solo as a 57 warlock.

The path up to the temple sorta sucks, mainly because of the troll Scouts.  If you engage one, they'll run to any nearby mobs, whether it's one or an entire encampment.  So it can go from fighting one mob to three or even four very quickly.  I managed to make it up the path with some difficulty, although it was nothing impossible.

Once you reach the top of the path, there's a wide open area, there's a sort of path on either side and a middle area.  In the middle are graves, stepping on these graves will summon a !@#$-ton of troll zombies which will immediately spell your demise.  Luckily, I only did this on the way out.  The middle seemed a little messy for me, as there's also already spawned zombies milling about on top of 2+ scouts.  To either side is a path with 2 small encampments of mobs on it.  There are random PATs all over the area, so I tried to take these down before engaging the encampments.  Using this method, I took the path to the left and it was pretty much easy street.  Once you get up to the corner of the temple, you're basically in the clear.  Hug the wall of the temple towards the front steps.  There is one mob on the steps who's easy to dispatch, none of the channeling mobs should attack.

For those of us that found this post unhelpful. Here is some tips for soloing(was level 59 warlock).

The mobs don't call for help. If you are not careful the scouts will run to the nearest guardpost and get help. The scouts did not start doing this until after I had gotton the tablets and Hameya's key.

Most of the mobs can passed without aggroing any of them.

BIGGEST TIP: Don't run through the graveyard in the central area at the bottom of the stairs of the temple. Infected Mossflayers will spawn everywhere. Make your way around one of the sides and jump over the wall at the bottom.

At the base of the temple just to the right of the stairs the fourth tablet is resting against the bottom tier wall. A lvl 59 Shadowhunter is channeling next to it. He can be killed without aggro from other mobs.

The third tablet as at the top of the temple on the left resting against the low wall. You can acquire this tablet without getting aggro from the channeler near it.

4th Tablet - 73,16

I completed this quest on 8 alts during 4 years, and I forget to take the flame in a bottle every damn time. Bad quest design.

Overall, a very difficult quest.  Perhaps the most difficult in the game (relative to level and Blizzard's expectations).

- Casters' Arcane Missiles are very high damage to take in.
- Hunters have pets to deal with.
- Medics can heal themselves and others.
- Mobs are bunched together, so pulling often results in aggro-ing several and running for your life.
- VERY fast respawn timers.
- Cannot plant flag in combat.

I completed the quest as a well-geared, level 51 pom-pyro mage without dying (although I ran for my life several times).  Here's how I did it:

1)  Make sure to take the Fire in a Bottle from behind the quest giver before you leave!
2)  Use any means necessary to get to the tent and set it ablaze (by right-clicking it).  You can do this in combat, and damage only slows the process down (it does not stop you from setting it on fire).  I simply pulled a side towards me, casted frost nova, and ran in and set it on fire (while getting hit slightly).  Then I ran for my life.
3)  Approach the camp from the north, killing as fast as you can.  The tent will respawn from being on fire, but don't worry about it.  Keep killing until you can stand right next to the dirt patch near the tent without being in combat.
4)  Use the tent given to you by the quest giver, and run for your life again.

[ul]
[li] After you pull one of the mobs, run back about 10 steps and then start attacking, this way if the mob decides to run you can easily kill it before it grabs more mobs. [li] If you have more than one mob on you and one of them is a mage, make sure you earthshock it every time the CD is up, this ensures the mage won't attack you for at least another 2 seconds. (will also make the mage run towards you if its far away)[/li]
[li] Pulling is all about geometry, I approached this from the south side, and honestly if you just make sure that the mob won't run diagonally into other mobs you should be fine.[/li]
[li] Don't fight the hunter's pet first, kill the hunter ASAP. Also even if you're a caster, get within melee range of the hunters, they hit much lower with their melee weapons...[/li]
[li] And if you ever screw up, just earthbind and ghost wolf for your life (and make sure you don't run into the farm next door, it can get ugly).[/li]
[li] Grounding Totem only takes in 1 of the mage's arcane missile hits, but its still pretty useful so use it ;P [/li]
[/ul]

Send in your pet at the elite and start torching (the above pic is a good reference about how far away to be). Hit AotC, start running and if you want and get your pet to follow (sacrificing is a very viable alternative, but rezzing slows the whole process). To get the quest:

Go to LBRS. From the entrance, go right up the ramp to the right. Jump down. You will see a mob with two dogs, etc...there is a door to the left...go through the doors; turn with the hallway...when you come out into the next room...turn  directly right and jump down on the ledge...run along the ledge and jump down one more level to the ground...there you will see mobs under camps...behind the first camp to the right you will notice an opening to a ramp which heads downward...fight the mob or use invisibility potion and then go down that ramp. At the bottom you will see the body where you can obtain this quest. You must be an armorsmith. After you get the quest...loot the same area again and you will get the Unfired Plate Gauntlets. You will need both the quest and the Unfired Plate Gauntlets item.

1. Return to Winterspring and to turn in the quest to Malyfous Darkhammer in Everlook. He will give you a follow-up quest to get him some mats.

3. Note: it's easiest to get these mats before you turn in the quest in the first place so you'd save a trip.
  -6 x Enchanted Thorium Bars
  -2 x Essence of Fire
  -4 x Star Ruby

Sadly, this means that for collectors, the plans for [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=12631]Fiery Plate Gauntlets[/url] are extinct, as well.  (And they were BoP, so don't go scanning the AH for them either - just /cry and move on.)

forever.body:
After turning in [url=?item=12845]Medallion of Faith[/url] to Aurius in the beginning (gained by looting a [url=?object=176112]chest[/url] in Stratholme Living side) he will come aid you at the fight against Baron.

Upon defeating him you will get the choice between these two fine things.

The Medallion of Faith is found in Human Strathholm about a third of the way into the actual 'scarlet crusade' part, inside of a small chest in a side room on the left of a hallway - this room contains a named mob that is for a quest (no loot, and I forget his name). 

Once someone has the medallion, you must assemble an Undead Strat group or raid. Only one person in the group needs the medallion; I believe everyone that has not already completed the quest will be elgibile for the reward if you are successful. I was able to complete the quest while I still had my own medallion after our priest turned theirs in to start the quest. 

Aurius himself is inside of the small building (a church) just inside of UD Strat. Speak with him to start the quest for that instance. If you fail to slay the baron, you will need to obtain a new medallion (or find someone else that has it to group with). 

Once started, you must clear UD Strat and kill the Baron. Partway throught the fight, Aurius shows up and attacks the baron - it is to my understanding that he will also heal members of your party, as he is a paladin. Once the baron is down, Aurius collapses and allows you to complete the quest, choosing either the necklace or ring for your reward. 

There as no faction reward for me at high Honored, but it did yeild 6800 exp at 60. 

I have not yet checked to see if I would be able to repeat the quest or do it in a raid - I did it in a great 5-man group.

You start off being teleported to Darrowmere Lake, near Scholomance.

Uses [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?spell=17168]Haleh's Will[/url] on you when you start [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?quest=5162]Wrath of the Blue Flight[/url]. 

I swear, it was so damn cool, I wanted to abandon the quest and go back to find her again and take the quest again, just to see it happen again.

What happens? [spoiler]She kicks you. In the face. You go flying... from Winterspring to Western Plaguelands. Luckily a lake breaks your fall, or you would've died.[/spoiler]

Actually, I think I WILL abandon this quest, just so I can go pick it up again any time I feel like seeing something awesome.

For best effect, try to be standing between her and the edge of the mountain you're on. If you're standing with her between you and the edge, she actually just kicks you through a mountain.

OK, so I'm doing the Wintersaber grind in Winterspring. And by grind, I mean 1 round a day, 3-5 rounds a week. So my hearth is going to be set to Everlook for a long time to come. I'm also doing wrapping up my Blackrock and Plagueland quests. Previously, the best way to get to Plaguelands was teleport (I'm a Mage) to Shattrath, take the Quel'Danas portal and fly to Light's Hope or Chillwind.

Now, I can hearth to Everlook, run to [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?npc=10929]Haleh[/url] (quickly, using the mountain+slowfall trick) and BAM! I'm at the Darrowmere Lake (Scholomance). Saves little time, but the novelty will take quite a while to wear off. I mean really, one kick from her and you end up [b][u]27181 yards away[/u][/b] (measured with Cartographer), on a different continent!

Lesson learnt: Don't mess with the Blue Dragonflight, or they'll kick your arse! [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?npc=28859](Or bring 24 friends)[/url].

Presumed to exist.  Only a greater chromatic dragonkin or dragon could pocess such a carapace.

[b]Information on the Chromatic Scale[/b]

Commonly found on the lesser chromatic flight: Whelps, Broodlings, lesser wyrmkin.

[b]Information on the Blood of Heroes[/b]

Legend claims that in places of extreme conflict, across what is now known as the Plaguelands; clean and holy springs may erupt from the ground.  The water from those springs has been named 'Blood of Heroes,' by artisans and commonfolk alike - in honor of those that fell in the war against the Scourge.

[b]Information on the Frayed Abomination Stichings[/b]

The threads that holds together the abominations of Stratholme are highly sought after by artisan craftsmen:  Extremly resilient - nearly unbreakable.

[b]Information on the Skin of Shadow[/b]

Used by the Barov family of the Scholomance as a mirror into the souls that they no longer possess.  A valuable keepsake.

forever.body:
[b]Information on the Chromatic Carapace[/b]

Presumed to exist.  Only a greater chromatic dragonkin or dragon could pocess such a carapace.

[b]Information on the Chromatic Scale[/b]

Commonly found on the lesser chromatic flight: Whelps, Broodlings, lesser wyrmkin.

[b]Information on the Blood of Heroes[/b]

Legend claims that in places of extreme conflict, across what is now known as the Plaguelands; clean and holy springs may erupt from the ground.  The water from those springs has been named 'Blood of Heroes,' by artisans and commonfolk alike - in honor of those that fell in the war against the Scourge.

[b]Information on the Frayed Abomination Stichings[/b]

The threads that holds together the abominations of Stratholme are highly sought after by artisan craftsmen:  Extremly resilient - nearly unbreakable.

[b]Information on the Skin of Shadow[/b]

Used by the Barov family of the Scholomance as a mirror into the souls that they no longer possess.  A valuable keepsake.

Chromatic Carapace is off Rend's Mount in Upper Blackrock Spire, and a descently rare drop at that. Binds when picked up.

The Brilliant Chromatic Scales drop off random high level elite dragonkin 57+ and are once again rather random.  NOT Binds when picked up.

Blood of Heroes spawns randomly on the ground in the Plaguelands.  Looting these will spawn 1-2 60+ elite 'Fallen Heroes' however you can loot even while they spawn  If you're a hunter freeze trap, loot, then run off and feign death.  Binds when picked up.

Skin of Shadows are also a ground spawn in Scholomance and possibly the most annoying of the items in my opinion.  Almost always on my server there is someone in group trying to make a shifting cloak and will also be after this.  And there is only one per Scholo run, so good luck and hopefully no ninja looting.  Binds when picked up

If you have a full set of Beaststalkers or Giantstalkers especially this will be a downgrade for you in DPS. However they are also possibly rarer then Giantstalkers' leggings and look very cool (Black with silver lining and trim) and are definite accomplishment.  Happy hunting everyone.

I managed to pull this quest off solo as a lvl70 rogue thanks to this [url=http://wow.allakhazam.com/db/quest.html?wquest=5213;page=1;howmany=50#m119795908282333476]post[/url]. Start by entering the side entrance and then opening the service entrance gate, pass through it and stealth. Continue up to the gauntlet gate and distract the stealth detecting mobs when needed. After you've opened the second gauntlet gate you'll see the boss you want to kill straight ahead. The door behind her will open when she dies and the chest you're looking for [i]may[/i] be inside. If not, you can have a shot at Nerub'enkan located to your left after the second gauntlet gate. But keep in mind that this fight will be alot harder because he's melee and he spawns two adds, at least he did for me.

 I had to use 2x evasion and a healing pot to survive even though I'm almost fully epic geared. Now, there's a risk that the chest is not located inside that place either and if so you'll have to reset the instance and try again (unless you feel like going for the third boss, which I never tried myself). MoD is strongly recommended, camouflage helps as well against the gargoyles. And remember that there's stealth detecting mobs in there that's also cloaked, called "Eye of Naxxramas", which you can only hope you won't encounter. It's also worth noting that the chest you're looking for is [i]not[/i] trackable with the dwarf racial "find treasure".
You can get the 2 trinkets (ap and spell damage), by dropping the one you got, and then speak with Betina Bigglezink, ask for one of them, and then ask for the other one faster.
Note that the Scourge Data needed for this quest spawns INSIDE the Ziggurats, so no need to look for it around and outside of them.

Adding a comment here since I finally found a competent 5 and completed this quest after having it on the log for months--Yes, just keep turning left and the store is in that dead end. 

No, you cannot complete this in raid, as with almost all other quests as of recent patches.

The dead end is naturally filled with mobs, and we found the Undead Courier there as well to kill him for the postbox keys. When you approach, the Great Fras Siabi himself shows up looking pretty ripe, and of course if you haven't cleared the area carefully and thoroughly first, you're in a position to get owned, which we almost did. Also don't screw around with the postbox until you're ready, as that spawns 3 elites too. After Fras is put down, everybody can loot the tobacco box for the win.

The Lighter isn't all that--with the exception of the fact that it doesn't get you drunk, it's graphically and effect-similar to Thunderbrew's Boot Flask. Yet another novelty trinket taking up space in the bank. 

If you're 5-manning Scarlet Strath, you might as well do this one as the dead end isn't very much additional work once you've cleared the street to that point anyway. It's not in itself a reason to do Scarlet Strath in 5, as the quest ends there and doesn't follow on to my knowledge. This, Flesh Does Not Lie, and Restless Souls are all pretty easy to complete in the first half-hour of the instance (Flesh is a drop quest so your mileage may vary).
