The key to doing that in a 5 man is to only pull the first one, and pull it to the very back. Then when an add wanders in you let it run to the back and then shackle it. Kill the add after the first one is done. After you kill the add you rest for mana. You always let them wander in on their own in a 5 man, unless you are very comfortable about pulling. Every one of the abominations will wander in on it's own, so you only need to pull the first one. Always stay at the back of entryway by the gate. This way when you kill the last Abom and Rammstien comes out (his aggro range is huge), you have enough time to let the casters regain mana before he charges the group. 

After Rammstien dies (try to remain back in the entryway still) the army of non-elite undead come after the group, AoE them, using any way you can to make them all stay in one spot. Warriors have Challenging Shout, Tauren have War Stomp, and Mages have that Frost Nova. Just make them all stay still for the AoE and you'll be fine. 

As soon as those guys die the REAL hard part comes. If you've never fought the 5 elite guards in a 5 man group before, then this will be very difficult. The key is to hold off on AoE until the tank establishes aggro on all the guards. Once the tank has the aggro under control you can AoE to your heart's content. A good idea is for the Mage to do the Frost Nova followed by Arcan Explosion until he's out of mana. 

Thus ends the Slaughterhouse Courtyard fun.

Performing the quest Above and Beyond in conjunction with 5 manning Riverdare will result in the 60th level questgiver with high dps and moderate hitpoints appearing to help you kill the baron.

The medallion of faith can be picked up in a raid group during a live side strat run beforehand. The questgiver for above and beyond is found in the chapel near the dead side entrance.

Just did it today, alliance side:

Group: All 60s -- Mage, Priest, Warrior, Paladin and Rogue

Baron startegy: Everybody is armed with a shadow protection potion and have one mana/health pot ready.

Paladin: Cocentration aura up to make sure priest/paladin heals don't get broken with constant damage. Job is to heal MT(Main Tank) and attack baron

Rogue: Unload as much damage as possible to baron

Mage: CC (crowd control) skeletons, make sure they all bunch up together so you don't waste mana also put dampen magic (improved) on everybody. Weakens the damage even more.

Priest: Shadow Protection buff and main healer. Keeps maintank alive

Warrior: Uses sunder and keeps aggro on him. Main tank.

Important part is to let the warrior build up aggro. Don't all attack at the same time. Wait for a few secs for baron to cocentrate on MT and then start fighting. 

Best of luck.

After reading all these comments, I was really worried about trying Baron in a five-man. We managed to take him down first try tonight, though, with the following group:

55 Priest (Holy/Disc)
60 Priest (Shadow)
60 Paladin
60 Mage (Frost)
60 Warrior (31/5/15 spec)

Yeah, I didn't think it was going to work either, but luck was on our side!

Burned 5 Shadow Protection potions, 5 Mana pots, and 2 Combat Healing Potions between us.

A good piece of advice for warriors, and part of the reason we won, is this: Keep your sword and 1-hander on for maybe the first half of the fight, while you keep aggro on you. After that, switch to a 2-hander, use Recklessness, and DPS him down in Battle Stance. 

Hope the advice helps!

This quest now rewards 1,000 Argent Dawn reputation, not the listed 350.  This quest alone, that is.  I'm not including the follow-up.

6 Corrupter's Scourgestones = 900 rep
10+ Invader's Scourgestones (avoiding most trash) = 150 rep
Rivendare kill within timer = 400 rep
Quest chain completion = 2500 rep
Miscellaneous trash rep = 50 rep
= 4,000 Argent Dawn reputation

There. No way to miss it. Enjoy!

OK here is what to do:

Target ghost, use zapper on them, it aggros them but they die after about 10 secs. Then 1-4 (I had 4 at least twice) "Restless souls" appear. You target one, use zapper again and again after 10 seconds they say "thanks to egan" "rivendare must die" etc and become "freed souls" repeat x15 and you do quest.

It was slightly bugged for me and stuck on 14/15 but when I logged out/in it was completed.

For those of you who, like me, prefer to make life easy for yourself, try this macro.

#showtooltip
/tar ghostly
/tar spectral
/tar restless
/use Egan's Blaster

Wakes doing the quest as easy as a single click.  Enjoy!

Some additional information: 

You can stand (at 59, anyhow) right near the entrance inside of the Live side, and not get aggro from the first pull ofr level 55-56 skeletons. If you look forward, you can see where the wall for the gates stop and the hallway begins. This is where you want to be. Be careful about running too far ahead, because the gates for the entrance close down behind you, and the only way out is hearthing (or dying). 

Be careful, because if you don't tag the mob immediately with the blaster when they're in range, they might walk out of range before the 2.5 seconds of channeling that's required elapses. You can stop some of them with /dance, but(!) they will not allow you to tag them with the blaster, while they're dancing, so it's kind of pointless. 

The mob will run at you, and maybe get in a hit before it "explodes" into often one, but I've gotten up to four, wisps that are Restless Spirits. 

These spirits will flicker around pretty wildly, and you have to tag them again with the blaster to get credit. The channeling effect will make it so that you will always be pointing at the spirit, so you don't have to manually try to keep it in front of you. 

Timing from my chat log, the Spectral Citizens show up roughly 8-9 minutes apart, so assuming you only get one wisp per pull, that's 2 hours of sitting at the entrance. I managed to get all mine in just over an hour, though (one pull had 3, another had 4 wisps).

Stealth does not work with the elite undeads, so just skip that idea. /Target Spectral and /Target Ghostly may help. Stand in the middle of the "T", out of aggro range of the first pack. Some ghosts go back into town, some go to the right, but every now and then, a ghost will walk through the tunnel, through that mob pack towards you. Be sure you already have the blaster equipped in the ranged slot, or you'll miss the first ghost (happened to me). By and by, you'll eventually free enough spirits (between 1 and 4 wisps will spawn). The deeds are scattered around scholomance. The deed to South Shore is in the first room of the instance on a desk. The deed to taurren mill is on a table, right before the whelp room, to the right. 1. Clear the dungeon
2. Ask one of the party member to invite your alt
3. Collect the deeds

I just solod this quest as a 70 resto druid, it can be done easily by any class, especially stealthers.

Through some trial and error, I found out you can be within about 5 yards of the mobs in this instance without aggroing.

I could open all the Iron doors without aggroing the guards near them.

The first deed: stand in the very corner behind the 2 guards and open it, no aggro.

Stealth through the next few rooms. Second deed: stand in front of the Iron Door right next to the deed, as far as possible from the mobs next to it. As long as the pat is moving away, you have plenty of time to unstealth, open the deed, and restealth.

Now you have to kill Rattlegore. Go down to the whelp room, drop into a hole, kill enough adds to clear to the boss. Adds have like 15k HP, boss has 30k. Loot the key, go back upstairs and through the other way (watch out for the disease cloud mobs).

If you stand along the wall of the locked door, in between the pulls, you can just barely reach the door and unlock it and continue.

3rd deed is cake compared to what you did before, just stealth when you enter Ras's room, walk over to the sparkles and loot.

Go back to the student room, go the other way. When you get to the final area, go down the stairs and straight forward.

4th deed: Watch out for the Unholy Aura of Alexi Barov, it will damage you if it doesn't resist, which is about once every 3 pulses. Approach along the wall so you don't aggro the Risen Warriors.

He has a [i]lot[/i] of HP, and will take awhile to bring down.  Of course, you want to kill him as fast as possible before the Alliance comes.

The first time, we weren't taking him seriously, and we wiped at 54%.

The second time, I pulled out my mechanicial greench and a mongoose potion.  I gave my tank an elixir of giants, a gift of Arthas, and an elixir of superior defense.  That got the job done...barely.  The priest healed continuously.  The tank went down at the same time the mob did.  The priest rezzed the warrior, we collected the head, and got our flagged butts out of there.

The trinket has a 10-minute cooldown.  You'd probably do well to swap it in and use it whenever the cooldown is up.  The summonables also have a really far aggro range and attack on their own, so be careful when you pop this that you don't anger mobs you'd rather leave alone.

The prerequisite is to collect all the deeds in Scholomance.  Really.  The other message is wrong.  That's a different quest chain.

Also, there's no doubt that the quest-giver is fratricidal, evil, and greedy.  I felt really dirty after I turned this one in.

Weldon Barov is also an easy solo kill for hunters, especially after 2.0 patch.

All the hunter needs to do is wait for the area to clear of alliance, then pull him with Arcane, followed by Serpent and Concussive shot. Sic your pet onto Weldon then just kite him around, drop traps if you wish, not needed but may help add a little advantage, especially if you are entrapment spec'd. Just run around and jump shot concussive, stop for a second to shoot a round or two, then run again. Be sure to keep Cheetah on the whole fight, unless he gets into melee range, then switch to monkey, hit him with a wing clip, and get back to range as quickly as possible. Feign Death if needed, your pet can always be rezzed.

The best place I found to kite him is down by the river, as alliance do not typically travel there and there are no mobs there that will aggro unless you are basically standing ontop of them.

Good luck and have fun!

He can be taken by two mages using the following strategy.

First mage will gain aggro using a high DPS spell, such pyroblast or Arcane Missles. At the same time the second mage will hit him with frostbolt to slow him.

We were able to stealth all three missions in this quest chain, multiple times, with various combos of rogues and druids. Here are some tips if you want to try stealthing it. Some of these comments were mentioned above as well.

[b]Group[/b]
Both four rogues and one druid, or three rogues and two druids works well. I personally prefer 4 and 1 and then the druid focuses on healing. The extra druid does not add much since the bear can't hold aggro and therefore it is better to have a 4th DPS rather than a second healer. You can get away with 58 rogues if they have talent points for master of deception. I think it's best to have 60 druids since they are spotted far more often.

[b]Preparation[/b]
To save time, make sure everyone knows to bring lots of heals, bandages, and the druids need mana type pots etc. You will burn through a lot of them and it sucks to get half way and run out of supplies. Usually a few people get to the instance early...get the early rogues to open the four doors that lead to Rattlegore. This saves a lot of time once everyone arrives. Unlock, Vanish, Prep, repeat or die and repeat. Opening the first four doors is not hard, expecially if the people don't mind dying. We found that it saved the most time to meet back at the bridge on the start and clear the four guards...the druids get seen by them too often and it helps to have them removed when getting through the locked door.

[b]Rattlegore[/b]
Get to rattlegore stealthed and have one rogue do the pulling

Some little fun and odd facts:

"Kirtonos the Herald is an undead level 60 elite who can transform into a gargoyle."

"Long ago, he became the master of Scholomance's Doctor Theolen Krastinov. Responsible for many of the atrocities during Krastinov's rule over Scholomance, Kirtonos fed on the blood of his innocent victims. To appease his master, Doctor Krastinov had to provide the gargoyle with more and more blood."

"In later days, Kirtonos was a rare visitor to Scholomance. The Blood of Innocents was not easy to obtain around Caer Darrow now that most of its inhabitants were dead. Only the ghosts remained, plotting the gargoyle's demise."

"Given his title, and the person who founded Scholomance, Kirtonos is probably the herald of Kel'Thuzad."

"On the way to the Stratholme Live side, after clearing the gate trap, you will see a sign in front of you at the fork in the road. This sign reads [b]Kirtonos Bros. Funeral Parlor[/b]. It is speculated that Kirtonos once lived in Stratholme before the war. How or if this is connected to his vampirism is unclear. Although, if he has always been a gargoyle, it probably is not connected to him." 

I thought the last bit (bolded) was interesting because I ran past the sign and couldn't find any lore behind the shop on google, other than this npc. All facts were taken from wowwiki here: [url=http://www.wowwiki.com/Kirtonos_the_Herald]http://www.wowwiki.com/Kirtonos_the_Herald[/url]

Soloed as 31-1/2 hunter (levelled mid-way through the quest).  As previous poster said, trick with with shield guard is to stop meleeing while their red shield is up.  As a hunter, you can keep shooting at them though, just put your pet on Stay while the shield is up.  With this strategy, I was able to take two on at a time.

The last NPC for quest was level 35.  The mob guarding was harder than the quest NPC (fortunately, the quest NPCs are not auto-aggro).  The guarding mob was a spellcaster that would sheep me.  If you're a hunter, keep your pet healed so that they can keep the attack on while sheeped.

The three quest NPCs will run earlier than most mobs (i.e., they have more health than usual when they decide to run away).  This can be a pain if they run and bring friends, so have a strategy in mind to keep them running too far.
Mobs are in "Lordamere Internment Camp" area which is directly north of Hillsbrad Fields.  Kill the yellow con mobs that are in the camp and the three story house beside it.

Not easy to solo under level 34, due to the last NPC mob. First of, what the #$@% is up with the stupid wall hack the caster mobs have? As you go into the building with the mage, the casters will keep sending ghosts at you. While attacking you, they are behind a wall and cannot be seen or counterattacked. Someone tell Blizz this is seriously messed up. You have to move all the way into the far corner of the building to draw them close enough to attack.
The mage is upstairs. When you go upstairs, you will be bumrushed by a 35/36 mage and two or three 33/34 mobs. The mage also has a polymorph (sheep) attack, if you are a hunter or a warlock she can sheep you while the mobs are killing your pet. Not fun to solo. With a group would be no sweat.

The first three undeads are in the area of the building enclosed with a big fence.  One is outside the building(mages and warriors patrol) and two are inside the building.  Those were easier to kill, but the last one was tricky.  I was able to do it on my second try though as a 31 shaman.  The last mob is upstairs of the second story building on the other side of the fence.  you have to fight your way through a couple of mobs but you should see a door on the opposite side of the room.  There are two more guys in the room when you go through the door and you can see some stairs.  after you kill those guys go up the stairs where there is one warrior, and a 36 mage  Warden.  I was able to kill here fairly easy as a shammy. just put down a searing totem and earth shocked her whenever she was trying to cast a spell.  I also used my Stomp(lol love druids!) Repeated that until i killed her.  Then regained mana and health, then just killed the last undead guy and got the jewel thing.

Did this last night as lvl34 (affliction) Warlock. Quite easy really. Pick off the wandering guards first, slip into first compound take them on 1 at a time if poss, use your succubus to seduce any adds. One Undead (yellow tagged) in the yard to the right. Two more in the hut in front of you. The last undead is in the second hut outside the stockade on the 2nd floor. When you get to the last room pull the guard from downstairs, kill them. Then Seduce the lvl 35 undead while you kill the lvl36 mage. Fight your way out....

Forget the guards for the stone token quest, for much easier drops kill the mages and workers.  They are west and a little north of the camp, closer to the purple shield.  (loc 13,78 ish)

The mages drop easy, and so do the workers.

That said, the guards ARE fairly easy if you stop meleeing them when they pop their shield up (which only lasts 4 seconds or so anyways).

Solo'd as a 30 Orc Rogue. Specs are in mostly in subtlety. It was challenging. First kill the 3 undead in the camp. They are simple, just be aware that lower lvl players (me) easily grab aggro of PAT's. 
  Then I used stealth and snuck my way to the next building where the last undead is at (lvl 35). He is on the top story and is guarded by 2 lvl 32's and a lvl 36 caster. As a rogue just kill the 2 NPC's on the lower floor and wait for your Vanish to be off of CD. While stealthed walk half way up the stairs and SAP one lvl 32, then use distraction to get the other lvl 32 to get in position where Ambush can be used. Try to kill this NPC fast!, then bandage and kill the other sap'd lvl 32. You more than likley will aggro the lvl 36 caster at this time. just hurry to burn the lvl 32 and then use vanish. Take a moment to get ready and then burn down caster. After that you can kill the undead and go turn in.

This is a horrible, horrible quest. Tried as a level 32 Blood Elf mage, and this was a yellow quest for me. While the Wedge, Marble, and Shard were easy to get, I found the Bloodstone Oval impossible to get to. I tried everything except bringing a group in. The level 36 mob is highly resistant to Counterspell, although I was able to polymorph her, but I could not bring Kegan down enough to survive the the Warden's fireball assault after the Polymorph expired. Her Fireball, by the way, averaged about 180 damage for me, which was more then 1/8 of my hit points. And, as others have stated, the corpse run for the Horde is terrible, and that combined with the quick respawn times for the mobs in the area makes this quest one of the most frustrating and badly designed I've encountered so far. I'll wait to continue the quest until I'm level 34 or higher.

I tried soloing this as a 33 Druid.  I worked on it at least couple hours.  The 12 Slaves were easy as you can pull them singly.  The Summoners, on the other hand are quite difficult.  They seem to have at least two together, or two other guards with them.  You might have to walk around the dome a bit, but you need to find a ruin where just one is pacing.  Patience is the key.  Pull any slaves or guards away first and kill them.  I found they just about always leave an opening for you to pull them in 1's or if you get too close sometimes 2's.  If at any time you see two casters throwing at you, time to run for cover and try again.  Once the guards and slaves are dispatched, you then need to rush the Summoner.  He has lots of tools in ranged combat, but is relatively easy to kill up close.

Obviously a group makes this whole process much much easier, but sometimes one isn't available.  

Good luck, and I hope you don't die as much as I did  :*)

The provided item (https://www.wowhead.com/forever/item=13752) is a 10-second targeted channel on Ras.  The range is only about 30 yards, so you have to get lucky or have some way of avoiding his fears and knockbacks.  If you're healing or tanking the run, make sure you have someone who can help tank/heal while you turn him human.

Okay First: this is the [u]Alliance[/u] quest chain for the key to Scholomance. Second: The lvl requirements are as listed on the net, so dont cry if you cant do solo them at this lvl or brag cause you could early. Third: This info is from various sites on the net, if you have info that counters this pls post it so that people are informed. Thanks.
That being said the quest chain is as follows:

A Call to Arms: The Plaguelands - Obtained from any of the criers in IF, SW, or Darn. This quest will take you to Chillwind Camp in Western Plaguelands and have you speak to Commander Ashlam Valorfist. (lvl 50 quest obtained at lvl 50)

Clear The Way - Chillwind Camp, Western Plaguelands
Starting NPC: Commander Ashlam Valorfist. This quest will have you Kill 10 Skeletal Flayers and 10 Slavering Ghouls in Sorrow Hill. Sorrow Hill is a graveyard just northeast of Chillwind Camp. Proceed there and kill the required number of ghouls and skellies and return to Commander Valorfist for your reward. (lvl 52/ obtained lvl 50)

All Along the Watchtowers - Chillwind Camp, Western Plaguelands Starting NPC: Commander Ashlam Valorfist. Using the Beacon Torch, mark each tower in Andorhal; you will need to stand in the doorway of the tower to successfully mark it. Commander Valorfist will provide you with the beacon torch to light the doorways with. Proceed to Andorhal, a ghost town northwest of Chillwind Camp and find the four towers. *NOTE* Unless the gods of warcraft love you there will be an elit

Since there is absolutely no information about this Item, I'll explain how to aquire the key.

You talk to [url=/npc=11056]Alchemist Arbington[/url] and get [url=/quest=5537]Quest: Skeletal Fragments[/url].
Go to Andorhal and kill any skeletons to get the fragments. Ghouls and abominations do not drop them.
Collect 15 and return to Alchemist Arbington, Turn in the fragments and pick up [url=/quest=5538]Quest: Mold Rhymes With...[/url].  Take the Imbued Skeletal Fragments, 15 Gold and 2 Thorium Bars to Gadgetzan and talk to [url=/npc=5411]Krinkle Goodsteel[/url]. This goblin does not take the Thorium bars from you; you really just brought them for the next part. Goodsteel gives you an Skeleton Key Mold and tells you to take it to Fire Plum Ridge along with 2 Thorium Bars to create an Unfinished Skeleton Key in the quest [url=/quest=5801]Quest: Fire Plume Forged[/url]. Go to the top of Fire Plume Ridge where there is Lava, it's right next to [url=/npc=9376]Blazerunner[/url]. You have to get pretty up close and personal to the lava but don't fall in, okay? Now you have the Unfinished Skeleton Key and you must take it back to Alchemist Arbington in Chillwind.  He then tells you that you need to kill [url=/npc=1852]Araj the Summoner[/url] in Andorhal.  This is great to do in conjunction with [url=http://wow.allakhaam.com/db/quest.html?wquest=211]Quest: Alas, Andorhal[/url].  Araj is pretty squishie, but don't underestimate him. He has about 5 adds. For this quest you kill loads of skeletons in the plaguelands they may drop Skeletal fragments. 
Onvce you have 15 take them back to him he makes a magic pile of bones.

Goto Gadgetzen and talk with the goblin by the thorium brother-hood nightelf who is blacksmithing.

The easiest way to kill Jandice, Mage decurse, warrior tank in battle stance and thunder clap adds, and everyone else dps/stun jandice.  The easiest way to target her is to just hit V on your keyboard so the health bar will appear above the mobs heads.  In doing so, when she reappears, she is the only one with health over her head.

During the fight with Jandice, she will spawn a large number of clones that do not take damage. A few useful tips:

1) Use the "V target" interface option so that nameplates show up above enemy NPCs. When Jandice clones, only her true form will have the name plate. DPS should target that instance.

2) Have a tank to an AoE taunt like demoralizing shout. Make sure not to AoE the clones, because once the tank loses aggro on a large number of them, it's going to be difficult to get them all off of whatever person aggroed them.

If you bring a hunter this is the time to use his/hers pet. It will not loose focus on the real Jandice.
Hit pets target and you shoot on the right one.

main.body:
I want to provide some useful information to people who are grinding these keys.   

Here are some points that will help you right away:

[u]Ogres: To Kill or Not To Kill[/u]
[ul]
[li]Keys drop at ~13-14% from the three guards, the bushwacker, and the captain.  If  you kill all 5 of these, and only these 5, you have a 50-53% chance of getting at least 1 key per run.[/li]
[li]There are certain groups of ogres that are directly on the path.  Count: 1 at the start, 5 after the first guard, 2 after the second guard and before the door, 4 down the corridor, 2 after the third guard, 2 near the tannin and 7 on the way to the captain.  This is 23 total ogres.[/li]
[li]The chance of getting at least one key from 23 ogres at 3% drop chance is ~50%.[/li]
[li]Therefore your chance of *not* getting at least one key per run halves if you kill the 23 ogres directly on your path to the guards and captian.[/li]
[/ul]

[u]How fast should I be going[/u]
[ul]
[li]You have at most 5 instances open per 60 minutes.  This means you must average 12 minutes per run to maximize the number runs per hour.[/li]
[li]As a level 80 arcane mage, using Blink as much as I can, and cooldowns on the guards, I can do 1 run, from the zone in, to the captain, out of the zone in, reset, and back in, rebuffed, and full hp/mana in ~10-11 minutes [u]if I kill only 7 ogres[/u].  [/li]
[li]Killing the extra 16 ogre puts me closer to 15 minutes, but brings the chance of a key drop up from 60% to 75%, which

This is a terrible attempt at a walkthru by me.  I'm doing it because I couldn't find any information about the quest anywhere.  So please forgive the massive inaccuracies.

1. Enter Dire Maul from the Feralas road, go up the ramp, past the patrolling dogs.  Kill the ogres along the way to the T-junction.  Turn left then Right thru the small doorway which takes you to a large open area columned area.

2. Head thru the large area, again killing dog patrols and ogres heading right to the Eastern Instance and enter.

3. Once inside it's easy to avoid the patrol from the right by hugging the wall the left.  Follow it around a short way to where the floor drops to the area below.  Take care when jumping down - about 1500 health loss and the possibility of a plant guard down there. Time it for when he's not there then fight him when he gets back.

4. The door you need to go thru is just ahead but it won't open till you talk to the big tree-man in the middle of the room.  You can't talk to him until you've killed a satyr.  Hugging the wall will avoid having to fight.  Follow the wall anti-clockwise to a pink stone doorway with a stealthed patrolling satyr.

5. Go thru the doorway, again hugging the right wall past satyrs and plants you won't have to fight, to a large swimming pool containing a Hydrosphere - water elemental.  This guy is very tough so get ready.

6. When he is dead go across the pool and you will see a pink passageway on each of the oposite walls, one leading up and

The village is populated by Tortured Druids (lvl 54-55) and Tortured Sentinels (lvl 56-57).  These guys are all single pulls and don't have any special attacks. This one's not hard.

1. Approach from the south, riding your mount.  You can ride through the gap between the 2nd and 3rd sentries (counting from right to left) without drawing aggro.  

2. The broken stone is slanted so you can ride right up to just below the balcony.  Ride up onto the rocks just east of the building.  

3. Jump your mount onto the ledge around the building.  You will auto-dismount. 

4. Walk around the SE corner to aggro the Elf on the balcony.  She will jump the balcony to engage you.  Kill her and jump onto the balcony; you will not draw aggro.

5. Aggro the closest Elf inside the building, drawing him onto the balcony.  Kill him there.

6. Walk into the building and immediately turn left; loot the box that is there.

Hearth out and return to Moonglade to turn in the quest.

Ok so here is how you get to the plague hatchings.  

First you must have the Skeleton Key to enter Scholomance.  If you don't you need to do the quests to obtain that.

I'm sitting here thinking, 15 gold is a steep quest requirement.  Has anyone finished the rest of the steps?  What is the reward?  Is it better than 15 gold?

Unless you are an obsessed WoW freak (having no time to farm some stuff to sell or make stuff to sell), 15 gold at level 60 is nothing.

It seems like a lot after levelling up your first character to 60, but once you realize you can go just about anywhere, including soloing instances that used to kick your a$$, it's just a matter of finding profitable stuff to farm/make/sell.

For instance, I made 70 gold in 6 days leveling up my cooking skill and selling the stuff I made to level up.  (I never levelled my cooking because I didn't need it as a Druid)  That's 6 days at 2-3 hours/day, by the way, not 16 hours a day like some people.

That's cooking -- mid to high-level food goes for 1-3 gold per stack of 10-20.  The leatherworking cash cows (at least on Llane server) are rugged armor kits and heavy leather.  I can farm about 30 rugged armor kits in a 2-3 hour night, and they go for 1.0-1.5 gold each at AH.  Don't ask me why, but stacks of 10 heavy leather sell for 1 gold each (more than thick leather), which is ridiculously easy to farm in Stranglethorn.

So, I could easily farm 30 gold per night, but straight farming is boring, so just mix and match.

As a nice side bonus, the Devourers that have the higher drop rate for the slabs of meat you need, also drop [url=/item=18512]Larval Acid[/url]... the higher level devourers will often drop 2 slabs at a time and  during this quest I picked up 3 Larval Acid -- they don't sell as well now, but for those who do make the [url=/item=18510]Hide of the Wild[/url] (lots of farming for the mats, and better cloaks do drop in outland, but not until a decent bit in; if you want a nice healer cloak, and get the larval acids and have the other materials on hand, it's not a bad item to have for a dedicated healer spec or for a healing kit on non-resto druid, shadow priest, pally or shaman.

Carrion Devourer drops Larval Acid twice as often as the Grubs - Devourers are found in EPL, Grubs are in both EPL and WPL -- and the slabs of Carrion Grubbage meat for the quest, also drop far more often on the Devourers. forever.body: Varimathis in the Undercity starts this quest.

Okay.  If you're in the UnderCity, navigate your way to the Apothecarium.  There is a long path leading down in a long spiral.  There will be 2 level 60 elite Deathguards on each side of the walls all down the path.  This is a good tip you're on the right path.

Once you get down, locate Varimathras (he's a big purple dude w/ big wings).  Get the quest from him.

Leave the UnderCity and go to the Zeppelin Tower.  Take the Zeppelin to Orgrimmar.

Once you've made it to Orgrimmar, enter the city and locate the Cleft of Shadows.  Once you've entered the Cleft of Shadows, you will be headed down a wooden ramp.  But if you notice at the very top of the ramp, the railing has a space between it and nothing.  Jump through the space to the left from the top of the ramp.  Then turn around and you should see the "portal" to the instance.

Once you've entered the instance (this quest is preferably done in a group of 3 or more since every NPC is elite), carefully fight your way through RFC (Ragefire Chasm).  You'll eventually kill the right people, and pick up what you need.

Now just go back to the zeppelin, back to the UnderCity, back to the Apothecarium, back to the Royal Quarter, find the path that lead you to Varimathras, go to Varimathras and turn it in.  I got 1450 XP, some money, and some gifts.  Cool mission but really difficult if you're  not careful.

DO NOT GET COCKY IN RFC!  Those elites will beat you

Dont, believe the hackxor thottbot, this both starts and ends at varimathras, found in Undercity. There is a path in the apothecarium that leads right to him(notice the bunch of elites on the way).

Now that you have the quest. head to RFC, the instance in Orgrimmar.(cleft of shadow to be more precise)fight your way through the troggs, earthborers, and elementals.
Now youll get to a big area filled with searing blade cultists. The books drops random off one of these. 

When you have the books, get to varimathras again for some exp and nice rewards

With a Tauren Druid bringing the TB quests, and an Undead rogue bringing the Undercity quest, two hunters and a warrior, ranging in levels from 11 (me) to 17 (warrior), we cleared the instance in one run, and finished all quests. The books dropped from consecutive cultist mobs in the camps to the left of the main ramp down on the ramp leading up to the Satyr boss. 

The really fun part was, only the rogue and I knew what we were doing. Thankfully, our tank offered to start tanking (IE switch to Defensive stance and Taunt) after the first two wipes, and things went pretty smoothly after that. Of course, I died twice pulling mobs off our druid because the tank had a bad case of target fixation, but hey, that's what hunters are for, right? 

Anyhow, long story short (too late), yes, the books drop off any old cultist, although it seems to me that almost every time I've done this instance, it was cultists on the ramp up to the Satyr that dropped them. In fact, it 

has 
been every time.

forever.body: This quest can be started once you have completed all of Tirion Fordring's kill quests.

- Demon Dogs

Sit and listen to my story, undead.

>>[i]I am ready to hear your tale, Tirion.[/i]

I must apologize for not being entirely truthful with you in regards to my identity.  I had to be certain that you could be trusted - few people would have selflessly lent assistance to an old and forgotten hermit.

You have proven yourself as one of those people: A person of integrity and honor.

>>[i]Thank you, Tirion.  What of your identity?[/i]

My son, Taelan, was only a child when I was found guilty of treason and banished from the Alliance to live a life in exile.  I chose to remain here so that I could watch over him; to somehow insure that he would group up an honorable man.

As I had hoped, he took my place as lord of Mardenholde; but in a cruel twist of fate, joined the ranks of the Scarlet Crusade.  He is now their Highlord, undead.

>>[i]That is terrible.[/i]

Indeed.  The Scarlet Crusade are an aberration of the Order of the Silver Hand.

You must believe me, undead; Taelan is a good man.  He needs guidance.  He needs to remember... remember what it is to be noble and honorable.  I know that in his heart, he knows what he does is wrong.  Will you help him?  Will you help him remember?

>>[i]I will, Tirion.[/i]

forever.body: Be sure to lure him off the rock bridge before you go to fight him as he CAN throw you into the lava surrounding it, which spells instant death.  I tried this quest 3 times in 3 different groups, both the first 2 times we failed.  Our successful group consisted of 2 tauren shamans, 2 rogues, and a hunter.  With the exception of one of the shamans and one of the rogues who were nearing level 20, everyone in the party was below level 15.  Also, be sure to kill all of the surrounding searing/burning blade cultists before you pick your fight with him as they are all elites and any one of them could easily take on 2 level 15 or lower players.  Last but not least, do not attempt to go into RFC without a healer or 2 in your party unless you know of a way to deal massive amounts of damage without taking any yourself.  Have rogues in your party to recon the place before you turn blind corners, and do NOT have anyone just rush into groups or else everyone will probably die.  You need to pull the NPCs in here away from their groups and have your group take them on one at a time or else you won't make it out alive.

OK, this is extremely difficult to solo as a rogue, but I just did it as a 59 rogue.  I am combat spec with a 16.57% chance to crit (not sure if that will make sense once BC comes along, but anyway...) it took me a few tries to figure out how to do it... first thing is make sure you have major healing potion or two.

First click the mound of dirt next to the gravestone.  The mobs walk in instead of spawning right away so immediately stealth.  Next, if you wait for them to get to the grave they start to mill about, which makes it a bit hard to position yourself, so distract them before they get to the grave. Cheap shot Mercutio and immediately use evasion.  This should keep you alive for most of the fight.  once evasion wears off, blind one of the graverobbers to try and lessen the DPS intake.  Also watch out for your health as you'll need that health pot eventually...  I was close to dying so once mercutio fell I Vanished.  His body didn't disappear or anything, so I waited a few seconds for a bit of health to come back.  Once I had some health I looted the corpse real quick and sprinted away.

Hope this helps someone...

It *is* possible as a feral druid. (was 57 at the time)

My sequence (you should only attack Mercutio): Open grave. Back up so you don't aggro them right away. Cast Regrowth, followed by Rejuvenation. Switch to bear form. Faerie Fire, Demoralizing Roar then swich it up between Mangle and Maul. You can also use Frenzied Regeneration when it's warranted. When you're around 40-50%, cast Barkskin. Heal yourself with Healing Touch, then follow it up with Regrowth and Rejuvenation. (Use a healing potion if you need to, they *might* kill you before you get the first heal off) Switch back to Bear Form. Mangle/Maul until Mercutio's dead. Shift-click his body so you auto-loot, go into Travel Form, run away with his kid's little toy warhammer.

These mobs were never bugged. The game doesn't allow players to damage any mobs that can't fight back, like aggressive fishes in lakes or these weird things in the cave pool before Wailing Caverns.
This means that if the mob is aggroed, you need to either go away and wait for combat to be over or to put your toe in lava and kill it while taking this hot tub.
If mob is on your pet/summon, it should let you damage the mob as long as you don't overaggro it from your pet.
TL;DR: if mob can see but can't fight back, it will dodge 100% of your attacks, just like these mobs that were aggroed by someone's mount and are running back to their usual routes.

Confirmed. Just beat the crap out of him as a solo level 62 prot pallie. He is still elite as of 2.3, although the [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?item=12650]Attuned Dampener[/url] used to help kill him has been greatly upgraded. First off, make sure you do the prequest, [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?quest=4972]Counting Out Time[/url], before you fight him, in order to get the Attuned Dampener. Using that will make him much easier.

Second, make sure you come into Andorhal through Sorrow Hill and over the bridge. Clear the area of solo mobs, and watch out for the Flesh Reapers on patrol, they're elites. It's a good idea to kill any of those in the immediate area. 

Now start [i]carefully[/i] pulling mobs from around Araj. You can pull not only the first group in front of him, but also the 2 spectral ghosts behind them, and if you go around to the side, the scorching ghouls and skeletal warlords as well. It isn't difficult at all to completely clear the area around him.

After he's clear, stand about 10 yards away and use the Attuned Dampener. From there on, keep yourself healed and he's cake. Pallies should know what to drop on him. Consecration, Exorcism, etc. Keep a mana potion handy just in case.

At any rate, rumors of his difficulty are greatly exaggerated.

Aight, here's whatcha do.  The painting is in the Archivist's room, directly across from Balnazzar's room, and on the right wall as you walk in.  

If you're in a 5-man, simply hit it after the Archivist and his buddies go down, and you're done.  

In a raid, it's a bit more complicated.
1) Beat Balnazzar (duh), this causes Scourge mobs to spawn all throughout the bastion.  
2) There is one set of mobs between Balnazzar's room and the Archivist's room after Balnazzar dies, have your raid kill them.  If you're a rogue or a druid, who is level 60, you can skip this step and stealth past the mobs (more at step 3.5)  DISCLAIMER: With the patch and true sight added to numerous Stratholme mobs, you may not be able to stealth past, I advise doing it the main way to be safe.  
3) Ask to be given leadership over the raid, wait for everyone to leave the instance, and once everyone but yourself is out, let everyone leave and/or kick any stragglers.
3.5) *For druids and rogues only, others go to step 4* The mobs will probably detect you at any lower than 60 unless you have Nightscape Boots, Improved Prowl, MoD, etc.  If you pass them safely, and are lower than 60, you run the risk of aggroing them while you chip the painting.  To avoid this, position yourself as far away from the door as possible while still being able to hit the painting, as described in step 4.
4) Hit the painting, it chips it and reveals your other painting (although you do not need to loot the real painting).

In order to get this quest you must complete ALL of Tirion Fordring's quests at the cave in EPL.  After numerous kill quests and a trip to Live Strath you will go to hearthglen in disguise.  Only with this disguise buff can you speak to Highlord Taelan Fordring and do this quest. 

You can keep your disguise on for a long time.  No need to remove it when he says.  The quest is very easy while you are in hearthglen, just let him kill everything and try not to get aggro from the elites.  

Once you get outside you will be attacked by 5 lvl 60 elites.  He can kill them all on his own if you let him.  You will not fail for dying at this stage if you can get rezzed immediately to catch up with the Highlord.

The last part is kinda rough.  The highlord will take you to the tower where everyone farms for Crusader enchants and yell for the Inquisitor to come out.  Do not attack them...it will take a little bit but eventually the Highlord will engage.  He will handle the main guy and he tells you to "deal with the crimson elites".  Doing this with just myself and a shaman proved to be fairly difficult.  There are only two guards with him but a group of 5 comes down the path and engages as well.  

I am not sure if these auto aggro you, or if you can let them aggro the highlord as well.  When i did it we got aggro and it was a mess.  The shaman ended up dying and even with a combat rez right away he failed the quest.

The highlord basically ends up getting owned and Tirion Fordring (th
Best is to let Highlord Taelan tackle them to death so do not terminate the disguise and watch from a distance until big daddy Fordring arrives to spank everybody.

Don't help Taelan fight.  Stay in your disguise so you don't aggro any of the guys fighting him.  He's good enough on his own, even against four level 60 Elites.  I thought for sure he was going to die against them but when his health was at 10% or so, it suddenly filled up again all the way.  Apparently the quest insists that he doesn't die until later.

He gets killed in front of the tower east of Hearthglen.  Forget about helping him--his death is inevitable.  Stay in your disguise if you can, and stay far enough away so as not to aggravate the level 63 Elite priest that helps take Taelan out... this is the only member of the Scarlet Crusade that you can aggro throughout the whole quest, assuming you're still disguised.  

When he dies, wait a minute.  His father will ride up to the tower and have words with the level 63 Elite that killed him.  Tirion proceeds to obliterate the priest.  If you haven't gotten it yet, you [i]still don't fight or try to help out[/i].  In fact, don't help Taelan or Tirion at all in this quest.  Just sit back and watch.  It's that easy, especially if you stay disguised.  Taelan will tell you to take your disguise off when he starts to leave his keep, but ignore that.  

After Tirion is done cracking skulls, he'll stay put in front of the tower, and after a long tangent about him and his son and his terrible regrets and mistakes, he'll be ready to reward you.

Okay guys, so I'm here to share my experience with this quest and to tell my tale of sorrow and perhaps caution. As of this moment, 22.11.2019 evening, I've had around 8 or 9 tries with this quest and I've yet to complete it. I might even go on and claim, that I know pretty much everything you can know about this quest and the mechanics right now.
So first of all SPOILERS AHEAD.
As all of you have probably read by now, you can't mine or pick herbs with the disguise. So just don't do it, even though Hearthglen has those really appealing Rich Thoriums sometimes.
So when you finally get your disguise and ride up to hearthglen just head to the big castle like building in the back and go to the 2nd floor. Assuming nobody else is doing the quest at that moment (if you ran into an unnaturally tall big dude going apedung on scarlet NPC:s with 0,9sec attack speed 2-h sword - somebody else is doing the quest) you walk up to Taelan and turn in the prequest. Now the part that never gets mentioned is that when you turn in Scarlet subterfuge, Taelan enrages, which actually gives him a long lasting buff. He then kills the guards in the room and offers you the next part, this very quest "In Dreams". On we go, accept and follow him. Don't remove the disguise when he tells you, makes your life easier. If you did it anyway by accident or it wore off, then just stay behind Taelan and try not to aggro anything extra. 

He will exit the main building, then saddle up proceed to slaughter every scar

Ok how to do this quest [i]solo[/i]. 
I tried a few times and [i]this [/i]method worked for me.

Escort the guy like normal while [u]keeping your disguise on[/u]. 

He will kill everything in his path, no need to help yet.

Outside the main large gate an Elite pack will attack him. These [u]will[/u] likely kill him. So drop your disguise when he is at about 75% health (so you know he has aggro) and help out. Fear works great and for me even reset his hp to full.

When he gets to the tower Elites from that tower will attack him, as well as Elites from the road you just came down. Help him out with those [i]and [/i]die trying.

[u]Die close to the front of the tower where the battle takes place[/u]. [b][u]DO NOT RELEASE[/u][/b].

Main villain dude [i]will [/i]kill your escort guy.

After a bit Tirion should come. It can take a long while. If you time out and auto spawn at graveyard it didn't work.

When Tirion arrives he will kill everyone, be upset and then your quest will show as "Completed", once he stops talking. 

You being there when Tirion finishes talking is likely the trigger for completion.

At this point I had 1 min left on release timer.

Release and run back. He will stay for 13 whole minutes (granted this could be tied to others starting the quest).

Talk to him and get your reward.

All you need to know:

1.  He will instruct you to remove your Scarlet Illusion.  Do not.  

2.  You do not need to help him in combat from where he starts until the gates of Hearthglen.  You can if you like, but it is not required.  I found that snaring mobs for him saved me lots of time and additional mobs since he is not the best at chasing down runners.

3.  At the gates of Hearthglen you may encouter a patrol of 4 level 60 elites.  If you do, Fordring will likely die and there is nothing you can do about it (if you are solo).  Once he gets a ways out of Hearthglen he becomes able to completely heal himself, so this same group of 4 level 60's is no problem.

4.  When he approaches the East Tower down the road from Hearthglen, go south off the road and up on to the hill - watch from there.  Do not get involved - you can not help and will only die.  Fordring will die, and a minute later his father will come up and kill all the scarlets and give you your reward.

-------

If fordring dies before the end, drop the quest and go back to the Hag at Uther's tomb.  She will give you another Illusion.  Took me 3 times to get it right.

If you somehow get agro in the final fight and die, do not release your corpse.  Wait until the father shows up and goes through his script, then release.  He will still be there when you rez and come back.

IF you've failed, there's no need to return to the hermit paladin for anything -- the gift that you give Taeron to initiate the quest first run doesn't need to be give twice.  Simply get the disguise from the hag gnome again, abandon the quest, and go talk to Taeron.  He will give you the escort quest once more, which you can complete normally.

This has got to be the most horrible quest line I've ever encountered. 
There's so many steps that require you to just run to a place and talk to a person, then return.
The last part has definitely got to be the worst. A stupid escort that requires a buff that only lasts 30 minutes to start, but it takes roughly 25-30 minutes for Taelen to re-spawn if another person already just started it. So there's a good chance your buff will run out before he does re-spawn. 
Taelen is very strong yes, but he can have weird issues getting to the end location and he holds very little threat so trying to help him kill mobs will probably just get you killed and you'll fail. Finally, the last part requires him and possibly you to die, this brings further issues with many different reports of the quest not given credit despite Tirion showing up and doing his thing. 
Ultimately, if not for the fact this quests just so happens gives Pre-Raid BiS for many classes, no one would ever do it, ever. The crooked hoops you have to jump through is far beyond even the jank charm that is Vanilla WoW.
Despite this being solo-able, if you're playing on a pvp server you better bring a group. Asshats will start a war over this quest and basically waste over an hour for everyone.

From the Bullwark in Tirisfal follow the road east through the Western Plaguelands. Follow the road all the way across the entire zone until you get to the bridge that crosses the Thandoril River. The Undercroft is a tomb-like structure about 30 yards off the road on your right hand side and it will have unfriendly troll mobs pacing around outside of it. If you happen to be a class that kills rather slowly, here's a little trick to do this easily...

Instead of immedietly looting the corpses of the monsters, kill a few but don't loot their corpses yet. The timer on the rot doesn't start until you pick it up. I managed to get 5 pieces of rot and barely start the 10 minute timer.

Also, the rot seems to drop from any creep at Corin's Crossing, they don't necessarily have to bef fleshy monsters to drop the rot. (i.e. Stitched Horror vs Wraith)

Hope those tips help.

Go to Corins Crossing and kill the Scourge. Nearly all the mobs outside the city drop the Living Rot.

The Living rot expires after 10 min, so the best way is to kill 5-7 monsters try to draw them to the same place and then loot the bodies all at the same time, as the timer does not start till after you pick up the living rot. This also means that you can look at the body, and loot everything but the living rot, so then you know which bodies and how much living rot you have.

Corin's Crossing 59.69
Kill any mobs there, they drop Living Rot randomly, get 7 of them, then click on your Mortar and Pestle in your inventory.
You'll receive Coagulate Blood.

Tips for soloing this quest:

Stay around the edges. The fastest kills are the gibbering ghouls and the stitched horrors. If you get a Hidden Servant, get outside the aggro range of town quick. If one of those "calls for help" inside the town limits, you're screwed.

Basically just keep killing until you have 7 of the things at once.. it took me about 40 kills to do this. The living rot does not drop on every kill, and I had to rest for mana about every 3 kills.

Book is guarded by two Quel'Lithien Protectors. They hit hard, they hit fast, they will attack from range, and they will interrupt your spells. In addition, the lodge and its surrounding area is packed very tightly with elves; inside the lodge there is a two-elf patrol that pats to the two protectors and the book.

A simple kite can tackle Duskwing.  Turn your pet's taunt off, tag him with an aimed shot, slap a serpent sting on him and high-tail it out of there.  Clear a path to the road, if you have to, or do what I did and wait until he passes near the Marris Stead.

Whichever way you do it, drag him to the road and make sure you keep a serpent sting on him whenever it wears off.  STAY AT THE EDGE OF YOUR BOW/GUN RANGE!  Don't let him get close to you, he's got a wicked attack that'll do 600-1200 damage, totally ruining your day.  

Use a conc shot if he gets too close for comfort and you shouldn't have any problems.  Just be sure to maintain the aggro on yourself - don't let your pet steal it.  A distracting shot now and then helps this along.

It took me halfway through WPL before he finally dropped, but it was a breeze.  Good hunting!

forever.body: They have changed the quest slightly you need to talk to Squire Rowe at the Stormwind Gate or Marshal Windsor will not show up.

If someone else is doing the Windsor quest that Squire Rowe starts, you'll get the following text from Rowe:

"Marshal Windsor has been expecting you, <name>. Unfortunately, he is currently indisposed. He should be returning shortly."

The wait time while Windsor's being escorted by another player to Stormwind Keep is approximately 10 minutes.

BTW, you don't need a raid for this quest, as the quest text would lead you to believe. Just escort Windsor to Stormwind Keep, where he will call upon Lady Prestor, turning her into her true form, Onyxia. This spawns eight dragonkin guards. You don't need to bother with them -- Highlord Bolivar Fodragon, a level ?? boss, can easily take them all out himself. You need to just stand there and watch. Windsor will die, then Bolivar will give you a new quest -- "The Dragon's Eye" -- for which you'll need to find the dragon Emberseer in Dustwallow Marsh. And that's all there is to it.

This quest is marked as a raid; however, it can easily be soloed if you desire and don't have the time to do it with a group of friends. Bolvar does all of the fighting, so just stand back away from him and the dragons. Take some bandages, a healthstone, or health potion just in case one of the dragons hits you. If you have a ranged attack you may use it to "tag" the kills and gain XP if you're not already 60. 

As a side note: Windsor is not attacked as you escort him to SW Keep.

It might help to use guild or SW City chat to [b]find out what state the Keep is in BEFORE accepting this quest.[/b] Make sure Lady Prestor is there (and human), the Highlord is at her side (and not in Attack Stance), and the boy-king is there with his usual blank stare.

When you go to find Marshal Windsor, also [b]make sure the General is there on horseback[/b], and there are NO kneeling guards to be seen.

Not sure whether it makes any difference, but you might also want to [b]ensure that ALL members of the group are actually on the quest.[/b]

I'm guessing that if this is the case, you should be able to complete the quest without a hitch.

BACKGROUND
After having Ony freeze as a dragon (and her guards freeze as SW guards) on our first attempt, we all abandonned this quest and met Marshal again. Half of us finished a few days ago on our second attempt. I just watched the other half FAIL the first time, but complete it on their THIRD try. Here's what happened for these last two runs:

We walked all the way through the city and arrived in the Keep, only to find that Lady Prestor was GONE, as were her guards, and the Highlord was standing around in his Battle Stance. Marshal had nobody to talk with... no dragon to conjure... and nothing changed for several minutes... so they were forced to abandon yet-again, and walk through town for their third time.

But this time I stayed in the Keep (I had completed the quest, so I was not in the group), and used guild chat to let the oth

This quest is a "moment". It's one of the greatest experiences in the game. I loved watching it as a lowbie. I loved dying, and I longed for the day when it would be my turn. 
The walk is so atmospheric, the guards are whispering about what a great honour this is. NPCs are awestruck. This is why you rolled Alliance. >YOU< are now involved in the affairs of Kings, Kingdoms and Dragons.

We make a guild event of this quest: Everyone is invited, Lowbies too. Everyone turns up in their finest dress gear: Not the best armour, but the stuff that looks coolest. Epic mounts: Novelty Pets: Evil Looking Weapons and Armour. Wear it all for the show.

Picking up other players just for the feeling of the march, and that *SOMETHING SPECIAL* is about to happen. The groups of lowbies who come along just to see it. This is a moment to treasure.

No, you don't have to join in the fight. But you *HAVE TO*. It's what is right.

On beginning the quest:

[b]Lady Katrana Prestor[/b] yells: Seize him! Seize the worthless criminal and his allies!

Windsor beings walking, and reaches Marcus Jonathan, who has formed a line with his guards to block Windsor.

[b]General Marcus Jonathan [/b]says: Reginald, you know that I cannot let you pass.
[b]Reginald Windsor [/b]says: You must do what you think is right, Marcus. We served together under Turalyon. He made us both the men that we are today. Did he err with me? Do you truly believe my intent is to cause harm to our alliance? Would I shame our heroes?
[b]Reginald Windsor[/b] says: Holding me here is not the right decision, Marcus.
[b]General Marcus Jonathan[/b] appears lost in contemplation.
[b]General Marcus Jonathan[/b] says: I am ashamed, old friend. I know not what I do anymore. It is not you that would dare bring shame to the heroes of legend - it is I. It is I and the rest of these corrupt politicians. They fill our lives with empty promises, unending lies.
[b]General Marcus Jonathan[/b] says: We shame our ancestors. We shame those lost to us... forgive me, Reginald.
[b]Reginald Windsor[/b] says: Dear friend, you honor them with your vigilant watch. You are steadfast in your allegiance. I do not doubt for a moment that you would not give as great a sacrifice for your people as any of the heroes you stand under.
[b]Reginald Windsor[/b] says: Now, it is time to bring her reign to and end, Marcus. Stand down, friend.

Hunters quick leason here on kiting. Which you will be asked to do here. Genreal Drakkisath has 2 mobs with him which are usually taken by the 2 warriors or whatever you have in the group. The big thing for you is getting the general as far away from the group as possible. What you need to do is put on aspect of the cheetah and get just in range of the general. 
   When everyone is ready it is really simple shoot drak and run like crazy to the beasts room. Drak should follow you and with aspect of the cheetah on he should not catch you.
   When you reach the beast room run him along the walls til he is in your range again. Once he is in your range again that means you are in his. Simply fiegn death and lose aggro. By now your group should be done with drak's mobs and ready for him. If not you can start the whole thing over as long as you are over the bridge. You might die the second time depended on how much cooldown you have left on fiegn death.
  One big thing to remember is that when entering the beasts room there is some fire. Make sure to JUMP over the fire or you will be dazed and probably die from the general.
   That is the jist of kiting Drak and I hope it helps. It isn't as hard as everyone thinks it is but for the most part it is needed.

Taken from my post about Malcin:

Malcin isn't exactly easy to find... more of a pain, but the quest rewards for killing him are decent (or vendor well).

He can be found in three different spots:
1. The first tent as you enter the RFD thistled area.
2. Take a right at the first fork you encounter, and you will see two tents. He's in between them, with about eight other mobs.
3. The final is past the second - follow the path to the next fork, and hang a left. He'll be at the end when you hit the wall. Worth noting is a rare spawn mob named Ambassador Bloodrage (https://www.wowhead.com/forever/npc=7895).

This is very good place to practice using Mind Control. The ambassador will spawn randomly, but always with one or two guards nearby. Well, last night I decided to try this quest.  Now, even though the mobs are outside RFD, there is no mention in my quest notes that it is an elite quest, just that it is a level 36 quest.  Make no mistake, though, you are gonna have to be GOOD to complete this at 36 solo.  I made my way all the way to the instance zone at first expecting to see him to the right of the zone.  Nope.  I eventually found him on the ledge overlooking 1K needles.  Basically, if you enter the RFD area via the Darkcloud Pinnacle route and then just stay right.  He was down a fork to the right, which also overlooked 1K Needles.  There was a hut he was standing outside of. He looked to be a robe-wearing undead.

He was surrounded by 3 or 4 friends (1 battleguard, a caster, and 1 or 2 regular warriors).  I was able to solo pull and kill one of them.  But could not get him solo.  Finally I developed this strategy which maybe borders on an exploit, but which I consider just good gameplay:

Stand near the ledge to 1K Needles and attack the Ambassador from range.  He will come running, as will his friends.  If you are lucky, he will start chain casting shadow magic on you.  Well, if you run all the way to the ledge (dont fall off) and then get as far from the mobs as possible, his friends will give up and return to their bind points, leaving the good ambassador standing there solo, still casting shadow magic on you.  He is a 36 Elite mob, but was pretty easy. I am a 36 shaman.  It took me a couple tries to
Cords: 48,91 area in tent of two tents in that area. 36 Elite

Kel'ris room must be cleared completely before you take him. Just let a hunter or warrior with range carefully pull 1 or 2 at a time (or more if your group can handle). Then you should be fine.. Just dispel the sleeped party members and he should be down pretty fast. We killed him verry easy and fast..

This boss is at the back of the instance, beyond all the cultist mobs.  He is...doing something (channelling?) at an altar in the middle of a large room.  You can fight around him, just don't get too close or he will 'wake up'.  Be sure to clear all the Twilight Hammer mobs from the room before you start.

Kelris is not that hard by himself.  His only real trick is to cast Sleep.  If you are doing this instance under-manned, that might cause problems.

Rumor has it that if you attempt to fight Kelris without first getting the Blessing of Blackfathom (from the Murloc altar earlier in the instance), he has the ability to mind control your character, thus making them activate the flames around his altar, which in turn summons waves of enemies.  I have not yet fought Kelris without the Blessing, however, so I can't confirm.

Once you beat Kelris, you can activate the flames at the four corners of the altar to open the way to the final area.  Each flame will summon monsters, so use one flame then clear out the enemies it summons.  Use the next flame and so on.  Don't use all four flames in quick succession or you'll be swarmed.

I highly recommend casters do this quest as early as they can, especially if you intend to do any wanding.  The wand you can get as a reward is as good a level 32-34 green wand.

Like the above said, the Blessing of Blackfathom or whatever it's called has nothing to do with the Kelris fight. He'll MC, but it's very rare. If it does happen, just dps Kelris down (the MC'd person can only melee). I belive it's also channeled, but I'll have to run BFD again to find out.

[i]What discoveries?[/i]

It would appear as if the influence of the Black Dragonflight had extended beyond the borders of the Burning Steppes and into the kingdom of Stormwind itself! The usurper has since been unmasked and ousted.

[i]Usurper?[/i]

Indeed. The brood mother of the Black Dragonflight had used illusion and trickery to disguise herself as [url=?npc=1749]a member of the royal court[/url]. Worse yet, she had assumed control of the current Highlord of Stormwind, [url=?npc=1748]Bolvar Fordragon[/url].

It is no wonder that such foolish military decisions had been made. The movement of Alliance forces as of late had left us scratching our heads. We now understand that the Black Flight was attempting to divide the empire - destroy it from within.

[i]With all due respect, Warchief - why not allow them to be destroyed? Does this not strengthen our position?[/i]

<Thrall laughs.>

So much to learn still, <race>.

You are too young to remember the wars and bloodshed of ages past. Too young to remember the burden of the curse carried by our people.

For our group (3 warriors, mage, and shaman), he was the toughest by far.   We killed Scryer and Chronalis in one try each, but Somnus took three.  You may want to have nature protection potions handy, and nature resist as well.  He also hits like a truck and has a knockback attack that throws you about 50 feet away and in the air.

He also has a circular path he takes through SoS, so pick an area where he goes, and after he passes, kill all the mobs in the area.  Lots of trash, either crocs, or elite dragonkin (level 43-45).  If you get knocked in to one of them, you have an add or two you don't need to deal with.

Axtroz is a dragon found in the wetlands (below Arathi Highlands).
Start walking on the eastward path from the center and you can't miss him.

There is a 75 non-elite on the boat, so if you're doing it on level, be careful. Otherwise just keep an eye out for alliance players who may not appreciate your presence.

A hopefully simple way to find Myriam Moonsinger:
start in Thousand Needles -- at The Great Lift, head southeast along the trail towards the Shimmering Flats.  At the beginning of the trail, before you get too far along towards the Flats, you will see stairs leading up.  These rope ladder stairs are also marked by a huge purple/blue-ish totem.

Take the stairs up, kill some Bloodtooth Guards (level 27-28 mob) along the way.  At the top, you will be on a plateau of sorts.  This network of ramps/rope ladder bridges/stairs is very large.  You want to go north towards the Barrens, working your way to the edge of Thousand Needles.  At the edge, turn right (east).  Once you see a Death's Head Cultist (level 33-34+ elite) with another guard (either Thornweaver or Battleguard level 33-34+ elite), you have arrived.

Myriam Moonsinger is north and a little east, once you get past the first five or so mob.  Look up on top of a hill, overlooking the mob on the eastern edge of Razorfen Downs.

Chain starts in Azshara at 79,73. 1st interaction with Duke Hydraxis will give you 2 quests:

main.body: The Fathom Core is actually under the water.  The water area I am talking about is the part where the path actually makes walls for you to walk inbetween bodies of water.

The Fathom core is found as a lootable item called Fathom Stone, so don't let that fool you. When Barn Aquanis spawns, kill him and you get a Strange Water Globe, which leads you to the quest, http://www.wowhead.com/?quest=6922 .

Since it's hard to find, here is a map. The instructions on wowhead were not exactly specific.
http://www.wowhead.com/?maps=719:522825

  I had to take my 70 to go find this, since I hadn't seen it as a group with my alt.

 It is indeed underwater. It doesn't shimmer like most other quest objectives, so keep an eye out. Under the walkway, in the water, where the dot on the map is.

  Once you loot it, a 24 elite elemental comes out.

Just a flavour note.

"Among the Ruins" is the first mission of the Zerg campaign in StarCraft.
This quest DOES count towards the [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?achievement=1680]Loremaster of Kalimdor Achievment[/url] (Horde).

It's not a 28 elite, it is a 24 elite. You need to loot him to get the  follow on quest as well as take the fathom core. This can be confusing as I am sure some people have just killed him and not picked up the quest. 
The fathom stone is not easy to find despite the excellent instructions from previous people. We had to get in the water and swim around to find it as couldn't see it from land.

The Fathom Core is found in the Moonshrine Ruins: this is the water room with stone hallways and pillars just before the sanctum, where Twilight Lord Kelris is located. If you look on your minimap, you will see a darker circle in the middle of the lighter grey areas designating the hallways and paths for this room. Jump in the water, swim under water to the dark circle location on your map to the Fathom Core - it is a cylindrical item, dark grey and doesn't sparkle as typical quest items do. It spawns a water elemental when looted.

This quest, as well as "The Essence of Aku'Mai" and "Blackfathom Villainy" (picked up inside the instance) count towards Loremaster of Kalimdor.

Don't be fooled by the map (and coords) on Wowhead and the clipping on your minimap. 

Continue south after the [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=4887]Ghamoo-ra[/url] and do a double right turn before [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=6243]Gelihast[/url]. The map will expand and you should come to [url=http://www.wowwiki.com/Moonshrine_Ruins]Moonshrine Ruins[/url] (ext. link). 

The stone is in the water to the right of the path going through the water. :)

Upon completion of this quest you will gain -500- reputation with [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?faction=530]Darkspear Trolls[/url], not 350.
[i]
(Note: This was done at level 70)[/i]

Here's a hint for you.  If you're catching up on quests that you missed for loremaster don't just leave after you get the stone.  If you did and you went to turn it in without looting baron aquanis then you won't be able to loot the stone to make him appear again to get his item.  Just an fyi.

[b]Preparation:[/b]
- Pick up the quest [quest=6921] for the [item=16762] at the Zoram'gar Outpost.
- Bring a [item=929], [item=7676], and [item=5996].
- Bring food buffs, scrolls, anything else to help.

- Stealth all the way to Moonshire Ruins in [url=https://www.wowhead.com/forever/blackfathom-deeps]Blackfathom Deeps[/url].

- There is a little ramp on the right before you go under water in Moonshire Ruins. You can chill here, [i]relax[/i], and eat some [item=5527] before summoning the boss.

[b]The Fight:[/b]

- Go to the right of the entrance to Moonshire Ruins, under water, and loot the [item=16762] from the [object=177964] to summon [npc=12876].

Get the WC quest "Leaders of the Fang," because it's on the way. Finish it.  When you've killed all 4 leaders, go back to the entrance to the instance, and talk to the Disciple who's waiting there.

He will ask you to escort him through to the sleeper.  Defend him.  When the sleeper awakes, make sure you loot the gem "The Glowing Shard" from the corpses left on the ground.  CLICK ON IT TO START THE QUEST "THE GLOWING SHARD."

Go to Ratchet.  Talk to the guy named "Sputtervalve" who is standing under a little awning by the ocean, inside the town, by the warf.  There's no little yellow dot on your minimap, but you can handle it.  :-)  Very carefully, read everything he has to say.  [b]This isn't a regular quest, just a discussion with him.[/b]

Then go back to the mountain over WC.  Climb up one of the spines to get to the very top of the mountain, and talk to the Tauren Druid at the top.  She'll give you the "In Nightmares" quest.

Now, fly to Thunder Bluff.  Or walk.  Whatever, dude.

Go to the Elder Rise, and talk to Hamuul Runetotem.  He's in the big tent, with a yellow dot and a question mark on his head, thank goodness.  He'll let you complete the quest.  I got a crap pair of boots and 2000 exp. :-)

There we go, hope this helps :-)

The absolute best drop rate is from The Nameless Prophet. He is a named NPC that wanders around in the first part of Mara, before you even enter 
any of the instances. The nice part is, the INSTANT you kill him (and usually one of his friends), he respawns a couple of feet away. 
So, basically, you can run back and forth, kill him over and over again, and get this quest done in no time. 
My drop rate was 11/13, or 85%. 
I would've gotten ALL of my crystals from him, had I known he had such a great respawn/drop rate! Have a hunter with you and he's easily 
trackable when he respawns.

(Classic) I filled up the vial outside the instance and was told I could complete the quest there too. That doesn't seem to be true. So I entered the instance alone on the orange side and had a look around. Turns out, as a level 51 warlock, this was easily soloable. There are two plants right at the start and resetting the instance once was enough to get 8/8 vines healed.

Right after the bridge there's a level 45-46 flower mob, sneak past it to the left. If it aggros you, just jump down and run out. To the right of the second mob is the plant you seek. Stand next to it and right click your (filled) vial. This spawns two non-elite water elementals that don't really hit that hard at all. The kills are what counts as "vines healed" and each kill can be worth more than one point.

The second plant is much harder as it's right next to three flower mobs. Interestingly, they only aggro if you pull by proximity, either the flowers or the elementals. Fortunately, I had a soulstone and learned my lesson. Turns out, if you range pull the elementals, you can pull them one at a time and none of the other mobs will aggro you. But if you mess this part up, you'll have a hard time escaping as they'll root you, and you still need to get past the previous mobs. It might be easier to just reset and do the first plant a few times.

As for knowing what to look for, it's a pretty small plant on the ground with no tooltip, not targetable. It's purple on top with greenish leaves.
The orange crystal pools, for filling the Vial, are just outside the orange instance portal.

There is a vine located at the 2nd mob when you enter orange.

The vine can spawn 2-3 scions, should be possible to solo for any class. The two mobs in the way, not so much, but you can possibly just use an invisibility potion to skip them. I did it as a rogue.

Reset dungeon 2-3 times to complete quest.

To be clear, the wines are located inside the instance in the orange part. Use the vial on the wines (it has about 10 yard range). They are non elites so quite easy to take out, even possible to take one at a time if you are careful.

Soloed this as a 43 Feral Tauren Druid with armor with lots of +agi.

Plus each flower spawns two or three of the level 46 Scions..

I entered through in the Orange area, stealthed past the first two Lashers, where there's a flower.  I'd use the liquid, and kill the two scions that came out.  If there were three, I ran.  :P

After I killed the two, I'd go out of the instance, reset it, and go back in.  I did this in 6 short trips (two trips spawned 3 guys).

This is in the Mauradon instance in Desolace, roughly 30,62.

You need to go in the instance - big Steel double doors.  Go to the right and follow the Orange crystals to the instance entrance.

Make sure you look at the screen shot of the plant. There's no label to the plant when you mouse over the item, so it's possible to run past several of these, especially when your party is pushing forward.

The orange crystal pool is JUST outside the orange instance entrance to the right. (39,58) 
The vines look like orange/red mushrooms with fern leaves coming from under the mushroom cap and are inside the orange side of the instance.
Please note that these do not sparkle like normal quest objects.  They also do not have a cog when you hover over them, so keep your eyes open.

The Celebrian Rod is found in the orange side of Mara and drops from Noxxian, a poison elemental 48 elite.  The Celebrian Diamond drops from Lord Vyletongue in the purple side of Mara.  Noxxion can hit fairly hard and spawns little adds during the fight. Vyletongue has two hidden demons that join the fight once it begins. When you've received both items, you need to defeat Celebras who is closer to the end of the purple side (near where you zone i if you have the scepter already). He spawns many adds but once you defeat him, speak to his ghost to complete the quest.

The NPC that gives you this quest, Cavindra, is located inside the fortress/cave that leads into the Maraudon instance. Look for orange crystals and continue heading down that path. She is a satyr NPC that will be standing on the left side of the hall.
Sadly if you have entered the instance via the portal created by the scepter and your party wipes. You will have to ressurect at one of the orange or purple portals and come back to use the scepter.

Secret to killing Noxxion is to have a powerful tank who can aggro him, while everyone else in your party concentrates only on attacking Noxxion...not the 5 NPCs who surround him.  Once you kill Noxxion, you can pick apart the remaining NPCs.

As a rogue, once our Pally tank aggro'ed Noxxion, I stealthed behind him, hit him with Ambush, then Backstab multiple times, in addition to my dagger and fist weapon being coated with poison.  Didn't take too many hits to put him down, since Ambush hit for 300+, and the Backstabs for 200-400 depending.  The Pally was grinding him from the front, and others were using ranged weapons, spells, etc.

I did have to quickly assist with taking out the remaining NPCs as the Pally was really taking a beating.  He was a L56, but everyone else in the party was L46-49.

We found Celebras behind lord Vyletounge, after jumping down a waterfall (but before the earthsong falls; it may also be possible to access this area through the orange crystals.) He spawns as a corrupted keeper, Celebras the Cursed. Kill him, and his ghost, Celebras the Redeemed, will spawn. The ghost will talk to those who do not have this quest, giving some backround on himself and Zaetar.

Celebras the Cursed spawns in the middle of 3-4 nonelite corrupted treants, and will summon more during the fight. It was once possible to pull the pre-spawned treants without pulling Celebras, but now they are aggro-linked.
