I just tried this quest, and when it's level-appropriate it's now pretty difficult. As mentioned, you have to get items from both the orange and purple wings of Maraudon, but Celebras the Cursed is in the Poison Falls, a no-man's land between both wings.

Being the tank, I figured it would be easy to lead the party the entire distance, going so far as to share the quest and explain my objectives to entice people to stay. The first group disbanded the moment they finished both wings. For the second group, I just zoned into the orange side, did the quest sharing/explanation thing, got them to continue through the Poison Falls (our hunter died twice in the poison clouds left by the dead slimes), and took out the final boss in the purple side by entering from the back way.

Then the healer zoned out, I urged the rest of them on with so little left to do, and went down the big waterfall in the poison section. If you stay in the water the elementals there are manageable as single pulls, compared to the slimes in groups of four on the dry ground. Celebras is to the left after jumping down the falls, on a small island with three non-elite trees. By the time we made it I felt like completing the quest warranted some kind of Feat of Strength achievement just for keeping the group together.

Here's how you get your Thrash Blade - the quick way if you don't want to waste the time of whoever 70 is pulling you through. I like doing it on the purple side because i hate the blobs in the orange side.. they can ruin your day.

1. Be [b]level 45 [/b]or higher, and go to Nijels Point (Alliance) or Shadowprey Village (Horde).[b] Make it your home for hearthing out[/b]
2. Get the "[b]Corruption of Earth and Seed[/b]" quest. [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?quest=7064]For Horde[/url], [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?quest=7065]For Alliance[/url]. 
3. Go To [b]Maraudon[/b]
4. From the entrance, follow the path until you get to a[b] room with three exits[/b] and one from where you came.
5. Pick the[b] leftmost tunnel,[/b] you should see [b]purple [/b]crystals lining the walls[b].Keep to the right[/b] as you follow the path, and soon you will see the entrance to the instance.

[url=http://img247.imageshack.us/img247/3406/maraudonmap1bze6.jpg]This map will help steps 6-10[/url]

6. Purple wing is pretty linear. Follow it to the end, and [b]skip [/b]or kill Lord Vyletongue .
7. Now, from Lord Vyletongue, keep going deeper in the purple dungeon. 
8. After quite a few pulls, you will reach a waterfilled area that ends in a waterfall (going down).
9. Jump [b]down [/b]the waterfall.
10. Go [b]left [/b] and forge ahead until you reach [b]Celebras the Cursed, pass him,[/b](or kill)[b] and jump down the waterfall behind him.[/b]

forever.body:
First, you have to kill an elite centaur named "The Nameless Prophet". He wanders near the stone door area. He will drop the Amulet of Spirits (https://www.wowhead.com/forever/item=17757). Then you have to find the five Kahns:

Kolk, The First Kahn, is located just outside the little room where you create the portal to Inner Maraudon (Middle part).
Gelk, The Second Kahn, is located outside the portal of the purple path, hanging with the rock elementals.
Magra, The Third Kahn, is located outside the portal of the orange path, in the stairs area.
Maraudos, The Fourth Kahn, is located inside the purple path, wandering not too far away from the instance.
Veng, The Fifth Kahn, is located inside the orange path, wandering by the end of the path.

To be able to attack them, just select the Kahn and use your Amulet of Spirits.
Once you have all the gems, just click on a random one to create the Amulet of Union, which you will turn in to Centaur Pariah.

Ok, here they are:

Nameless Prophet: Once you enter Maraudon through the main gate, keep heading down towards the area where the dungeon splits into 3 main parts. He will come before that area. He will drop the Amulet of Spirits; you use this to materialize the Khans in order to kill them. You can only get the Amulet of Spirits if you have the quest. If you don't, he won't drop the Amulet of Spirits.

1st Khan: Once the instance splits into 3 roads (left takes you to purple, right takes you to orange and middle has 2 centaur statues), take the MIDDLE road. Keep going down until you get near the portal room. The first khan will be there.

2nd Khan: He is outside the Purple instance on the bottom level. He will be near a fountain looking thing.

3rd Khan: He is outside the Orange instance on patrol. Go past the pool where you filled the Cerulean vial and keep heading in that direction.

4th Khan: Go inside the Purple instance. Head to the demon who gives you the Celebrian Diamond (Lord Vyletongue or something)

5th Khan: I am positive about the others, but not this one since I got the 5th gem a long time ago. Pretty sure he is in the Orange instance.

To recap: 3 of the khans are outside the instances and the other 2 are inside, 1 in purple, 1 in orange.

The kahns are found in these areas:

Middle area = 1st
Purple area = 2nd
Orange area = 3rd
Purple instance = 4th
Orange instance = 5th

The best sequence to find the amulet and the Khans:
Enter the stone door. This is not the entrance to the dungeon. The Nameless prophet is red (aggressive) and is located directly under the first bridge. He is an elite. The adds are non-elite. He drops the amulet that you need to change the Khans from green (non-aggressive) to red. 
The khans can be targeted by making a macro of: 
/Target spirit
This will target all the khans because they all have spirit in their name. 
1st Khan: Head down the path until you see purple and orange crystals. Go in the middle and he will be in front of the last room on this short path. This room can be used as a portal if you finish the dungeon. The adds are non-elite.
2nd Khan: Leave this area and head down the purple path to your right. After crossing the first bridge you will see two bridges. One has two blue and the other has two orange braziers. The next Khan is directly below this and between these two bridges. Try targeting him. You can see the purple entrance to the dungeon off to your right. Jump down off to the lower level on the left. There will be an elite snake where you jump down. The Khan will be in front of you down that path with an elite add on either side of him.  After killing him head left up the two flights of stairs to the dungeon entrance. 
4th Khan: He is in the purple dungeon entrance. As soon as you enter, the 4th Khan will start making his way through the dungeon. He starts his path on the lower level. You need

This quest is given by a centaur who roams near the end of the zone opposite Najel's point. To find him can be tricky, but he normally wanders in the hills south by the coven (demon area). The centaur is on the demon side of them. Talk to him and get the quest. Head to mauradon (instance dungeon in desolace)

Mauradon is not a place for the meek. the entry mobs are in the low 40's and become elite quickly as you progress. This dungeon is located in the "Valley of Spears" which is full of very aggressive centaurs. The entrance itself is basically designed like a big mine with a metal looking fanged head with steel doors in the mouth. The valley it is in is closer to the coast, not far from both the horde village and the ghelkis (sp) clan of centaurs.

I soloed this trinket at 50 with my decently-geared hunter. It was not easy, but I will give you the gist of where to find things and what you need for the Mark of the Chosen.

First you have to kill a few normal centaurs working into the mine. In a little ways, you hit a small clearing with an unnamed prophet and 3-4 ghost centaurs. Kill the prophet for the base amulet (phase 1). Clear the room.

From here you are presented with three passages. To  your left is the purple crystal area. To the right is the orange crystal area. Center is a crypt looking pas

I recommend using the orange entrance to the instance (turn north at the bottom of the entrance and you should be following orange crystals).  There is an orange pool along the way you fill the vial for https://www.wowhead.com/forever/quest=7029  Look for the red plants and use your vial when you are near them.

You can track the Khans using Track Undead if you are a hunter, or Sense Undead if you are a Paladin.  That helps find them, since there aren't any other Undead nearby.

Had this quest in my log, partied and killed the last boss (using the inner maurderan portal) of the instance and got the quest "seed of life" by speaking to the spirt that spawned.  Hearthed out, went and turned it in and went back to the dungeon with no group.  Was able to solo this quest as a level 50 dwarf paladin, here's how...

Using sense undead to see them on the map, I killed the unkown/nameless prophet to get the amulet needed for the rest of this quest.  Went to the orange side first (right), avoiding most mobs, running to where the khan was.  Use the amulet to get him to attack you, kill him and take the gem.  Run to the instance entrance and heal up.  After entering this instance it is important to not aggro anything.  If you do, you will need to reset the instance (I did this by logging out for a few minutes).  Run up the spiral stairs, and stay to the left over the little bridge, jump a gap to avoid the mob on the bridge if necessary.  Hug the left wall and take the right fork, staying to the left side of it as well.  At this point, I had caught up to the Khan and was able to use the amulet, kill him and take the gem.  Run back to the instance entrance and you just finsihed the most difficult part.

Head back to where the purple and orange forks split, and take the center path, kill the Khan there and go back to the purple side.  Follow the path, again avoiding most fights until you get to where the purple instance portal is.  Skip it for now, and head over the bridge, following that path to the next Khan.  He is in a room with 2 lvl 40 elite guys, which you can pull 1 at a time and clear out before killing the Khan.  Head back to the purple instance portal, heal up and go in.  Run along the path, and avoid the little jumping guys sticking to the right hand side of the wall.  Go up to the edge, and look down, there is a little 2 tier path down.  Jump on down and wait for the Khan to come to you.  Amulet him, kill him, loot the last gem, right click a gem to finish the quest.  Hearthstone out.

Took me about 4 re-sets on the orange side, and 2 re-sets on the purple side to successfully not aggro anything and catch up to the Khan, and learning their path.  If you don't reset, the Khan will be too far into the instance to catch him without aggroing anything.  I reset by logging out for a bit each time, but by manipulating parties, you can also reset instances.  All in all I ended up killing only about 5-6 guys other than the Khans for the whole quest, avoided the rest.

main.body:
The tablet is not in the instance, it is just outside the instance.

Enter the Uldaman caves as though you are heading toward the instance. Keep following the path, you should run off a small ledge and through a tunnel. Continue following the path until you get to a much higher ledge overlooking the instance entrance. Don't jump off the ledge! Ignore the instance entrance, keep following the path round to the left, almost immediately you will come to a kind of fork, keep to the left. You will shortly come across an entrance on your right to a room full of troggs, ignore this room, stay left, keep going. Next on your right you should see a big corded off room that is set slightly lower than the path and is full of dwarves, this is the room! (if you accidentally miss this and go too far don't worry you will get to a dead end almost straight away) The room is full of various Elites who will aggro each other easily, so if you plan to solo this then plan to fight 2-4 Elites at once :) The tablet is inside that big chest (ark-like thing) in the middle of the room.

I soloed this with a lvl44 mage, I died in the main room but I ressed just behind the chest without aggroing anything, grabbed the tablet and teleported outta there! Good luck!

Well, the first time I attempted to complete this tier of the quest, Hammertoe was not responding. There was no "?" above him, and he did not show up as a dot on the minimap. There was no gear anywhere around him and no response for any sort of command. I had not read Thottbot yet and did not realize that this was continually problematic. The quest was green for me, so after reading Thottbot, I abandoned the quest. The next day, I helped run a friend through Uldaman and since it was on the way and he was on this step also, I asked him to share it with me. He did and to our surprise, Hammertoe was operational. We also had one of my friends that had run through with me the previous night, so he tried as well. We all had the quest and spoke with him and accepted the next tier to the quest. He asks you to get an amulet off a named dwarf not far from where he is. Success once again, and back to Hammertoe. We all spoke with him, he dies and his spirit is supposed to go into the amulet for you to return to Ryedol. The spirit only went into my amulet, and as soon as everyone had left the instance, no one else even had the amulet anymore. The rewards for this quest are not that good, the xp (by the time you actually get the quest to work) is terrible at best, and the effort and frustration you go through to discover that it is bugged all to hell is more than a little irritating. In my opinion, you should just not bother with it at all.

Good luck to everyone, and happy hunting.

forever.body:
Pusillin is an imp in the East Instance of Dire Maul.  You'll start on a path around an open area with lots tree and flower elementals.  You work your way around to the NE where there is a tunnel leading down.  You'll pass by an entrance to a large hall (there may be 2 entrances to this hall).  Pass this by and go to the second hall.  You'll kill some mobs near the entrance, but about 20-30 yards inside you'll see Pusillin, a little imp.  Talk to him once about giving up the book and he'll run off deeper into the hall and up a ramp off to your right (as you're facing into the hall).  Clear out any mobs b/n you and the ramp and walk upstairs.

Pusillin will be up on this balcony waiting for you.  Before your party does anything, make sure everyone buffs/manas up and put your healer on your main AoE caster.  Have someone else talk to Pusillin.  He'll transform into a large lvl 57+ imp and summon about 8 non-elite imps to assist.  One person tank Pusillin, healers focus on the AoE person, and non-healers can assist with non-elites.  After that, take out Pusillin.  He'll drop the quest item for anyone who has the quest.  

This encounter shouldn't be a problem for any group that was able to get this far.

main.body:
To do this quest, you have to [b]kill the elementals surrounding each of the five pylons[/b]. All of the elementals have to die in order for the pylon to power down. When the last one dies, you heard a shattering sound and you'll see the pylon 'explode' and it won't glow bright bluish-white anymore. (It'll be an ugly white afterwards). The [b]elementals[/b] surrounding the pylons are [b]immune to arcane magic[/b]. They also hit rather hard so it's best if you don't take all of them down at a time. It's possible to [b]pull 1-2[/b] from the pylon without aggroing the others. 

When you go in, you'll see a pylon right away. Be careful to not aggro the trees on both sides of the pylon, and watch out for the walking giant trees (But if you;'re going to kill the big tree boss, Tendris Warpwood, you should just kill the giant trees walking around. Tendris Warpwood will call them all to defend him if you engage in a fight with him.)

Then, walk upstairs to where the undead are (the place is relatively small, I'll assume you can [b]see[/b] the upstairs are from the first pylon). There, they'll be two pylons, one on the left side, one on the right. Either way you go (it's like a rectangle shape, [~ == ~] the middle is a hole you cannot 'float' over and the pylons are marked here with a ~. Illyanna Ravenoak (boss) and her bear are walking around one side of the rectangle (the side away from the entrance) so you migth want to kill that side), you'll have to kill a mob of non-elite sk

forever.body:
I'm sure almost every mage wants to do this quest. 4200 mana over 30 seconds is invalueble. Here's my attempt at a detailed decription on how to obtain and complete the quest.

Navigating in Dire Maul (DM):
There are 3 sections of DM (North, East and West). Only 2 sections concern this quest, which is North and East. The questgiver is in the North, and the quest item is from the East. You will need a Crescent key to enter the North instance or a rog with max lock picking skill (Engineers, I have already tried blowing the doors up. Didn't work).

Upon entering DM from Feralas, you just need to follow the corridor till you reach a "T" path (you will notice a huge double wooden door at the T - Only graphics, cannot be opened). To the sides of the door, there are two slip-in entries. Go through both of them and it will bring you into a courtyard with ogres. Hugging the right wall will take into the east instance, left to west and straight across the courtyard is north.

Aggro range here is very small so its easy to slip past them. Dog patrols exist and they see through invis. 

Step 1: Obtaining a Crescent Key https://www.wowhead.com/forever/item=35607 
This is gotten from the east instance (entering from the courtyard). Immediately entering the instance, you see a non-aggro imp on your left. Speak to him and he will start running. Fight your way in the direction he ran to (right of entering the instance). Speak to him again, and he starts running. It goes on for a couple of time

Quest giver is in the Library area of the west wing-- you will need the key from the east wing to get there. If you enter through the north and have leet skills, you can get to the Library without aggro.

The mob you have to kill is back in the east wing, the water elemental.

Upon interacting with Master Winthalus's skeleton and following the dialogue bubble, [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?npc=14368]Lorekeeper Lydros[/url] turns to you and says the following:

[quote]I very much doubt that he will have anything to say, stranger...

I personally didn't mind him. It was the Prince who took exception to a high elf in his domain. Alas, I am not one to question the Prince. In his defense, he did not incinerate Master Winthalus immediately.

main.body: For those of you wondering, she's in Dire Maul East.
This quest counts towards the Loremaster of Kalimdor achievement.

You enter the Dire Maul trough main gate, turn right and go the path called Eldreth Row until the East end. There is a small tunnel which leads to the instance. Inside once again go on the right side - clean or pass mobs and at the end turn right. First room on the right side is where you can find Lethtendris. She's on the platform walking around  a campfire.

In Dire Maul East, make sure your in the Warpwood Quarter.  Go to the North East corner and turn right into the hallway.  There's another entrance on the right after entering The Hidden Reach (which is the hallway you just turned into).  Turn right into that room, go all the way to the back and go up the ramp.  Lethtendris is up the ramp circling a campfire.  If you don't turn into that room, you'll go down a narrow hallway and you've gone too far.
also, [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?quest=7494]Feathermoon Stronghold[/url] is not a prerequisite.  this is a follow-up but you can pick up this quest without doing that one.

I just soloed her tonight (60 rogue). I attempted this several times prior to hitting 60, and I can tell you right now that without a ton of shadow and fire resist, she will "WTFPWN" you, as they say in the vernacular.

I pulled it off as a NON-EPIC Cold Blood/Preparation spec rogue (so, 24/2/25) with around 1200 HP to spare. This was an expensive project, and I also had help from engineering trinket pets. Kids, don't try this at home. Or, at least if you're going to, read the following.

This fight took me a buttload of potions. I brought along an Elixir of the Mongoose, two Greater Shadow Protection Potions (one for before and one for after killing the imp), one Greater Fire Protection Potion, one Gift of Arthas, the obligatory stack of Major Healing Potions, and I managed to get a Major Healthstone beforehand, too. Quite the shopping list, right?

First off, I opened with a distract and went pure DPS on the imp. This means Ambush. Lethtendris hits freaking HARD, so you don't want this to last long. I opened up with Ambush, hit Evasion, racked up my five combo points, Cold Blood, Eviscerate. I managed to kill him before Evasion wore off, so I Vanished right then. Lethtendris will usually have you dotted here, which will break stealth (potion or no), so you need to get out of her "comfort zone" before you vanish. If you're about 10 yards back from her wander path, it won't matter if stealth breaks while she's running back.

Cross over to the Court of the Highborne (on left side), then through door at bottom of ramp that needs to be lockpicked, which brings you into the Prision of Immol'tharm, then take a right and go through corridor (another door but not locked) into the Athenaeum, which is where you will find Lorekeeper Kildrath. main.body:
This book starts a warlock quest rewarding a class-specific trinket, the [url=?item=18467]Royal Seal of Eldre'Thalas[/url]. A class book can randomly drop from any boss in [url=?zone=2557]Dire Maul[/url] or can be contained in the [url=?object=179547]Dusty Tome[/url] at the end of Dire Maul North.

Upon accepting the quest, [url=?quest=7502]Harnessing Shadows[/url], players must return the book to Shen'dralar [url=?npc=14382]Lorekeeper Mykos[/url], located in the Athenaeum of Dire Maul. The Athanaeum is an underground library that is most easily accessed via Dire Maul North, though can be reached at the end of Dire Maul West, as well. Both paths will require the [url=?item=18249]Crescent Key[/url] to enter.

Just to add to the very helpful post above, this is pretty easy to solo. I had never been to the instance, however, so I didn't know what the North entrance was or how to get there. I'll try to clarify for complete noobs like myself.

As you come up to the main entrance, which is marked on the map, you'll go up a ramp which has an ogre at the top. There are walkways to the left and right, but you want to go straight through the big doorway and into a hallway that turns a couple of times ... there's only one way to go here, so just follow it. I was level 56 and I was able to go around the ogres without aggro. [b]Watch out for patrolling packs of dogs, they're pretty frequent.[/b]

At the end of the hallway there's a giant door-looking thing, but you have to go around to the back of it to continue. It's pretty clear on the map. When you get around and through there's a giant open courtyard with a sunken forum in the middle and ogres all over. I stuck to the left wall and was able to get past all the ogres. Go all the way north here to find the door.

At the north end there's a ramp that is guarded by a couple of ogres that are a little too close to sneak by, at least at level 56. At this point I used my pet to distract them and ran to the door, feign death.

Here you either need a crimson key, which you can't solo, or you can use a powerful seaforium charge (if you're an engineer), which worked like a charm. Keep in mind that you'll need 2 of them, one for this door and one for

You can actually just go straight into DM North and take the door in the south-west corner of the lower area and it will lead you straight to the quest turn-in. There's no mobs to fight at 80(maybe lower too) going this way.

Also, you can only turn in this quest once, so don't make the same mistake I did and buy a whole bunch of them trying to get rep, it won't work.

Go in through the west set of doors from the courtyard of Dire Maul. You really don't need to clear anything except a path if you have ever cleared DM before. The one exception could be the big tree guy right before the door where you use the crescent key for the first time in the instance (just to get around him). He's at the bottom of the ramp. 80's shouldn't have much trouble getting past most mobs without drawing aggro.

Once you're past that, you'll enter the big circular room.. Hug the right wall until you get to the next door. This will take you to the library where this quest point terminates.

If you're looking for the 700 quest achievement in Kalimdor, this is one more towards that goal.

forever.body: Solo'd this quest as a 58 priest, granted I did have the Crescent Key. Simply run in at the northern entrance and wait for the guard to run to patrol to the right (He may stand still for a while, but it's safer to wait him out.) As soon as you think you're out of aggro range, go left to see a group of 3 ogres. Mind sooth the one closest to you and then run down the stairs to the right. Jump over the banister of the steps to the left and huge the wall around the other group. Mind soothe the one closest to the door, run down, and voila, you've got yourself a nifty trinket in about 6 minutes flat. :)

You turn it to the Athenaeum inside Dire Maul.  This is in the west instance (instance with Immol'thar).  Sepulcher has nothing to do with this quest.

Reward is Royal Seal of Eldre'Thalas, a trinket that give +10 Fire resist, increases effects of heal spells by up to 30 and regens 4 mana every 5 seconds.

To complete this quest, follow a few simple steps:
1. Get the book, trigger the quest. 
2. Find the Library in Dire Maul, and use the Crescent key to open the door. 
3. Inside there's a bunch of friendly NPCs, and you can find the quest target on the minimap
4. Turn in the book to him, and you'll recieve an awesome trinket and 7000 experience.

This is the reward from the quest.

You can sneak through this pretty easily.  Enter DM north.  On each side there are a group of ogres and a ogre pat that walks through.  Wait for the pat to be on the right side and run straight.  There will be a ramp down to a grassy area with a campfire surrounded by ogres.  Be careful here as there is a pat of hyenas walking around.  Jump on the left edge of the ramp and drop down onto the "ledge" down by the grassy area.  Follow the "ledge" along the wall and you'll reach the side of the ramp that leads down into library.

This is a bit tricky.  You can try to jump to get onto the side of the ramp, then run down.  If you miss the jump, run down the wall and get in range of the ogres to Mind Soothe them.  Once mind soothed, run along the edge and down the ramp.  Then you just have to follow the trail down into library.

I did this at lvl 60, so if you're lower lvl becareful of the aggro range.

Good luck!

Alright, as I had a horrible time finding the library to turn in the quest, here's a breakdown of how to find it/get there:
1. Enter Dire Maul, and go into the main courtyard where the PVP arena is located (don't go in it, though).
2. Go to the [u]North[/u] Side of the courtyard, or, directly on the other side of the arena from where you entered. There is a door that requires the [u]Crescent Key[/u].
3. Once inside, you will see another courtyard below you. There is a steep ramp only slightly to the left. There are a LOT of dogs down there, so be careful if you're low level. Go down the ramp and to the left. (If you go through a big archway and see only a couple dogs, you went too far. Like me...lol)
4. There is a bluish doorway on the left. Go in.
5. The doorway leads into a very, very long hallway. There are no bad guys in here so feel free to pop Aspect of the Cheetah or Dash, etc. 
6. The hallway ends in the Athenaeum (The Library!). Go inside and to the right. On the right and just before the large bronze globe you will find Lorekeeper Javon.
7. Turn in your quest and celebrate! :)

Lords & Ladies:

There is a lot of whining above, but let me set the record straight. My guildmates and I have assisted in the forging of no less than half a dozen Quel Serrars in Onyxia's Lair. It is not all that hard if you know what to do.

After the first two phases of the Onyxia battle have passed, let your tank be absolutely confident that he has the great wyrm under control. Get her down to bout 5% so that you know that you've got this battle within reach. Plant the blade in front of Onyxia's face next to your tank, then quickly get the heck away from her. 

(If the battle is going badly and you're not completely confident that you're going to win, KEEP THE BLADE in it's sheath. You can always try again after you wipe if you didn't put it down to be breathed on.)

Your tank (who should have sufficent Fire Resistance to sustain a GREAT MANY breaths, duh!) can give you a shout when the blades been breathed on.

Run over and pick up the blade. If you're concerned about getting killed, down a Fire Resistance potion before running over to Onyxia's face. Grab the blade and get the heck away from her.

At that point you've now got 20 minutes to take her from 5% to 0%. If you can't do that, well, maybe you should have sold the book to start with. :-P

Grab your blade and stick it in her corpse. Run back to Dire Maul and complete the quest. 

If you've pulled it off, welcome to the elite ranks of Azeroth.

I soloed this as a level 70 affliction / demonology warlock without too many trouble. Here's a little guide:

Go to the back entrance of Dire Maul in Feralas. The location is shown on the map Burgermeal posted, and it's pretty hard to miss. Just look for a structure with the same design as Dire Maul and head through the tunnel. When you're there, either open the door with the Crescent Key or Life Tap / Hellfire and revive your spirit at the other side of the door.

When inside the instance, you'll see you skipped the entire elemental area of Dire Maul East and are at the demons you need straight away. Your Voidwalker is the one you'll love in here. First, you see two plants which aren't linked. Just pull them, drain tank a bit and they'll die without too many problems. Time for the real work now.

In the area you'll find a couple of patrols which you'll want to pull first. They're not much stronger than a regular level ~68 mob, so you'll hardly have trouble with them. If you've cleared some patrols, it's time for the packs. Stick your Voidwalker on one Satyr, banish the Betrayer and DoT + drain tank the other Satyr. When your mob is down, kill the mob the Voidwalker is tanking and then kill the Betrayer which should be unbanished by now.

This tactic will allow you to clear most of the area you need and should provide you with sufficient Satyr Bloods to complete the quest. Judging by the comments in this thread, many people seem to think there's also packs of four demons. Thi

This is an easy quest for a Warlock to solo at 45. Use a voidwalker as you'll quite often get multiple mobs for it to tank; make sure you let it recover if it gets a beating. You should find you can get to the relevant room without even coming close to dieing as long as you use Curse of Recklessness for crowd control.

Once you're in there, make sure you clear out the whole of upstairs before you head towards the elementals - the last thing you want is a Shadowforge Caster healing them or, worse, shielding them or, worse still, putting you to sleep! Once you've done that, you can attack the nearest elemental without aggroing the others (or, at least, I could at 45) and he goes down quick as he's only a 38. Next up, stand on the right-hand staircase, and attack the right-hand stone elemental with your voidwalker. Somehow the left one doesn't get aggroed. When he's nearly there, use Banish on Ambassador Infernus and polish off the stone elemental. Set your voidwalker on the other elemental and just wait until Banish runs out on the ambassador - and then banish him again. Then kill the other stone elemental.

Now the tricky bit. All your fire spells aren't much use here, so use shadow spells, health funnel and banish to keep your voidwalker alive whilst you kill the ambassador... very... slowly. He'll go down eventually, although you might well have to use a healthstone, a potion and a bandage to make sure your own life tap spell doesn't kill you.

Midgelle's advice worked perfectly.  My warlock friend and I soloed this part after numerous failed PUG scholo runs.

Here is how:  Wait by entrance until a group comes out that has just competed scholo.  Make sure they have killed Ras as part of their run.  Ask them for an invite and to make you leader.  Then you can invite any other warlocks who need this.  Enter scholo (u need a key or get someone to open door for you).  Come in the entry way to a hall where there is more than likely a respawn.  Hug the right corner railing and go just barely in and jump over.  You shouldn't get aggro at this point.  Jump all the way to the bottom and run through, you will come to a room that is full of yellow mobs that won't attack you.  Run to the exit at the far end of that room.  That will take you to a path to a room called "The Laboratory."  Come inside just a little then go straight to the right wall.  You will see an alchemy lab here - go ahead and release imp (fast)as mobs may have seen you on the way down and could be coming for you.  The imp will do his thing and even if the mobs see you and come in and attack you, just wait for imp to finish before releasing your spirit.  It will show as "Parchment Created 1/1" and then you're done.  There is no paper to pick up or anything, just go back to see Mor'zul. Very simple!

The two of us cleared a few guards and minimal mobs and stealthed to Rattlegore to get the Viewing Room key. Once we had that we stealthed to the viewing room and went through it and we cleared the room that Ras is in. We didn't have to kill Ras but we killed him for the fun of it. 

Then my druid left the party and my warlock was invited. I entered instance, jumped down, ran through viewing room and entered Ras' room. There I released the imp to complete the quest. It took less than a half an hour. So if you have a druid and rogue friend who can help you out, the quest will be much easier than trying to find a full run or help with a full run just to complete Imp Delivery. Good luck.

This is a very useful guide for all 70 Warlocks. I followed it myself as an affliction Warlock and it went smoothly.

From thottbot, written by Shahwigs

SOLO: 70 Demo lock, regular BC drop/quest gear.

1) Have the key to scholo...
2) Bring at least 10 shards, I did it with 5.
3) Curse on Weakness is your BEST friend here.
4) Enter scholo, 4 dead skelly warriors on the entry bridge. Single pull right and left front statics with Curse of Weakness. Dont send pet or you get ALL 4. The 2 in the back you will get together so just CoW them, throw some dots, tap tank, and HEAL Felguard. It's really not hard at 70 it seems, or CoW is just really awesome.
5)Open the door and pull the roaming skell warrior you see. Go in room, go down to the right side corner and pull the roamers to here as they walk by. You can clear the close statics if you want. Go left across the room and through the other gate. I pulled the right statics next to the door, 3 mobs, but probably didnt have too as the other side didnt aggro when I went through door.
6) Go in and turn left and you will see a long hall with 3 roamers and static bad guys on each side. You can ignore the statics and actually kill the roamers in the middle of the room without aggroing them. Go to the end of the room and open the gate.

7) 4 roamers in this next room and 2 come close enough to the door to pull them outside the room 1 at a time. when this is done, go in and turn left.Straight across this room is where your going

forever.body:
Alright, after defeating Immol'thar (be aware to kill his eyes quickly!), our group - warrior, hunter, priest, paladin, warlock (me) - buffed up and I released the imp from his jar. After releasing the Imp he will start placing the bell, wheel and candle in the circle. After placing those 3 items he will disappear. As soon as the Imp leaves, Imps spawn at the edge of the summoning circle. These don't hit for more than 1 if the artifacts are all working. 
When an artifact goes down, it makes a loud noise and floats lower, and it can be easily identified by mousing over it (if it's broken it will have the wheel instead of the mouse pointer). Fixing it costs a soul shard, so bring plenty. I used around 10 for repairing the artifacts, and 3 more for enslaving a demon, a healthstone for the warrior and a soulstone for the pala.
After a while, dread guards will spawn after each other (4 to be precise). It's wise to enslave the first one so he can attack the next dread guard that spawns. (If there are 2 warlocks in the group, you each enslave one and let the enslaved one kill the other spawns). If another one adds while the other hasn't died yet, you should banish it, since these are strong (level 60 elites). 
Once all four dread guards have spawned, the ritual will soon be over. You can check this by looking at the pink symbols at the floor - 9 have to be lit to create enough energy for the summoning circle. 
You will directly notice when the ritual is complete as around the circle

You absolutely need a group, this is in an instance (Dire Maul -- west side). All in all, its not a hard quest. 5 lvl 60s should be able to handle it well. If you dont have a priest, it can be tricky to get where you need to go since there is a portion where shackle undead is very helpful. Mor'zul's instructions explain quite well what to do. After you defeat immol'thar, release jeevee from his jar and he will set up the circle. simply have your whole party inside the circle fighting the many demons who come running in. It is useful to have an additional AoEer beyond the warlock who is doing this quest since the warlock will be mostly occupied with repairing the 3 elements of the circle. There will be a lot of demons running in to the circle and fighting your group, but if the warlock does his job and keeps the devices from failing, its actually pretty easy. The summoning portal takes a few minutes to complete and the warlock must have many soulshards to keep the repairs up (I used 10). Once the portal is complete rest up, rebuff and then summon the dreadsteed. After you have been fighting for a bit an elite demon will say something like "Who dares steal my steed?" and will join the fight against you. My all-60 party of 2 warlocks 1 druid 1 warrior and a paladin had no trouble completing any of the battles involved with this quest. 

Also of note: Even if only one warlock has purchased the items for the summoning circle, repairing, and dreadsteed summoning, other warlocks wit

DM West is rather easy for Warlocks due to their banish spell.  Having 2 'locks makes taking down the pylons very easy.

Having 2 'locks around for enslave demon during the Xorothian Dreadsteed event is sometimes the edge you need to succeed.  Since the elite demons spawn at a certain rate during the event, it is possible to fall behind and then it becomes very diffictult to finish.   With a second 'lock handy it's no trouble to have 2 elite demons controlled and fighting one (or two if you're really behind in dps) elite demon(s).

I recently got my warlock to lvl 60.  I was very anxious to get my dreadsteed so I did the following and got it within less than a day of when I picked up the first quest!

See your lock trainer and he sends you to talk to Bloodbringer in Burning Steppes.  (Note: Thottbot has quest under lvl 58 but you cannot begin until 60.)  When you get to him, pick up quest "Rage of Blood" and then save yourself some travel time and pick up "Lord Banehollow" from the goblin behind him.  Purchase your shadowy potions and keep em handy.  The longest part of this quest for me was the blood, but it can be done in about an hour or so.  Do whichever first according to preference, I preferred getting the most annoying part done first.

Go to Winterspring and hit Owl Wing Thicket for the Rage of Blood quest items.  I teamed up with a very nice warrior who was only looking for regularly dropped items by saying I would only loot my quest items.  Went much faster.  After getting 30 bloods, hit Felwood.  Once at the entrance to Jaedenar, pop your shadowy potion (you have 3 so don't worry about losing the buff).  This way you won't have to fight your way to the tunnel.  It's a long run to get to Banehollow you should have about 15 mins left on your buff when you get to him.  Pick up your quest and backtrack (not very far) to Ulathek.  If you wish, pop a new potion and then speak to him.  He will (along with his guards) aggro.&n

I just tried to complete this quest with a warlock guildie.  We read everything we could about it on thottbot and in the dungeon guide, so we thought we were ready.  Well, it would have been really nice to know some VERY important details about this instance and quest BEFORE doing it!

1.  When you assemble your group, make sure someone has the Crescent Key to get in the West side instance.

2.  Before you even think about clearing the summoning circle and beginning that process, you MUST clear the voidwalker-type demons from around 5 different mana pylons throughout the instance.  There are groups of about 7 of these mobs around each one, and these mobs must be cleared to deactivate each pylon.  Each pylon must be deactivated in order to lower the shield around the final boss that is sitting inside your soon to be summoning circle for the quest!

3.  Before attempting to kill Tendris Warpwood (the big tree boss in the second room of the instance down the ramp) be sure to kill ALL of the big pats that look like him from the first room.  If you don't, you will pull all 6 of them plus the boss!

Anyway, this saved us quite a few hours of work and repair bills, so I thought I'd share it.

5 Holy Water: These are found in crates inside Stratholme (Both Scarlet & Baron) and are also needed in a comon quest found in Eastern Plagueland. May be found in stacks of 1-3 in each crate. 
(Carefull if you choose wrong crates they spawn "dangerus" critters)

10 Arthas Tear: Ask a Herbalist (Or do it yourself if you are one) to go gather these, they are a not too rare flower that show up in plauged area. (Felwood, etc.) 
Search Arthas Tear for their best whereabouts or simply buy them off AH.

6 Arcanite Bar: Ask an alchemist to make you these. They are transmuted from an Arcane Crystal & a Thorium Bar. They can, however, only transmute once every 48 hour. If you got Arcane Crystals and Thorium bars yourself, try getting them to transmute for you for 3-5g. If not expect to pay a larger amount of Gold for them...

40 Runecloth: Dropp on many different +52 Humanoids & Undeads, you really shouldn't have any problems finding these. If you do you allways got other players to buy from.

150 Gold: You get this true grinding, questing (+60), selling items, or any other way you may find fitting.

Stratholme Holy Water can be obtained from Supply Crates in Stratholme.

10 Arthas' Tears can be purchased at the AH for around 2g.

Runecloth shouldn't be a problem at all at 55-60. You should easily have 40 by the time you get the quest.

Arcanite Bars can be transmuted by Alchemists, but you need to have 1 Thorium Bar and 1 Arcane Crystal. If you ask politely, you are bound to meet some people that will transmute them for you  for free. You can purchase these from the AH for about 10-15g, but I found it cheaper the first way.

It is near impossible to get a good enough group of lvl60+ to get the items from stratholme, when finally getting the holy water which took me almost 2 weeks, I hand in the quest, along with the 150Gold, to find out that there is another quest chain to complete that makes this one look like a sitting with jakanory!

Not only that but you have to pay a further 150Gold to the guy in ironforge for a tome that allows you to summon the 25 undead in the plaguelands that you have to kill before getting the super hard quest that requires you to go to Dire Maul and Scholomance - with TBC it is way too hard to get a group to do these instances!

After getting this far I have decided it's not worth continuing with this quest line! Thats my take!

So think on...

Hope this helps!

OK.  I was very frustrated over this, but it's fine now.  There are TWO quest chains that roll into one for the epic mount.  In order to get the Ancient Equine Spirit quest you must also finish a separate quest chain called "Exorcising Terrordale".  I tried to do the Exorcising Terrordale quest before this one and ever time I killed a spirit I DIDN't get credit for the kill.  After doing the blessed "Arcantie Barding quest" Lord Grayson took the barding from me and didn't give me the Ancient Equine Spirit quest or give me the barding back.  I then re-tried the Terrordale quest (and got credit for the kills) and turn it in to Lord Grayson and he then gave me the barding back and the next quest - Ancient Equine Spirit.  Hope this helps others.

Also, the tree is very easy to get to and you do not have to fight any mobs before hand.  The tree will be directly in front of you when you enter the instance.  Just sneak past the patrols by staying to your right.  Then hug the wall, cut a couple of corners and you will see a ramp going down to the tree.

Max hit on me with Devotion Aura up was around 900.  Druid healed only when absolutely necessary and went bear form if she stole aggro until I could regain it.  I had to shield twice during the fight to bandage.

I soloed this quest with my 64 prot pally last night.  It was close, got down to 2% of health twice.  I though I was dead, but two critical hits in a row saved me.

OK.  Solo as 61 protection pally.  

Yes, you must kill the patrols in the first room, but you do NOT need to kill the stationary mobs.  

I used seal of light, blessing of wisdom, judgment of light, and righteous fury.  be patient.  keep hitting him and heal at 50% health... just in case you get interrupted when he tosses you in the air.  I did not even need to bubble... but note that I was running low on mana at the end.  Be careful not to use too many attack spells that are high in mana, or you could get in trouble.  Other than that, this really isn't that difficult.

Lastly, you'll need the crescent key to get in.  He's in dire maul west.

Ok , just solod this one as a 60 ret paladin.

1st kill all the patrolling guardians outside.
2nd make sure you have all cooldowns availible.
3rd pray for good luck!

My setup was BoK, Seal of Light and concentration aura (didnt do much use) and 35Ap buff and 12 dmg on wpn sharpening stone :D.
I had rage Rage reaver from outlands along with some other outlands gear. I had 4700 hp.

Tactics was to keep Hp up so spamming Judgement of light, Crusader strike and Divinestorm (for art of War)
was essential. I also tried to keep consecration up and exorcism as often I could. I never stopped and healed
so the concentration aura was to no use. I used lay on hands when low on hp and divine shield when low on hp to heal
up. I also popped one mana potion. I had 23% crit chance but still had a lot of luck with the crits for art of war , and make sure you use art of war as soon as possible though not when you've full hp. I managed to survive with about 7% hp spamming hammer of wrath, and all abilities at the end of the fight.
This was my second try and I would have given up if I had died but I barely made it so.. Its is possible.

Good luck with this one!

Was first to finish it on Al'Akir and I will try to list the tips here:

[b]Best combo[/b]
The best combination for completing this quest is:
4 Paladins, 1 Priest (harder to get to event, but easier to complete)
3 Paladins, 1 Mage, 1 Priest (easier to get to event, but harder to complete)

[i]Don't bring warriors for the sake of "warrior holds aggro from mage" crap or "rogues have very good dmg output" crap[/i]
You need good Paladins for this quest, as unleashing correct seals will do Area Effect damage to all ghosts withing 10 yards[/i]

[b]You need highest ranks in following Seals:[/b]

[ul]
  [li]Seal of Wisdom (rank 3) -> Banality
[/li]
  [li]Seal of Justice (rank 1) -> Malicious
[/li]
  [li]Seal of Righteousness (rank 8) -> Corrupted
[/li]
  [li]Seal of Light (rank 4) -> Shadowed
[/li]
[/ul]
[b]Don't spam Judgements[/b]
Wait for stun effect fade from ghosts between unleashing next Judgement (takes about 4 seconds).

[b]Stay in North-East corner until boss comes[/b]
Stay in North-East corner until boss comes and refresh as much as possible (drink mana potions, heal, resurrect, buff).

[b]If you fail, you have to restart instance[/b]
If you are wiped out after activating quest event, all doors leading to the basement will be closed, so you must reset instance to restart event.
If you fail abandon and re-accept quest to receive the items for starting the event.

At boss pray that you don't get a message "Server restarting for maintenance" which had happened to me.

Mystic Ward.

1a: Exorcise 25 spirits in Terrordale. There are green glowing circles around in the ruins of Terrordale (near the Terrorweb 

Tunnel exit). Use the censor within these circles and 1-3 spirits will spawn. Simply kill them until you have killed 25 of 

them. The green circles spawn relatively fast. I soloed this portion and took approximately 30 minutes.

barding and Manna-Enriched Horse Feed on you and someone with the crescent key with you. Go into Dire Maul West and simply 

run past all the mobs. We did t

I now know why some people say the quest is a cakewalk and others say it is not do-able. Both are correct. The quest is buggy! I have experienced both so I know. You will either complete this without trouble or fail miserably. Please do not flame me with corrections. If you have something to add to help great! Please keep it constructive. I found the lack of advice/help on this quest frustrating and wish to make it easier for people who follow me. 

 I will now recount the problem areas and how we overcame them. This quest is very do-able and you can have your mount on the first attempt if you follow the advice below. I am not saying this is the ONLY way to complete it. It is how we did and what I learned in the process I think can help others.

[b]Composition of Party[/b]
[b]Number of Paladins:[/b] Paladins are required to complete the end sequence. 3 is your sweet spot of balance between getting to room without trouble and ease of completing the end sequence. 4 makes the end sequence do-able even if they things go buggy on you. But with 4 Paladins, the trip to the room will be harder and longer (It is do-able). If you want to be sure you complete the quest, 4 Paladins would guarantee you complete the Judgements portion. You should have a priest. Not only do you get heals you get crowd control with shackle. This is invaluable in end sequence (see below).
[b]Rest of Party:[/b]
Slot 1: Paladin
Slot 2: Paladin
Slot 3: Paladin or Warrior or Rogue
Slot 4: Paladin or Mage or Warlo

When you start the fight, put the scryer as far as you can in the NW corner, and stand in the SE corner. For the first 2 waves, you can single-pull the spirits. Last two waves are groups of 3+. It's not a hard fight as long as your pally (or pallies) use the proper judgement on the mobs, I've done it with only the pally with the quest before with minimal problem. The order is Wisdom, Justice, Righteousness, Light. The spirits will have names that hint at what to use (Banality, Malice, Corruption, Shadow) At the end of each wave, an Aspect of (wave name) appears, basically supposed to be a miniboss for that wave, but they're easy. Once the boss comes up, he goes down quick and the pally has his mount!

You summon the spirits in the same room as Rattlegore stand in.
 
Clear it and place the divination scryer in the NW corner but still on the mound (which rattlegore stand on). Tell your party to stand in the SE corner before you start.
As soon as you place the scryer ghosts spawn but they are easy to kill so just run to the other players and kill the ghosts. You can judge seal of wisdom (I used the highest rank on all seals and it worked just fine) to stun them for a few seconds. Also works on the aspect. Second wave isn't too hard either, few elites but can be pulled one and one. Judge seal of justice to stun spirits and the aspect. Third wave is three groups of three elites. Do NOT pull the middle group first. Start with the group by the door and take the middle group last. When you pull the middle group all remaining groups will aggro. Remember to judge seal of righteousness on both spirits and aspect.

Might be useful to put the shadow res aura on for the last wave. The last wave was easy too, few elites spawn every now and then. We had to wait a while betweent the spawns. Good time to rest and drink/eat. Use seal of light on spirits and the aspect. When the aspect is killed the boss will spawn. He's easy to kill.
Loot the boss, use the charger's lost soul to get the charger's redeemed soul and hand in the quest :)

Did it with a 70 hunter, 70 mage, 70 shadow priest, 69 rogue and me, 61 pally. Its really easy when you figure it out and do it right, hope some of you won't

Got it first try. I read the above comments and it helped a bunch! Group up in a corner, set scryer in opposite corner. 

First Wave = Wisdom
Second Wave = Justice
Thrid Wave = Righteousness
Fourth Wave = Light

It's best if you use the highest rank of each seal, though if your pallies have different ranks, they actually do stack. 

Bunching in the corner is needed if you actaully want a break in between attacks. You can med and rebuff all day till you're ready to pull the next bunch. Just sit there and AOE and Exorcise the ghosts as well as releasing your seals. Oh, and Baby Baron is a joke, totally easy. Good luck!

In my experience, the ranks of the judgements do not matter, so go ahead and use you're highest one. just make sure you have them in the right order and your set. I found that setting up a separate casting bar with the seals in the 1-4 order with judgement in the #5 slot helped a great deal.

If you wipe you'll find the gates are locked so you wont get back in. Also your scryer will be gone.
This was with 1 Pally who had the scryer, don't know if the gates stay open if you have another Pally with the scryer.

Only solution is to reset the instance (if you have another Pally with scryer).

If you do have to give up, go back to Stormwind and see [b]Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker[/b]. You have to [b][u]abandon 'Judgment and Redemption' quest[/u] [/b] and he will give it to you again. You'll get a new bag with only the scryer as you should still have the barding in your inventory.

I just completed this quest on the first try and no one died.    One pally also    We had me a warrior a priest a druid and a mage.  Make sure you set your group up in the very far N.W. corner and dont wander.  Make sure the mage does DPS and not AoE and the druid does just healing. Our mage stuck with frost spells to limit agro and save mana.  Mana is the key  pally's should only seal and judge  thats it  i dont think i ever got below 1/2 mana the entire fight.

Also,  played with the judgments listed above  and the only one that had an effect  was the seal of light on the fourth wave.  In my opinion  the third wave was the hardest, at one point we had 7-8 60 elites. 

We had several chances to stop and regen mana, i never drank one mana pot or health pot,  it went that smooth.    Good luck pally's  :)

Read the strategy from WHOME above - perfect.

our group owned the Death Knight and the spirits. 

Composition?

1. Pally
2. Pally
3. Warrior
4. Warlock
5. Priest

Two pallies CAN EASILY judge the spirits *IF* they rotate properly (we used Teamspeak).  Having a def/pro warrior assisted the final battle as the priest only had to worry about healing one person.

We took 7 GREATER shadow prot potions with us.  Everyone drank one at the start of the fourth wave.  The Tank and the Warlock each had one extra - this assists the main tank GREATLY.  Most pots are done after the 4th wave before the Death Knight.  We shackled the 4th mini boss (as per the above guide) and then the priest gave shadow prot to everyone but the Warlock and Tank (who each had a pot left)

We soulstoned the PRIEST for the last battle - that way if he drops, he can pop back up.  If you wipe on the final battle then you are done.  The Death Knight aggros on the entire room.

Everyone should move to the CENTER of the room BEFORE you drop the shackle on the 4th mini boss.  This puts you in position to intercept the Death Knight immediately when he pops.  Otherwise, he will get free shadow bolt attacks on you as you run in on him.  He will mind control, so be sure the priest is ready to get rid of it.

With the tweaks we made above to the original guide from whome above we owned the Death Knight.

GOOD LUCK!

When you kill Darkreaver, and loot the "Charger's lost soul", make sure you're standing next to the ghostly charger, not necessarily the divination scryer.

When we finished this quest form myself and another paladin, I tried standing next to the scryer and clicking on the soul - that didn't work; it said "Requires Great Ossuary".  I was starting to freak a little bit when someone said to stand near the charger's ghost.

I did that, and it worked.  I was too excited to take screenshots of the final quest completion pages... wish I had.  EDIT: I found them thanks to Google, though. :)

So anyway, if you get that far and think something's wrong because the soul won't redeem, make sure you're standing close to the horse spirit, not the divination scryer.

EDIT: Seemed odd that I had to move closer to the spirit, since when Darkreaver died, we were right near the scryer.

Solo'd as a 67 retri pala ... the satisfaction was immensely.

[b]Getting there[/b]

First of all, in order to access the basement easy without clearing too much trash you can jump down on the right of the platform, into the corner of the room bellow, as you enter the instance (right before the very first guards). BoP yourself if you want, it's only about 1k health loss. You will be agroed immediately by a group of 3-4 mobs, easy to solo. After this, stay close to wall (walk the edge) and exit through the door on the left; in the next room you don't have to fight anyone (aggro range was small enough at 67), just watch the patrols and you can enter the whelps room safely (door on the left again). In the whelp room hug the left wall and you have to clear through 2 groups of mobs maximum.

[b]Basement of the Great Ossuary[/b]

Range pull with Exorcism the first 2 mobs on left and right  and deal with them at the door. You can range pull Rattlegore just the same, but be careful of the mobs wandering [b]behind him[/b] so you don't get any add. I wanted to play safe so I used SoL & JoL throughout the fight, spamming CS, DS and consecration. Only had to use 1 mana pot, the instant healing FoL from Art of War was enough to keep me alive (around 24% crit in mixed greens and blues from q rewards).

[b]The waves[/b]

My party composition was a 57 warlock, 58 hunter, 60 mage, 60 priest (very well geared, renews were ticking for 406) and myself, a level 62 protection spec paladin. no one in the group came close to dying, except on the miniboss for each wave where i hit 50%. sure we had to mana up a little after the wave with all the shadow bolts, but other than that, piece of cake. I don't know any 'ideal' group setup for this, but the other night, myself and a fellow paladin, a mage, a priest, and a hunter did this quest. It really helps to alternate judgements between the paladins to keep the mobs stunned.

Also nice to know that multiple paladins can do the quest at once.

A nifty tactic (if you have a priest) is to shackle one of the mobs in each wave. Kill everything else but the shackled one and it gives you a breather. We managed to keep the group up at almost full life/mana this way.

Alternatively, a paladin could try and keep one perma-feared. That may work too.

I just two-boxed this easily with a 60 Holy Paladin and a 70 Arms Warrior after failing in my first attempt. In addition to the advice given so far, here are a few tips that may help if you run it with a similarly minimalist crew.

1) The first 3 waves are cake, even more so if you have anything that can lower the melee damage of the spirits (like Demo Shout). You can safely run Ret Aura for most if not all of these first 3 waves.

2) The 4th wave is when it can get a bit tricky if you're unprepared - the mobs will lob a lot of  Shadowbolts and Shadowbolt Volleys. Shadow Protection Potions will essentially trivialize the rest of the event, so feel free to bring some if you're running with a light crew. The final boss (Death Knight Darkreaver) will go spam-happy with shadowbolts, but they're much more manageable than the 4th wave.

3) Darkreaver's Mind Control *may* be ranged-based. My paladin was MCed early on when she was standing 10 feet from the DK. I moved her to max healing range after the first MC and was untouched the rest of the fight.

I had to place the Scryer in the middle of the room to start the event. Still, standing in one of the corners by the entrance can help provide some downtime when needed.

Besides that, a walk in the park, and it was slightly cheaper then buying the epic riding skill too! :)

So go get it, it's worth the time to do it :D

Do you plan to wear an element forever? I see this epic as pretty decent. I wish they would substitute strength for intelligence. Im going to jump in on the "OMFG IDIOT!" arguement.

% is a %.. a chance. There is no real telling if you'll crit every hit throughout the duel or not at all. You can make a % to try to determine what % you may crit..but even that is still random, its like a /roll 1-100...

So the whole 4.52 min jive based off a math theory imo is very wrong. Percentages in this game are talking about chances, not percentages as in amounts. Your dividing and calculating it as an amount. I suck at math and even I know this.

Going around screaming "omfg this helm sux omfgz0r lawll bbq sauze OH NOESZZZ!" 24/7 isn't going to stop people from wearing it. Its all about personal prefference. With the strength I see it better than elemental for melee situations. Unless you are somehow cursed by blizzard, you have more than 1 slot. Which means you can carry the sky and the elements at the same time via bag..and swap them when you PvP/Duel.

To help clarify for people doing this in 2018 or later:  

Step 1. Enter the ogre section of the dungeon. 
2. Ignore all the all the bosses (you can kill trash if you want) until you reach a room with a goblin and an ice trap. 
2.5. Get the quest from the goblin if you've never been here before- if you have, he'll have a blue question mark which means it's a repeatable quest.
3. Go to the floor above and grab the basket of Ogre Tannin, then jump down and exchange it with the goblin for a Gordok Ogre Suit.
4. Continue heading through the dungeon until you reach Captain Kromcrush at the end of a hall before an outside area
5. Use the Gordok Ogre Suit and talk to him until he runs off yelling about one of the Guards.
6. Kill the King, wait for an ogre to run up to you, then click through his dialogue until he spawns a treasure chest with some really rare loot.
7. Run BACK through the dungeon until you reach the spot where the second guard boss was, where Kromcrush will be offering this quest to talk to the first boss.
8. Talk to the first boss and the quest will be completed.

For those of you who are new to DM and figuring out this quest, you can do this quest in two ways.

First one is to go to the dungeon with the materials to make the ogresuit, talk to the goblin that seems to be captured and chained who can be found on the way to Captain Kromcrush, get the ogresuit and talk to the Captain while wearing it.

Another way, which is applicable if you can accomplish the following which is to walk around the Captain to kill the Gorduk King, who is just a bit further behind the Captain.  Once you kill that boss, you will get a buff that lets the other ogres recognize you as the new king.  With this buff, all monsters in the dungeon turn 'green' on you (except these two voidwalkers that I found; when killed they are not lootable) and talk to you.  This applies to Captain Kromcrush as well.  Talk to him throuh the dialogue and eventually he will throw on the "!" sign.

If you've killed the prince already, great.  You just have to go back to the spot and loot the small chest there.  If you haven't, find Shan'dralar Ancient in the west wing who gives the quest to kill the prince, along with a beast named Imol'thar.  This way you can catch two birds with one stone.

The west and north wings are connected and Shan'dralar Ancient is located on the top tier of the west wing.  Refer to the map of Dire Maul map on this site for directions, it's quite easy to figure out how they are connected.  As far as getting to the top tier is concerned to get to Sh

main.body:
To complete this quest:
1. Enter Blackrock Spire instance
2. In first room you come to, go up the left set of stairs and turn left up a shorter flight of stairs into Dragonspire Hall
3. You must kill everything in this hall - mobs are in groups in small rooms on the sides.
4. When everything is dead, a door opens at the north end of the hall. Go through it and follow the stairs up and around.
5. Now you enter the Hall of Binding and another locked door blocks your path.
6. Click on the Blackrock Altar on the left side, kill all adds.
7. Wait until the elemental on the platform in the middle reaches full power and he then becomes attackable.  Kill him and the door at the Southern end of the room will open.
8. Go through the door into The Rookery (this is the room where you get the Jenkins achievement, incidentally)
9. Go right and double back on yourself up a slope. Take the first set of steps up, into the Hall of Blackhand.
10. Turn right, go through the hall and up one of the sets of stairs at the East end.  You're now at Blackrock Stadium.  Jump down into the pit to start the boss encounter here.
11. Kill waves of adds and finally kill a boss (Warchief Rend). 
12. A small gate on the South Side of the pit opens up when Rend dies.  Go through it.
13. Left. Up a slope. Right. Down a slope. Right again. Over a bridge. 
14. Enter a room called Spire Throne.  You'll find General Drakkisath in this room.  Kill him and loot the orb that appears behind him.  

Quest

All you need to do is get the letter from the quartermaster who is near the UBRS/LBRS entrance.

Once you have the letter you start the quest and you need to go through UBRS and kill General Drakkisath and touch the orb to finish the quest.

You will then be attuned to BWL and able to use the outside orb to enter BWL.

Good Luck

-SolarFusion

All you need is a few invisibility potions, and maybe some fire protection potions. It helps to be a night elf, because you can shadowmeld in certain places to allow patrols to go by. You also need to have the Shadowforge Key, and have to be able to solo a single lvl 50 Bloodhound. Basically, I followed the path that the rogue takes in the video someone posted earlier, but at the beginning, where he uses distract to make the dog look away, I popped an invis pot, and I went to the right of the group of men, directly toward the dog. He senses you, but he will be the only one aggro'd if you run into the middle of the room. Once you kill him, just avoid aggroing mobs till you get to Incendius, then you can aggro the two elementals and jump into the lava on the left. Doing that takes you out of combat and resets the elementals. All thats left is watching for the elementals in the lava to pat away from you, and you can make your way on the same path the rogue did. Once at the final bridge, pop another invis pot (before you run up, because even as a lvl 60 you cannot run in front of the bridge without aggroing the elementals), and bolt across. I stopped in the middle to be safe, waited for the pot cooldown, and popped one more to avoid the last group. In total, about 10g in pots on my server, and you have yourself a solo'ed MC attunement.

Directions on getting there (without swimming through the Lava, I always got lost doing that).

Enter BRD. Go left through the wrought-iron door which is now permanently unlocked. Open another wrought-iron door to your right. Then open another steel door in the wall, just ahead. This should take you into the Garrison.

Operate a big mechanism in the garrison room that you're in. Then go up the flight of stairs, hang a left, and follow that passage until you come to the Manufactory. There is only one way out of the manufactory, and it leads to the Grim Guzzler.

In the Grim Guzzler, buy Dark Iron Ale from Plugger and turn all of it in to Private Rocknot. Then go stand by Phalanx, a small event happens and Phalanx opens the door. Exit the door that he just opened and go left, and left again. Pass ambassador flamelash in the Chamber of Enchantment to the left. This should take you into the Mold Foundry, a big place with forges and golems. 

There's only one way out of here, and it leads to the Chamber of the Seven. Talk to the ghost, defeat 7 ghosts, and exit the chamber through the door that just opened. The next passage will have a right turn almost immediately; it's easy to miss, but leads to a molten bridge with sets of 3 fire elementals. (If you reach the lyceaum you went the wrong way. ) Past the fire elementals you'll see a large green raid instance portal, and the Core Fragment should be in a glowing rock just next to it. Takes 3 minutes using my shortcut to get attuned, no running for the bar, getting lost or directions:

HOW DO I GET INTO BRD?:  Get the quest from Lothos Riftweaver and enter the instance.  BRD is a little hard to find but if you really don't know where it is, it's the doorway next to Lothos's tiny room.  Enter that doorway and go right and you should see some stairs into a zone with Dark Iron Dwarves working called "The Grinding Quarry."  I usually look for a large nut/bolt looking rock on the right, and turn right between the large nut/bolt rock and a flat table looking rock down a hallway.  This will be "The Masonary."  At the end of that hallway I go right into the instance. 

NOW I'M IN BRD, HOW DO I GET TO THE CORE FRAGMENT QUICKLY BY SWIMMING?:  

EDITED FOR 4.0: The mole machine has been added.  Click "just past the Grim Guzzler."  You will be transported to a half circular balcony above a bridge with some rooms up ramps behind you.  On the bridge, you see Lord Incendius.  Jump down onto the bridge, kill him, and then jump into the lava WEST of him.  Swim NORTH to the first island (there will be fire elementals on that island).  Swim to the second island (same thing, fire elementals on it).  Keep swimming North, and swim under the bridge which is like a metal grate with fire elementals roaming around.  

IS THERE AN ALTERNATE WAY TO REACH LORD INCENDIUS? If you a different route, use the "Dark Iron Highway" (which is accessed via the gate on the left, straight ahead,

How to complete this quest

 -Walk into ZF and head towards the courtyard with the Shadowcasters surrounding the fountain. Hang a right as if you were going to clear the dungeon normally. Before heading down the long hallway, look inside the huts on the right for a Clay Vessel. Distract any group outside these huts and or sap any mobs guarding the entrance. Open the Vessel and pick up the Vile concoction.

-Now go down the long hallway and skip Theka, head into the cave where Antu'sul is standing. Get close to the cauldron Infront of Antu'sul and throw the Vile concoction. Once the boss is dead loot the bag next to cage. Now make your way to the pyramid.

-Once in the courtyard with the temple, loot another Vile concoction from a hut. Turn around and head back to the witch doctor, throw it into the cauldron like the previous step. Loot the bag and equip the trinket. Find a glowing grave and click on it. Loot the Blood Magic Essence.  Head towards the pyramid once again. 

-In the pyramid courtyard, above the huts that you looted the Vile concoction from. There is more huts, head towards the pyramid and turn right towards the wall. There is a ledge you can jump onto, walk along the wall and open the and loot Hollow Emblem from the chest. Combine both the Hollow Emblem and magic Essence.

-Walk up the pyramid and sap Nekrum Gutchewer. Loot the chest.

Head back to ravenholdt to turn in the quest.

When it comes to your reward choices there are a couple of things to consider.

In my opinion, the Hunting Spear is probably the least useful of the three items.  Weapons themselves will eventually become outdated, to begin with, as people level up, especially with the upcoming expansion.  Also, if one truly wants a decent spear, many hunters go and get the Ice Barbed Spear  (https://www.wowhead.com/forever/item=19106) which is a reward if you win ONE battle in Alterac Valley.  This spear has better overall stats, in my opinion, than the Hunting Spear, as it has an abundance of agility as well as stamina.

This brings it down to the last two items.  Now if you are a Marks or Surv hunter, the Devilsaur Eye is clearly the best choice for you.  However, I'm not certain if there are other trinkets more useful than this for Marks/Surv hunters, so please make a comment if you believe there is.

Being a BM hunter, I instinctively went for the Devilsaur Tooth.  I have no doubt in my mind that this trinket is one of the best for hunters with this spec.  It's highly useful for opening attacks, especially if one has a cat.  A cat put into Prowl, with the Devilsaur Tooth buff, as well as triggering Bestial Wrath the moment before it reaches the intended target means a strong critical opening attack that will proc Frenzy instantly.

This will become especially useful when the expansion pack is released.  One of the new BM abilities is Ferocious Inspiration.  It means that when your pet sc

For levels 50-55 these are actually quite nice rewards.

The polearm is very nice, does good damage, restores mana, and adds +1% crit. I myself use 2 Dawns Edges which give me +2% crit, so this one is useless for hunters that have those.

The Tooth is nice. But i see little use for it. A BM hunter will most likely have the +15% extra crit chance for the pet making it a 20% crit chance machine. Using this trinket might tell it to crit when your beast was already about to crit. If you don't have the extra damage talent for your pet, this single crit chance will add very little extra damage...

Now the Eye is most interesting for me...

I'm lvl 60, and obviously dont need the polearm nor the tooth. The eye however fits in nicely with my crit gear and trueshot aura. (with crit gear i have a 23% ranged attack crit chance) If i use this trinket right before rapid fire, i'll be missing very little, and critting a lot. The extra attack power also makes for higher crits! The 2 minute cooldown makes this a usable trinket for me.

Until i find something better ;)

...expanding on what glassthorne posted:

When this quest was first available, all the way to the release of AQ40, there were no replacements for the Devilsaur Eye, and any hunter who took the spear found it quickly replaced, and any hunter who took the Devilsaur Tooth quickly found that it was useless in raids, and nominal in PvP.  However, with the release of AQ40, Naxx, and the expansion, there are several replacements for the Devilsaur Eye.  Examples being: Badge of the Swarmguard, Drake Fang Talisman, Jom Gabber, Kiss of the Spider and Slayer's Crest.  Even outside of raids, the Earthstrike trinket from the Cenarian Circle replaces the Devilsaur Eye.

However, nothing in the game replaces the Devilsaur Tooth.  So, if you are a hunter that has not yet chosen your reward, it is probably in your best interest to get the Devilsaur Tooth.  Even in the expansion, there is not a replacement for this item.

I'd had this quest for ages and couldn't find a group willing to do it. Eventually at level 60 I got help from another lvl 60 hunter. 

You enter the instance in the temple and take the right hand steps up to the top. You are then faced with a group of dragons. Simply, run through the dragons and then use fake death. Keep doing this until you reach the large room full of dragons.

You then do exactly the same until you reach the 3rd opening on the right, go through there and at the end of the passage if the room with the two dragons. If you hug the wall they won't attack.

Wait until they have passed you and then both run out and place a trap (freezing traps don't appear to affect them). Set your pets onto them and use ranged attack. Use fake death if necessary, but you should be able to kill Morphas and get the tooth.

The above took less than 10 minutes, so it can be done fairly quickly.

In my opinion, the Hunting Spear is probably the least useful of the three items.
