It's highly useful for opening attacks, especially if one has a cat.  A cat put into Prowl, with the Devilsaur Tooth buff, as well as triggering Bestial Wrath the moment before it reaches the intended target means a strong critical opening attack that will proc Frenzy instantly.

This will become especially useful when the expansion pack is released.  One of the new BM abilities is Ferocious Inspiration.  It means that when your pet scores a c

...expanding on what glassthorne posted:

When this quest was first available, all the way to the release of AQ40, there were no replacements for the Devilsaur Eye, and any hunter who took the spear found it quickly replaced, and any hunter who took the Devilsaur Tooth quickly found that it was useless in raids, and nominal in PvP.  However, with the release of AQ40, Naxx, and the expansion, there are several replacements for the Devilsaur Eye.  Examples being: Badge of the Swarmguard, Drake Fang Talisman, Jom Gabber, Kiss of the Spider and Slayer's Crest.  Even outside of raids, the Earthstrike trinket from the Cenarian Circle replaces the Devilsaur Eye.

However, nothing in the game replaces the Devilsaur Tooth.  So, if you are a hunter that has not yet chosen your reward, it is probably in your best interest to get the Devilsaur Tooth.  Even in the expansion, there is not a replacement for this item.

I think there's too many arguments that exist on the premise of an item being "irreplaceable". It's said also for the warlock quest, with one trinket being pretty much unique and the other two items being eventually replaceable. But that trinket is a 30 minute cooldown free void walker. My problem with taking the "irreplaceable" trinket is that odds are you're not going to wear the thing at higher levels even if you can't replace it. What it does simply isn't special enough to matter.

In this case we have the Eye versus the Tooth. The polearm is pretty bad, nice crit, but while leveling your crit isn't terribly high to begin with. Greens at least increase your AP while they're at it. The Tooth gives a free crit on your pet's next attack. Now, if you're MM, or Survival, this doesn't really matter, your pet isn't a huge amount of your DPS and a crit other then the minor extra damage (especially if it's a claw or bite rather then a melee swing) is tiny. But if you're BM, you're looking at Ferocious Inspiration and Frenzy both procing every crit.

The problem exists that your pet simply can maintain both up a ridiculously large amount of the time without the trinket. Particularly after the first crit, frenzy helps increase the odds he'll proc before the effect is over and refresh the duration. With cobra reflexes, serpent's swiftness, and frenzy, your pet attacks slightly more then once a second (.99 per second). Combined with a focus dump like Claw, and he doesn't need the

Unless you're able to tank both bosses simultaneously, I suggest using Vanish to pull Morhphaz alone.

  To Vanish pull:

  (1) Distract Morphaz close to you as shown in the video (to single him out).

  (2) When Hazzas is on the other side of the room, use your x/bow/gun to shoot Morphaz, and run back a few paces.

  (3) When Morphaz has reached you, and Hazzas is closing in -- Vanish. Both dragons will reset, but Morphaz will get there first (if you timed it right so Hazzas was farther away from his return point). Immediately shoot Morphaz again with your x/bow/gun (while Hazzas is still in Evade mode). This second shot requires careful timing!

  (4) If successful, you will have pulled Morphaz alone.

Or you can do it the easy way and just do this quest while in a group and get some xp from the other mobs aswell!
Good luck!

Just got done soloing Morph after my 3rd attempt. My gear is mostly blue with a few epics, my HP around 3800. Combat spec 20/31 with DalRend set.

First time I went in unprepared. After sneaking to the dragons, I distracted Morph, garroted and proceeded to beat him down. Got him to 25% health before I died.

Second time, I had Greater nature absorbtion potions on me and I equiped my lifestone. Again I distracted, proceeded to beat him down to 5% health before I died .. lifestone healed me for 306hp (6 over the minimum) =( .. their normal hits were between 250 and 300 damage with crits at 500+

Third time again I had greater nature absorb, since the cooldown on my lifestone wasnt up, I equiped my gnomish shrinkray. Once again .. distracted, garroted and proceeded to beat him down. As my evasion was wearing off I hit the shrinkray and that knocked Morph's average hits down from 250-300ish to 160-200ish. This did the trick as I finished off Morph, vanished out and hid in that little alcove that seperates the 2 rooms. Ran back and looted when Haz was at farthest distance.

One thing I noticed .. the Greater nature protection potion was overkill, their acid breath did not eat through it the 2nd or 3rd time. You can prob get away with the normal ones (much cheaper too)

So, this is still doable, however, I used a different strategy.  I used the same strat I use to solo Lord Incendris in BRD, for farming the Ace of Elementals.  I have a 22/3/26 Hemo build.

So, same deal, nature protection pots, etc. etc. all the usual buffs.  Distract, just to stop movement.  Stealth up, and opened with Hemo, then 4 more hemo's to get 5 combo points.  Vanish.

Then step out of agro rang, (the little nook)  But make sure not to deselect Morphaz, you have to keep these 5 combo points on him.  Once you're all healed up, food buff etc.  Down your nature protection pot.  Wait 2 minutes.  Then drink a Magic Resistance pot.  (it lasts 3 minutes but the cooldown is 2, so If you wait 1:45 before going in, you'll be able to drink a healing pot before the fight's over as well.  The magic res pot. will give you an additional +50 to all resistances.)  

Distract again, open with ambush (if you have imp ambush/oppertunity). Directly follow your ambush opener with a 5 point expose.  Then launch in to him.  give him everything you got.  With the ambush opener, prep and 2 cold blood evis's, he's pretty much dead if you land them.  once he died, I looted him, vanished, and waited 10 minutes.  Then I went in to kill the other guy, using the same method.

Opening with a 5 point expose is key.  It makes your cold blood evis's rock.

main.body: You can't go wrong with the pendant. You'll outgrow the Glacial Spike, and the Fire Ruby is tedius if you use any other trinkets[I keep my insignia of the alliance and my rune of perfection on at most all times]. The dagger is pretty underwhelming. A 6% chance on casting Frostbolt to restore 50 mana is effectively 50 * 0.06 mana off each spell, or 3 mana back per spell.

This is what I'm using now, arguably better.

http://www.wowhead.com/?item=22403

You lose some spell damage, but gain 10 stats and a hit rating.

I would be inclined to say that of the three the Fire Ruby is hands down the best of the rewards.

I think we can agree the mana return on the Glacial Spike is not worthwhile considering other options.

The Necklace is easily replaceable as you can see above.

The Ruby however, improves your mana efficiency, returning as someone said an average of 250 mana every 3 minutes. This is roughly 7 mp/5, though it will end up being slighly more useful than that as it will come in larger chunks, which could mean an extra cast. 

The 100 fire spell bonus may seem only useful for Fire mages, but I know that leveling my Frost Mage, there is one fire spell I cast very frequently. Fire Blast! Frost is short on instants, and Cone of Cold is short range and rather mana intensive for a single target. I tend to finish off mobs with Fire Blast even as a full frost mage, as well as make use of the instant cast to do big Frostbolt/ Fire Blast Shatter combos. To make use of this trinket a simple Fire Blast macro can be used to minimize the hassle.

/use Fire Ruby
/cast Fire Blast

As instants get 42.86% spell damage, you'd recieve about an extra 43 damage on Fire Blast whenever the trinket is up, as well as the mana back. An extra 65 damage on a crit in  a Frostbolt/Fire Blast shatter combo.

Hardly useless for a leveling Frost Mage!

I would encourage any leveling Frost Mage to take the Fire Ruby for juicy Shatter combos

post-BC Frost Mage view:

I think it is worth noting at this point that since BC came out and there are Jewelcrafters out there, the dagger looks a lot more appealing. You're no longer looking at a level 60 cap anymore where you might end up using that neck for quite a while, and the dagger will help you grind more efficiently.

As for the neck, look in the AH or ask a Jewelcrafter to make you one of these if you can:

http://www.wowhead.com/?item=21790

At least as a fire mage, I am already wearing the Ruby Pendant of Fire, and have been since level 48: http://www.wowhead.com/?item=21764

The necklace is an upgrade, but not a huge one.  I'm frankly disappointed in the trinket.  Having another button to bind and a thing to click on which just doesn't help that much, I'd rather skip.  Compare with the Diamond Flask for the equivalent warrior quest which gives a large boost for around the length of a typical difficult battle: http://www.wowhead.com/?item=20130

In short, the fire trinket could use some buffing.

Post TBC these items are all pretty useless:

Necklace. If you look at http://www.wowhead.com/?item=20966 you can see you get 7 more spell damage by using a charge, as these things cost about 1g to make (or 50s to buy on AH from a levelling JC) then this a nominal cost of just 5-10s a charge. This item also buffs your group so it better for instances.

Trinket. In comparason to http://www.wowhead.com/?item=21769 this thing is just an embarrasment. It's once only use is pretty poor and will not contribute any meaningful damage over time. The mana back is nice but with mana gems, potions and evocation I rarely run short of mana, even in long fights. On use trinkets like this one I find rarely get used as often as you might think, I would prefer a simple passive trinket like http://www.wowhead.com/?item=10659 to this.

I doubt I would bother replacing my http://www.wowhead.com/?item=7714 with this. Chain casting Improved Frostbolt (2.5 seconds casting time) will only produce an average equivalent of 6 MP/5 which is pretty low. Given that you will not be casting FB's in a row and will be mixing in other spells then you really won't be getting much mana back at all.  Another way of looking at this is that you will be getting an average of 3 mana back per cast of FB - that will lower your level 50 FB from 225 mana to 223!  Look at it compared to this dagger http://www.wowhead.com/?item=20647 - which you can get at level 54 by popping into Silithus and asking any random 60+ to

I think that the trinket is the best thing there. The necklace and dagger are easily replaced fairly soon, whereas the trinket can last you well into outlands, since trinkets are so much harder to come by.

Did this quest on my shammy and then next morning went through to take two guidie friends on it. Had read a lot about how hard or even impossible this is and also heard lots of stories since about failed attempts on this server (Thunderhorn). Had two successful runs with no wipes and so thought I would share how we did it.

Class mix:
Group 1: Shaman x 3 (one rest/enh, two enh/ele), mage and warrior. All well decked out in blues and odd purple.
Group 2: Shamans x 3, priest and warrior (warrior well decked out in purple, rest blues)

Issues with this fight are the duration requiring mana conservation, and a hard point where burst damage is needed, where most people keep wiping (see notes below on the 3rd wave, green mobs). All mobs are lvl 60-61 undead and immune to war stomps and stunning (exception being grenades which I am pretty sure did stun them). At the end of each wave an "Aspect Of" spirit appears, which is bigger than the regular mob. Killing it triggers the onset of the next wave. We fought from the SW corner on the pile of bones both times. Apparently this fight was made harder a few patches ago. There are very few points in the fight where you get to drink and eat (and then only for a few seconds), so bring first aid and lots of mana pots! The fight lasts 20-30mins.

The Waves:

1) About 10-15 non elites (?red)- moderate hps, easily taken out by a well supported mage. 3 shamans with magma totems did it easily too. Easy.

2) About 15 elites (blue) - one group spawn

[b]overview:[/b] The quest involves four waves of nine elite ghosts apiece, plus an elite boss at the end. You can't just charge in all willy-nilly and expect to complete the quest. Unless, of course, you're uber-geared to the max in which case why would you need the reward helm in the first place? :)  Here's the method my friends and I use and it's never failed.

[b]Ideal group:[/b] Well, I'm a priest, so I've never done this quest without a priest. Priests play a roll in making this easier, but I'm thinking it could be done with a resto druid too, so long as they know how to make the most of thier mana pool. Other than that, you could pretty much do this with any class. [b]NOTE:[/b]  The more shammies the merrier, totems make the fourth wave of ghosts easier to deal with, as you'll see further down this post.
  
[b]Before you start the event:[/b] Have your entire group go the the corner that's to your right as you enter Rattlegore's room. I believe it's the south-east corner. You'll stay in that corner for the first two fights. [b]IMPORTANT![/b] STAY in that corner,NO ONE leaves. Again.. you'll see why later. This quest was fairly easy for my group to complete. Mind you, this was coordinated over a vent, all guildies. The group:
60 warrior
60 priest
60 hunter
60 resto shammy
60 elem / enh shammy

You have to place the scryer in the upper righthand corner of the Rattlegore room, while the rest of the party stands in the bottom lefthand corner. The ghosts spawn in 4 waves. Generally, you will want to stay in the corner and pull the ghosts to it so as to avoid adds.

Wave 1: Easy. Just a bunch of nonelites.

Wave 2: Just pull em one by one and drink between fights. No problems.

Wave 3: The Green Ghosts. If you have a hunter, have him pull the ghosts. If he's good, he can get 3 per pull. If he gets more than three, have him feign death. Retry til you get a good pull. When you do, lay a disease cleansing totem, because these ghosts have a disease that decreases sta substantially. Then, just proceed as normal with undead mobs (shackle, etc.). Now, when the aspect spawns, be mindful that in Wave 4, you will need to begin dpsing immediately. Therefore, CONSERVE mana. Shackle the aspect if needed, then let spirit + mana spring/tide totems get you up to full before finishing the aspect off.

Wave 4: Easy if you know what to do. Just dps the ghosts as soon as they spawn. Drink as needed, but just realize that the ghosts are on a timer and you will need to get them down quickly or you will have many ghosts to deal with and you will wipe.

My opinions on the quest are as follows.

When I originally set out to do this quest, I was expecting that it would be as hard or harder than the Warlock epic mount fight in Dire Maul. In fact everyone was looking forward to a very challenging and interesting encounter.

What we got was a big disappointment. It was a long and boring slog through a mindless and uninteresting series of mobs. You have loads of time between waves to drink and heal up. Halfway through we were all saying "omg this is it?".

If you have a warrior, a priest, shaman, warlock and mage you will have no problem. Heck, any type of moderately competent group should be able to finish this. Sit in the North East corner and just take things as they come.

Alright you knw when u first start the quest u have to lay down the item and the mobs will start spawning right afterwards, this is exactly what i did with my paladin epic mount quest and its very similar.

1. Lay down the item furthest off from the middle and closer to the opposite corner.
so this way you have good distance between mobs, so they spawn they dont attack you right away and you have a chance to rest up.

2. Once you grab the mobs pull them back to the corner your staying at, and lay down Earthbind totem and Windfurry totem. The Earthbind totem removes the ghost illusions right away. so you dont have to waste ur mana and hp. And the Windfury totem allows the classes that are Meleeing to gain extra hits off of the ghost mobs.

3. Now comes the hard part. the Ghost are gonna come in waves, but read instruction #1 and if you follow that first rule then you should almost always have a chance to rest up between the fights. And the rest should be easy.

1 Shaman (that being you)
1 Warrior
1 Preist 
1 druid (Heal/intervate only)
1 Mage (AOE mobs)

Honestly if you follow these simple rules and take my reccomendations down then you should have no problem at all.

This quest is simple. 5 man Scholo, and it takes place in Rattlegores room.

The mobs come in waves, blue, green, and purple.

Position the party in the far corner, just right of the entrance to the room, and be sure to completely  clear the room of every mob before dropping the Scyer. This event is long, so be patient and expect people to die/wipe.

My group setup was, Warrior, Priest, Warlock, Hunter, and myself Shaman.

The first blue wave are all non-elite mobs, so pull a few at a time to the corner. Once the blue wave is gone, the tricky part begins. 

The Green wave are all 59-60 elite and are grouped up in 3-4. The ghosts wonder aimlessly sometimes, so careful not to pull the whole room. From the corner the Shaman sits, out of combat, while the other 4 hug the right wall and pull the group closest to them. Killing 1 or 2 generally gets the job done. Everyone should die and have the Shaman raise the group. You can repeat this to clear the Green Wave.

The Purple wave is constist spawns heading toward you w/ a mini boss at the end before Darkreaver spawns. w/ the Priest shackling, this is really easy, and if you wipe, no biggie, you can still finish the event. Once you down the Purple wave mini boss, Darkreaver spawns.

Finally got around to doing this last night. 

Party was 

Me  - Heavy Resto (0/14/37) Shammy 
Warrior - Protection/Ams 
Priest - Shadow/Disc 
Priest - Disc/Holy 
Hunter - Marks/Survival 

All members were equipped in standard instance blues/set items (no gear from anywhere higher than DM/UBRS) me and one of the priests had 1 Epic (Hide of the Wild) 

Had some problems summoning at first but found the spot eventually. Stayed mostly in the north west corner. 

Managed to pull more mobs than was advisable a couple of times but between Frost traps and 2 shackles mostly kept it under control. Rested by shackling the 'Aspect' ghosts and waiting on regen when we needed to (only needed this on the last spawn before the Deathknight) Combined with Mana Spring/Tide totems we only went OOM once or twice (yay for pots) 

Only casualty was myself (and the hunters pet :P)due to aggroing the Deathknight straight away at low health after the last aspect mob. Party drew him away and continued the fight while I ankhed/drank and joined the fray again to finish him off. 

Event was a challenge but not quite the nightmare I was expecting from some of the comments above. Seems one of the few fights i've been in where mana conservation is the key to victory rather than straight dps. I also cant emphasise enough how helpful having two priests for shackle was. 

Helm is nice but not much use for a heal spec (I prefer the 27 int of Horns of Eranikus for that) so i'll more likely wear it for posin

I made the mistake of choosing the ring when I completed this quest.  The +7 str/sta/int and healing bonus looked nice to me at the time, but now that I am 60 it's obsolete.  If I could choose again I would definitely pick the trinket.  Trinket bonuses never seem to get replaced as you progress in levels.

The trinket is OK, and will have uses at endgame.

The ring will also last you until endgame when you find an epic ring.

Personally, I chose the ring, though you may want to get the trinket, because while the ring will be upgraded, the trinket probably won't.

To complete this quest you will have to go to the Sunken Temple (Atal'Hakkar) instance in the Swamp of Sorrows.  The feathers will drop off of various mini-bosses.  I did this while doing Haze of Evil quest that I picked up in Un'Goro.  This instance really requires a full party.  I did it with a party of 4 but it was pretty rough.  You will mostly fight mobs of 3 or 4  50 elites that group aggro.  Coordinates for the Sunken Temple are 69,55 in the swamp of sorrows.  You can take a gryphon to the blasted lands, and its about 5 minutes north or there.  Hope this helps some folks.

Guys, seriously, it's simple.  Get rid of the rightous BS here, and boil your needs/wants down to the below:

Staff = If you want short term looks, this is it.

Robe = If you want short term bump in stats (about 5 - 10 levels worth) this is it.

Trinket = If you want something that you can ALWAYS use, but may not always use, this is it.

Also, don't forget that with the expansion, new warlock abilities are being added.  My two cents is go with the trinket, because there just MIGHT be that spec where this trinket would be invaluable.  It would be a shame to have picked up a robe or staff that will DEFINITELY be replaced by level 70 and then be in a position that you wish you had picked the trinket...

~Rashna
AP Server

Exactly.   Later on towards end-game the trinket will still retain some marginal value as it will save you a soul shard and lots of mana.  It's nice to have, but not a big deal.   

It helps when grinding or with repeated boss attempts... or in the middle of a boss battle and your pet goes down, but you need more dps - or another off-tank for adds.  Lots of neat little uses, but nothing major.   Still through time it will hold it's value longer than either the scythe or robes.   

The only reason not to take the shard is if you are levelling very quickly and just want something to replace your staff/robe for the moment. 

Basically the choice is Abyssal Shard, Large brilliant shard, or large brilliant shard.   (if your an enchanter). 

:-)

The quest now rewards all three items.

No longer do you miss out on the scythe because the trinket is better long-term.

PvE raiding

PvP

You should ALWAYS have as many shards as the situation you are in requires, be it a raid or some PvP. If you don't, go get some. One extra voidwalker won't help with those.

If you don't know how to kill a single mob without a pet or with an imp out then you need to do some learning. If you are farming low-level content and can't get any more shards you are extremely poorly prepared and one voidwalker won't help for long.

For those unfamiliar with ST, you want to go up to the top floor (Hall of the Cursed) and clear around the circle. Go down each set of stairs (3 on right side, 3 on left side) and kill the troll mini boss.  Each set of stairs on the left has a platform with a pack of mobs and 2 exits.  One exit will bring you back to the first floor, the other to the mini boss.  If you find yourself going down more than a few stairs you are going the wrong way.  Hope this description helps the people who haven't been to ST in a long time (or ever).

A)
The succubus is your favorite minion. You are out of Soul Shards and your succubus isn't summoned. Not one mob that generates XP is in sight. You want to summon the succubus. What will you do?
1. Use the Abysss Shard to summon the Voidwalker.
2. Tell the VW to Stay.
3. Run away from the VW until it is out of sight: You will get a Soul Shard.
4. Summon the succubus.

B)
You are a Demonology spec Warlock. You are in a tough battle, solo. Both your HP and mana are low, and you are getting aggro. Your minion's HP is low too. What will you do?
1. Cast Fel Domination and use the Abysss Shard to summon the Voidwalker. 
2. Choose to sacrifice the VW and run away (to fight another day) and/or choose to let VW attempt to tank (giving you time to use pots and/or bandages).

I am sure there are other senarios :).

[b]Alliance Quests for Wailing Caverns[/b]

Since many people are trying out these low-level dungeons since the new dungeon tool appeared, perhaps for the first time, I thought it might be nice to make a summary of quests for WC for Alliance characters. Note that, for the Alliance, there isn't a quest for killing any of the bosses, although there is a quest triggered by a drop from the final boss.

Also note that since the mobs in the entry area (outside of the actual instance) are not elite, three of the four quests can be completed without actually grouping or entering the instance, as long as you're a high enough level to handle these non-elite mobs. On the other hand, since many people will be zoning directly in to the instance using the new tool, it's important to note that three of the four can be completed in the instance itself.

Soloable by any level 60 class.

1. Enter instance and go through 2nd hallfway from the right. Hug the left and wait at the first stairs (do not go up yet).
2. Wait for the patrol to go down the stairs. Once they go down, you hug left and go up the stairs.
3. Go up 3 long flights of stairs. Once you see a trash pack, hug the right and go into the hallway. Keep going through hallway to balcony where mini-boss Zolo is at.
4. Jump down from balcony (don't aggro any mobs).
5. Walk through middle (don't fall into hole) and get close to southern hallway, there will be a trash pack impeding your way.
6. Rogues/Druids can stealth. Hunters can send pet and feign death. Warlocks can send pet, run, die, and SS. Rest of us use Invisibility Potion. Get close to the left side of hallway (don't aggro) and pop Invisibility Potion (helps to have move speed to boots). Keep running and keeping to the left.
7. Watch the patrol path of Hazzas and Morphaz, your Invisibility Potion will expire near the corner where you turn left towards Eranikus room. I got lucky and they were on the far right, so I was able to safely keep running and made it towards Eranikus room. If Hazzas and Morphaz are on the left, don't go past the corner and wait for them to patrol through and then make a run for it.

The formerly "broken" Questline of Eranikus finds itself prolonged - but you need Neutral reputation with the Brood of Nozdormu (36.000 rep) and a good raid guild, since you WILL need to kill one green dragon in the Hinterlands, Feralas, Ashenvale and Duskwood. Each. 

Good luck to all of you out there.

This quest is horribly annoying is that the description is incredibly vague on where to find the quest guy.  Nor does it tell you the name of who you're looking for.

The quest person you are looking for is a wisp (named "Wisp").  It can be found just inside Teldrassil from the gates of Darnassus.  Upon leaving the gate, turn left and head up the path to the north.  It's just left off the path hidden in a little cul-de-sac.

This is easy for Alliance to do, but horde will need to venture through the city.  As Darnassus is usually mostly empty this shouldn't be a problem, but take 2-3 friends along as company (and for pvp fun).

As for how to start this quest, the questline begins in Silithus with the dragons in Tanarsis.  The questline eventually splits into several "sub-lines" of which this is one.

Solo as 60 warlock:

1) enter instance (can be done without aggroing a single mob, but void is your insurance here).
2) go to the middle right hallway and up the stairs
3) turn right above the stairs, pass Hukku and jump down (take care not to aggro whelps down there). If you are in combat with some NPC on the 1st floor, they would evade and you should leave combat
4) take stamina gear, summon void, apply SS, prepare HS
5) run through the south hallway so your void is going first, aggroing all mobs. When void is low HP, sacrifice him and continue running.
6) turn left and die somewhere safe
7) use SS (wait for dragons to go away)
8) approach Shade of Eranikus and Malfurion Stormrage appears
9) accept quest
10) hearthstone

To be more specific than "various toons", the [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?item=12753]Skin of Shadow[/url] drops from Risen Bonewarders around Rattlegore, Risen Constructs around Illucia Barov, Illucia herself, the Ravenian, Lorekeeper Polkelt and Instructor Malicia. To get them, jump down over the railing in that entrance area to Scholomance (it might take trial and error to find the right place to jump), turn right out of the room you jumped into and go into the room with dragon whelps, and jump down one of the holes around the side of the room (or just go down the staircase on the far side of the room) to find Rattlegore and Risen Constructs. Kill Rattlegore for the key and constructs for the Skins, go back to the room you jumped into, unlock the locked door, turn right through the other door and down one set of stairs, and you'll find all the minibosses in little rooms on two levels around that central area. They have trash mobs, but some can be avoided and the rest die easily to aoe. When I stealth I can do this without aggroing a single unnecessary mob except for one miniboss's trash and the group by the locked door, but even without stealth your aggro radius should be small enough at 80 to not pull too many mobs. All mobs that can drop skins have basically the same drop rate and there are more in Rattlegore's room than in the rest of the instance, so some people might prefer to skip the part after Rattlegore and just farm them from his room.

Note that the cumulative set bonuses for your tier 0 (Dungeon Set 1) set (somewhat different for each class) are arranged IN REVERSE ORDER for the tier 0.5 (Dungeon Set 2) set!

As you trade in the bracers in "An Earnest Proposition", you'll obviously worry about losing that precious "+8 All Resistances" for the complete Tier 0 set.  But if you look at the set bonuses for Tier 0.5, you'll note that the FIRST bonus (for 2 items) is "+8 All Resistances".  This means that you'll actually recover that set bonus after turning in your second and third pieces (belt and gloves)in the "A Supernatural Device" quest chain.

Not as bad as it could be!

main.body:
This is part of the set of quests which convert your [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?itemsets&filter=ta=1]Dungeon Set 1[/url] gear into [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?itemsets&filter=ta=2]Dungeon Set 2[/url].  In every case, the quest starts from [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?npc=16013]Delina[/url] and is called [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?search=An+earnest+proposition#quests:0+3+1+2]An Earnest Proposition[/url].  Because the upgrade quests are available to all classes on both sides, there are actually 18 quests with this name (9 classes x 2 "sides").

The quests are rather involved and require a significant amount of travel to complete.  In some cases, you will require groups to complete the associated dungeons or the summons in Silithus.  Although 8 of 8 pieces of Dungeon Set 1 are not required to start the quest, it is proposed that the Dungeon Set 1 bracers are required to begin the quest chain - the other pieces of Dungeon Set 1 can be collected along the way.

Dungeon Set 2 is, in appearance, recolored versions of Dungeon Set 1.

More information, and an extensive write-up, can be found [url=http://www.wowwiki.com/Dungeon_Set_2]at WoWWiki.com[/url].
Does not count for Loremaster of Kalimdor, although some of the follow-ups do.

Depends on how you've spec'd your hunter as to which pair of gloves would be better.  If you have not put many points into the Beast Mastery tree, then the Beaststalker's gloves would be the better choice.  However, if you have put a lot of points into BM (as I have), then the Beastmaster's gloves would probably be better for you.  Frenzy rank 5 gives your pet a 100 percent chance to gain 30 percent haste after landing a critical strike.  Ferocity rank 5 gives your pet plus 15 percent to its chance to land a critical strike.  With a fast pet (1.0/1.3 attack speed or so), you land crits pretty darn often, which gives that haste effect pretty frequently.  An additional 2 percent is nothing to scoff at.  For hunters like myself who solo or duo a lot, you find that making your pet more effective greatly increases your survivability/chances of completing quests, etc.  For me, the Beastmaster's gloves would be a better choice, but as I said earlier, it's very dependent on how you have spec'd yourself.

This is the infamous "45-minute Strat" run that many have tried and few have beaten.  It's part of the Dungeon Set 2 (Tier 0.5) upgrade quest chain, so it's appropriately difficult.

In order to pull this off successfully, you need to know how to cut the right corners:

1. you do not need (or want) to pull every group of mobs that you would normally pull on a Strat dead run.  Walk around every group you possibly can.  Battle the fewest number of enemies possible.

2. do not loot anything (except - maybe! - for the minibosses).  You do not have the time to roll for random greens, but more importantly, if it takes you 3s to loot a mob and you loot 100 over the course of the run, that's 5 full minutes used.  The timer is too tight to justify 5 minutes of looting.

3. start the next pull before the current mob is dead.  The DPS players (specifically rogues and hunters) should basically have no downtime throughout the run.  The only breaks you should take are for the casters to drink up, and even then you should only drop out of combat long enough for them to start.

4. most importantly and most obviously, remember to concentrate your firepower on a single target before moving onto the next one.  That actually applies to every group, but people seem to forget easily.

Unfortunately a good part of this run is luck.  With that said, best of luck to you.  :)

Attempted this with a Protection warrior (me), MC/BWL-geared mage and warlock, a priest and a not-so-great paladin.  There should be no breaks - constant pulling and fighting is required.  We got through the gauntlet with about 10 minutes left, and it took about 15 minutes to clear the abominations, Rammstein, the skeleton spawns, and Baron.  So aim to start pulling the abominations with 15 minutes left and if you keep the pace up pulling them you should be good.

Team make-up:
Hunter: Giantstalkers
Rogue: PVP gear, bits of ZG gear.
Priest: Devout + blues
Mage: Magister's + blues
Paladin: highest blue armor with stam I could find, shield, and the Argent Dawn's reward sword.

3 of us had the upgraded Argent Dawn trinkets.

I got to tank. Kinda.

What we did was the hunter did most of the pulling, else I did it. When the creeps we were killing were at <20% health, he went and pulled another. This worked really well for us, except at the Abominations. I made the mistake of leaving the priest with an Abomination so I could go pull, and the oozies ate him. Just a warning for that section.

Also very key is that you need to fight the urge to play defensively. We're all used to pulling, and then moving back to the group so the creeps move back. Here, I had to move forward (cautiously) so we could move faster. Use your discretion, of course. As usual, you can pull some casters by moving out of sight, or you can run up if they refuse to come.

Best things ever: shackles (for accidental pulls), silence, holy waters, bombs, and your corporal trinket.

We had to reset twice after the rogue and I were feared into mobs. Either equip your trinket, or save your Divine Shield (if you're a pally). Your other options are stunlocks and silences.

I just did this, with my group it technically took one try (had a warlock and a different rouge the time before the winning run). We weren't that well geared, I'm a priest and I had just most of my dungeon set on me, but here's a nifty trick tp cut a decent ammount of time:

(This really applies largely to Horde, but if you have a warlock that works too)
Go about how you would regularly do the run. Kill the spider, baroness, and Malakai. When you make the transition to Malakai be sure not to take the gated trap where all the bugs spawn, go the back way from the Baroness. After you come from the alleyway only kill the pats and the monsters on the right side working up to Malakai. When you kill him (here's the nifty bit (and make sure you have a shammy who can pop or an SS on the priest)) shield the tank, cast a renew on him, and let him draw aggro all the way to the gates with the rest of your party behind him (to a resonable extent). Once you get in the gates die, pop, heal, pull the abominations. It doesn't sound all that great but it got us to the Baronn in time, and that's all that matter. You skip about seven or ten pulls, which is pretty precious time.

Pally (me)(holy) - all blues, only 1 epic
Driud (feral-tank) - all blues, only 1 epic

Mage (fire) - all blues, only 1 epic

It is true that the more dps you bring to the party, the easier it will be, which is why we were concerned that we wouldn't be able to do it, but we were very organized and were able to get to the baron with 2 minutes left (time enough for us to lick our wounds, rebuff, and kill kill kill)

The biggest trick we learned was to have the Priest pull all of the mobs....that's right!  Our priest chain pulled mobs for 2 main reasons...

1)  They are the only ones NOT doing dps, therefore, by chain-pulling (ie, pull next mob while current mob has about 50% health) all of the damage dealers were able to NEVER stop fighting.  It was basically a 43 minute slug-fest.  

2)  Since he was the primary healer, he controlled the pulls and managed his own mana.  When he would need a break (3-4 times total), the pally would take over healing and pulling.  Also, an innervate or 2 (or 6 actually, lol) from the druid helped out a lot.

The order we took was Spider, Baroness, Pallid.  After the baroness, which we pulled way back to the gate so as to avoid the accidental agro from her fear, we continued counter-clockwise to the pallid.

> Unfortunately a good part of this run is luck

Good players make their own luck. Having reached Exalted by doing Strat 45 runs (with ZG blues) with ~10 minutes to spare, it boils down to:

1) Group buildup. Tank and primary Healer are the obvious. We mostly opted for a two mage team, with some melee DPS to wrap things up. Warrior will duel wield most of the time, using 1H+Shield when fighting multiple mobs and/or mob type.

2) Crowd-control. Priests are always healing, so they'll never shackle. But having two Frost Novas for spamming during four mob pulls is critical. Three are pinned to the floor, allowing the group to kill one mob that is extracted from the group.

3) Fast pulling (and counterspell from Mage), but one that allows a slight pause between kill/re-entering combat: this allows drinking (even if of small amounts). Most pulls are from the Warrior, but some are better if they are sheep pulls,

4) Fixed pulling order. You aren't pulling all of the mobs, and we had our mob pulls numbered. Our path is different than the one below, but it gives you a good idea of the notion of mob avoidance.
http://www.wowwiki.com/Image:Baron45.jpg

5) Use line-of-sight to move mobs to kill locations. Depends on your pathing.

6) Mage solos a Ziggurat. Once the group kills Baroness Anastari, four players continue to clear to Nerub while a mage solos the zigg. Mage will solo the trap, while the group is killing Nerub, and then solo the zigg. Mage will solo zigg on Malek

main.body:
This is the infamous "45-minute Strat" run that many have tried and few have beaten.  It's part of the Dungeon Set 2 (Tier 0.5) upgrade quest chain, so it's appropriately difficult.

In order to pull this off successfully, you need to know how to cut the right corners:

1. you do not need (or want) to pull every group of mobs that you would normally pull on a Strat dead run.  Walk around every group you possibly can.  Battle the fewest number of enemies possible.

2. do not loot anything (except - maybe! - for the minibosses).  You do not have the time to roll for random greens, but more importantly, if it takes you 3s to loot a mob and you loot 100 over the course of the run, that's 5 full minutes used.  The timer is too tight to justify 5 minutes of looting.

3. start the next pull before the current mob is dead.  The DPS players (specifically rogues and hunters) should basically have no downtime throughout the run.  The only breaks you should take are for the casters to drink up, and even then you should only drop out of combat long enough for them to start.

4. most importantly and most obviously, remember to concentrate your firepower on a single target before moving onto the next one.  That actually applies to every group, but people seem to forget easily.

Unfortunately a good part of this run is luck.  With that said, best of luck to you.  :)

Some notes on soloing this for Loremaster. I found it pretty hard to figure out what to do from the previous posts. 

I avoided Strat while levelling; I just didn't like the instance much. But trying to finish Loremaster, it was either get a raid together to run ZA, or solo Strat.

My toon is a lvl 80 Pally. He worked in his alternate spec, Retadin. He's reasonably well geared, mostly ilvl 200 stuff. 

Main points:
[ul]
[li] At lvl 80, your aggro radius is tiny. You can walk pretty close to the mobs without aggro. Edge your way around groups, or wait till traffic opens a gap and dash through. This really speeds things up.[/li]
[li]Doing this, you will occasionally get a swarm of very low level nuisance mobs coming from crates near the edges of the road. Take them out without AoE to avoid aggroing the others. For me, Retribution Aura did the trick.[/li]
[li] At this level, none of the bosses are challenging, so I won't go into detail on the fights. What's more difficult is the occasional aggroing of a group of trash. I found AoE very useful when that happened, as well as being able to self heal. The occasions where that was required were far enough apart that I could probably have just used potions. Some of the mobs will web you, and having a trinket or other means of removing movement problems helps.[/li]
[li]If you do aggro a trash mob or two, don't try to run away; as they follow you they pick up more trash. Deal with it on the original site, preferrably without AoE. [/li]

Attempted this with a Protection warrior (me), MC/BWL-geared mage and warlock, a priest and a not-so-great paladin.  There should be no breaks - constant pulling and fighting is required.  We got through the gauntlet with about 10 minutes left, and it took about 15 minutes to clear the abominations, Rammstein, the skeleton spawns, and Baron.  So aim to start pulling the abominations with 15 minutes left and if you keep the pace up pulling them you should be good.

Keep in mind you don't have to [i]kill[/i] the Baron within the 45 minutes.  You just have to [i]engage[/i] him.  Unless you're critically short on time, get buffed, your cooldowns up, and to full health and mana before starting it up.  After all, no matter how much time you have left you only get one shot at him if you want complete the quest.

Go in Dire Maul north (the ogre zone) (either use the crescent key, get someone else to open it up, or strip, die, and rez on the other side).

Stealth straight across to the ramp into the courtyard full of ogres and dogs.  You must avoid any ogre pats and especially dogs -- they see through stealth.

Hop onto the left lip of the ramp.  Angle yourself so that you're mostly aiming down for best results.  Don't go very far down the ramp.

Hop down onto the ledge and sneak around to the ramp down on the left side of the courtyard.  You can stay clear of the ogres.

Open the door below and walk to the library.  (I'm not sure if this door opening requires the crescent key or not -- I had it at the time).

Otherwise you'll require a party.
[quest=8949] DM or LBRS!

Either the Crescent Key, some kind of Seaforium Charge, or lockpicking skill is required to get past that second door as well as the first.  The strip/die/rez on other side trick won't work here, since you'll be in an instance at this point.

This is part of the set of quests which convert your [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?itemsets&filter=ta=1]Dungeon Set 1[/url] gear into [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?itemsets&filter=ta=2]Dungeon Set 2[/url].  In every case, the quest starts from [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?npc=16013]Delina[/url] and is called [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?search=An+earnest+proposition#quests:0+3+1+2]An Earnest Proposition[/url].  Because the upgrade quests are available to all classes on both sides, there are actually 18 quests with this name (9 classes x 2 "sides").

The quests are rather involved and require a significant amount of travel to complete.  In some cases, you will require groups to complete the associated dungeons or the summons in Silithus.  Although 8 of 8 pieces of Dungeon Set 1 are not required to start the quest, it is proposed that the Dungeon Set 1 bracers are required to begin the quest chain - the other pieces of Dungeon Set 1 can be collected along the way.

Dungeon Set 2 is, in appearance, recolored versions of Dungeon Set 1.

More information, and an extensive write-up, can be found [url=http://www.wowwiki.com/Dungeon_Set_2]at WoWWiki.com[/url].

As seen at the top of this page, all three items are bind on pickup and therefore cannot be bought off the auction house, requiring one to farm them off bosses.

[ul]


[li]Wildheart Boots drop off [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=10596]Mother Smolderweb[/url] in Lower Blackrock Spire.[/li]

[li]Wildheart Kilt drops off [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=10440]Baron Rivendare[/url] in Stratholme.[/li]

[li]Wildheart Spaluders drop off [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=10268]Gizrul the Slavener[/url] in Lower Blackrock Spire.[/li]

[/ul]

Copied from http://www.wowwiki.com/Tier_0.5

Step Three: Pants, Shoulders, and Boots
[edit]
Baron Rivendare

Your next step takes you, along with the Extra-Dimensional Ghost Revealer, to the entrance of Stratholme to talk with the ghost of Anthion Harman. He asks you to rescue Ysida Harmon from Baron Rivendare. The quest is a timed event, requiring the group to engage Baron Rivendare in combat within 45 minutes once the second gate from the Stratholme service entrance has been opened.

    * NOTE: The rumour about using Spectral Essence to talk to the prisoner at the end is not true. Did strath in 1h on 3/30, and equipping at the end didn't reveal anyone. 

    * WARNING: Using the Medallion of Faith and summoning Aurius for the Baron Rivendare fight seems to break the quest script and hence making this quest impossible to complete. 

[edit]
Gathering Mats

After the 45 min baron run you return to the ghost and he asks you for 3 Dark Iron Bar, 3 Mooncloth, 20 Enchanted Leather, and 4 Cured Rugged Hide. After you turn these in, he sends you to Dire Maul library to talk to Falrin Treeshaper.
[edit]
Ogre Warbeads

Falrin Treeshaper in Dire Maul gives you a quest to gather 25 Ogre Warbeads off the ogres in Dire Maul and Lower Blackrock Spire. The droprate goes (roughly) as follows: Dire Maul (Outside): 1:30, Dire Maul (North): 1:5, Lower Blackrock Spire: 1:2.

Although the drop rate is much higher in Lower Blackrock Spire, there is also much fewer ogres in that instance. It will

main.body: The hardest part is probably trying to get the Cinder of Cynders: You need to summon the NPC via doing long and grueling farming in silithus to get the items needed to summon him from his Wind Stone. =|
Turn back now! It's not too late!

Obtaining the [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=21989]Cinder of Cynders[/url] from the [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=15206]Duke of Cynders[/url] is easily the most annoying part of the entire D2 set quest line. Here's the entire frustrating process:

1. Obtain 4 sets of [url=http://www.wowhead.com/itemset=492]twilight cultist trappings[/url].
2. Summon 3 templars from 3 [url=http://www.wowhead.com/object=180456]Lesser Wind Stones[/url].
3. They each drop an [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=20513]Abyssal Crest[/url]. Take those 3 to [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=15282]Aurel Goldleaf[/url].
4. She will offer you the repeatable quest [url=http://www.wowhead.com/quest=8333] Medallion of Station[/url]. Combine the 3 Abyssal Crests with 1 [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=14344]large brilliant shard[/url] to receive the [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=20422]Twilight Cultist Medallion of Station[/url].
5. Wearing the medallion with your fourth set of trappings, summon a duke from a regular [url=http://www.wowhead.com/object=180461]Wind Stone[/url].
6. Unless you have the Signet of Beckoning: Fire (see below), PRAY. You have a 25% chance of summoning the Duke of Cynders.


If the auction house is lacking in sets of clothing and you're forced to farm them off the Twilight Cultists, be sure to turn in the [url=http://www.wowhead.com/item=20404]encrypted twilight texts[/url] (10 at a time) to [url=http://www.wowhead.com/npc=15194]Hermit Ortell[/url] to have a whopping 4% ch
Count Loremaster EK

I'd advice anyone who wants to do this questline, to just jump into it. Had I known the sheer amount of travel and frustration I doubt I'd ever have started it.

So worth it in the end though.

I'd just wish it was more clear what you have to do in Silithus for that flame thing though.
Heres what you have to do (Three kings quest):

Go to silithus, farm Twilight cultist sets, when you're wearing a full set, you can click on a lesser wind stone, this burns some part(s) of your Twilight armor, but you get 1 Abyssal crest, you need to get 3 crests, once you have three, speak with the lady to the left of the Inn in Silithus, hand in 1 Large Brilliant Shard + 3 crests for a necklace. With this necklace + a full cultist set, you can click the Wind Stone - Which has a 20%~ chance of spawning the boss you want. I got my boss on the 5'th try, southern camp.

The strat we used on the 2nd/3rd attempt was pretty simple.  The one with out a shield has a nasty cleave so you want to keep her away from the party.  The first time we had our feral druid offtank her away from everyone but he went down as did our Proctection tank.  So on the 2nd attempt we switched the tanking spots.

Neither of them can be stunned by rogues and all the spells appear to be instants and so you can't interrupt.

main.body:
Sothos and Jarien are spawned as part of the Dungeon Set 2 questline, in the last room of the Scarlet side of Stratholme. They spawn simultaneously, in the center of the room, facing each other perpendicular to the door. It is possible to move out of the room before they become hostile - they do not aggro automatically. They will remain until defeated; there is no need to resummon them upon wiping, or even if the brazier holder leaves the instance or group.

They have several abilities:

Sothos
Shadow Bolt Volley: Hits all targets for 300-700 shadow damage.
Shield Charge: Charges and knocks down a single random target dealing a small amout of physical damage.
Shield Slam: Interrupts spell casting and deals a small amount of physical damage; used on caster targets in melee range.
Fear: Fears all enemies. Interruptible.

Jarien
Shadow Shock: Deals roughly 800 shadow damage to a single target.
Cleave: Standard frontal cleave.
Mortal Strike: Typical MS effect.

After one twin is killed, it will spawn as a human ghost, and assist you in killing the other, which will enrage, increasing damage dealt and movement speed by a very significant margin (http://www.wowhead.com/?spell=27650). If you wipe after killing one twin, the ghost will despawn and both twins will completely reset.

They are not leashable. The twins have far higher than normal weapon skill, enough so to land crushing blows on level 70 players with 350 defense.

This group is not that tough of a fight if you do it right!
As said above Sothos has AoE fear and a charge ability to the next highest person on the aggro meter, also he has Shadowbolt volley (AoE whole party). Jarien has mortal strike and heroic strike. 
[b]Group Makeup[/b]
1 HEALER
2 TANKS (or pally / druid)
2 DPS CLASSES
[b]STRATEGY[/b]
Have a tank charge Sothos and remain in room have a second plate wearer (or feral druid) get Jarien out into the hall.
The big problem is the tank, who is on Sothos when he gets feared Sothos will go to the next person on the aggro meter, this usually is the priest unless of course you decide to take him down first. Which is a good idea if your group is more range damage. If not my suggestion is to just leave a warrior on him and burn down Jarien first. The warrior on sothos should be using beserker rage as often as possible they don't hit too hard so your priest shouldn't have to worry about healing too much from physical damage. The shadow volley is done every 30 seconds or so, basically once it happens have a priest use AoE healing or a druid can use tranquility I guess.
When one of the two dies the other will go to full health so the second tank isn't worried about damage just hold your target get some aggro. Also once one dies the others damage will increase 100%. Meaning this fight just became interesting, mash him down try to keep your healer alive if not keep a res'er alive. This fight is infinitly easier than scholo.
Have fun and e

The bracers drop from orcs in Blackrock Spire, but the drop rate is far higher in the Upper part (UBRS).

Doing this solo at 70 you are restricted to the section of UBRS up to the room with Pyroguard Emberseer in, as you need three players to click the altar to release him and open the next door.  I found that killing all the Blackhand orcs between the UBRS door and Emberseer's room gave around 10-15 bracers each time.  Killing the same number of Scarshield orcs in Lower Blackrock Spire gave just one!

So, assuming you have the Seal of Ascension, you should be able to do this in 3 or 4 runs through the very first part of UBRS.  Doing the entire instance with a group ought to easily give you all 40 bracers in one run.

My preferred method at Level 80 to do this is to go into the Halls Of Ascension (the beginning of the upper portion of Blackrock Spire) and go into a room with a flame rune and kill all the enemies except the summoners. Loot the dead corpses to see if they have any Blackrock Bracers on them, then sit and "play goalie" as the summoners summon more and more enemies to kill. Loot them all for their Blackrock Bracers. If you don't move quickly enough, however, eventually things will get hectic and you will need to kill them all and move on to the next room.

For anyone trying to do this that isn't trained in Alchemy AND herbalism you're going to have a REALLY hard time getting that flask. If anyone has a tip to acquiring the Dreamfoil I'd really appreciate the help.

This is definitely the hardest non raid boss to try and solo from the original game, and quite possibly from TBC and WOTLK too, due to the fact that you have virtually no time at all to down those adds before defile is cast.

For rogues, it is even harder as we have no healing abilities, no bubble, no pet. However after about 10 tries, I finally got him down. Yay.

Unless you are combat specced and have Fan of Knives, forget it, you wont get the adds down no matter what you try.

Here is what I did. Equipped in nothing more than lv 200 gear.

Equip Zandalarian Hero Badge (this is the Warrior badge from the Heart of Hakkar Quest)
Equip a spec that allows FoK and Unfair Advantage from Combat spec AND Preparation from Subtlety. (Macro the Prep with Evasion) It also helps to have a glyph of evasion equipped as this will give you an extra 10 secs overall.
Drink an Indestructible potion, which gives extra armor for 2 mins.

Open up on Valthalak and immediately pop Evasion, Blade Flurry, plus a trinket for extra attack power (these should be macroed btw). Attack him for maybe 5-6 seconds then STOP because the adds will soon appear. (If you continue attacking you wont have enough energy to immediately use FoK, and it NEEDS to be immediate)

As soon as the adds appear, FoK them, then open up again on Valthalak for another 5-6 seconds and again wait for the adds. Now pop your macroed Preparation/Evasion. FoK the adds again, and re-open up on Valthalak, if he doesnt get to

Witness the magnificence of my power, and despair!". And then he starts burning down your hp. I had to use bubble because I wasn't paying much attention at this point.

Just a simple clarification about summoning him:

The brazier of beckoning seems to be extremely picky about where it is placed.  You cannot set it just anywhere in the room.

 - After you dispatch Beast, go back outside of the barricade, and stand so you are facing Beast's room.

 - Position yourself so that you are closest to the left-hand corner.

 - Immediately as you step over the barricade, turn left to round the corner, then stop walking.

 - This is where you place the brazier.

Hopefully this helps someone else from wasting time running around going WTF, and thinking the quest is bugged.

After you are done fighting him (for info on the fight itself, see above posts, as well as the hotlinks of his name), use your amulet on his corpse.  A beam will channel onto his corpse, and his spirit will appear.  You get the quest from him to return to Bodley.

After I accepted the quest from his spirit though, my toon still remained there channeling the beam from the amulet, and would not stop channeling.  My toon could still move however, so I moved my toon out of the room, and once I broke LOS of the corpse, the channeling stopped.

After many tries I've done it solo with lvl 80 protection warrior. Here are tips:
[ul]
[li]First group of assasins killed with Schockwave - strong enough to kill them with one shot[/li]
[li]Second group killed with combo Cleave + Thunder Clap - since Cleave is procced on next melee if you stop attacking boss it is popped at the same time as Thunder Clap, and both should do enough damage to kill the group[/li]
[li]Third group killed with Shockwave - I have glyph so CD is only 17 seconds and the last group appeared in 18th seccond of fight[/li]
[/ul]
After 3 groups of assasins boss went down to 40k health. Second phase is a piece of cake - in hp race boss has no chances with protection warrior (I went down to like 30k hp from 36k total).

And another tip since Thunder Clap CD is 6s with a bit of luck you can use only Cleave + Thunder Clap - I've tried 3 times and it didn't work out for me.

With patch 3.3 Improved Revange hits two targets - it hits hard enough to kill assasins with one shot, but it is not the best idea to use it. It is almost certain that one of the targets will be Valthalak, so if he spawns two assasins one will survive and kill you.

Fun and interesting quest to deal with. Ran this with a warrior. After clearing most of the bottom area we went up and began clearing around the statues.

[quote]Killing the ST boss:
This part was easier than I thought it would be. Getting to the boss:
1) take the stairs all the way down to the pit
2) clear the snakes there
3) go back up to the entrance
4) take one of the front pathways and follow stairs down to the ring
5) sneak around the ring activating the statues in order: S N SW SE NW NE. Note that for most of these (maybe all actually) you don't have to kill the mobs on the balcony. Just be sneaky.

Now jump down to the boss, find a corner and get ready. He hits pretty hard (about 250-350) but slow. Like lots of fights with elites, it's just a matter of wearing him down and keep your hp up. He can be bashed and warstomped, so use those as necessary. I think my fight went bash/heal, frenzied regen, bash/heal, dance. The fight took me about 3 minutes

His only special attack is a huge punt. My first attempt ended with 2354 damage from the landing. You can completely avoid this damage though. Everytime he punts you, feral charge back to him. Often you'll go higher than charge's range... just wait until you're close enough and hit it. [/quote]

Be careful of mobs that travel a path. We learned that the hard way when a slime came around the corner unexpectedly. And there is an order to the statues that must be followed.

Before activating the last statue, be sure nothing has re-spawned down below on the steps or in the water. If clear, activate the last statue click into cat form and jump down (softer landing) and try to not get punted by the mob that spawned. The punt won't kill you... the fall from being punted will.

The good thing about this quest is that it's near the beginning of the instance and as long as everyone knows what they are doing things will roll along smoothly.
Does not count towards, Loremaster of Kalimdor.

In case you don't want to risk having the pool respawn in the middle of your battle with the guardian (this happened to my party and the spawns hit our healer so fast that the rest of us wiped in no time), when we came back, we did it the opposite way. We cleared upstairs first and then had someone activate all but the final statue, while the rest of the party jumped down to take on the mobs. Then, when the pool was clear, the last statue was activated and our last guy jumped down to take on the guardian. Easy after that.

For ultimate clarity, since people seem to be horribly confused by the existence of three separate attunement quests. The only requirement for picking up each quest is a certain reputation level with the Argent Dawn, but the objectives for completing the quests vary. You can only pick up the 'highest' version availible to you, and cannot do more than one of the attunement quests on the same character.

Note that you need to be at least honored with the Argent Dawn to become attuned to Naxxramas. There are no quests at neutral or friendly.

At [b]revered[/b] you can do [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?quest=9122]this[/url] quest. The cost is reduced to less than half.
At [b]exalted[/b] you can do [url=http://www.wowhead.com/?quest=9123]this[/url] quest. It's free, as a bonus for reaching exalted.

Halfway there youll see Lord Pythas,kill him and take his gem^^.
A little further you get too choose from two different paths. 
Dont worry, they both end up at the Lord Serpentis, but if you choos the water way, you can fight a mini boss too (nice drops). When you arrive at the top, slay serpentis, take his gem, and youll get mission completed. 
Slay the giant in the same room, for nice drops.

Cheers^^

Stealth guide:

DM North:
From the entrance, walk across the courtyard, avoiding the dogs (which have stealth detection). Hug the wall and walk into the next courtyard, keeping to the right and avoiding patrols with dogs in them. Sneak past the ogre group around the corner, and continue forwards until you reach the plant mobs. Sneak up the ramp and to the middle of the area. Loot the chest for the key, and walk to and through the door at the far north end of the courtyard. Continue down the corridor, into the room beyond and take to the left. Up the ramp, and the flame is just to the left. Be careful of the patrolling Eye, since it will probably see you standing by the flame when it comes past.

+ All guards can be killed for loot (vendor or Large Brilliant Shards, plus DM books). Just be careful to pull them away from nearby mobs, since they call for help and enrage when reaching low hp. A tailorer or leatherworker may enjoy a Gordok Shackle Key which leads to http://www.wowhead.com/?item=18250.

Straholme (scarlet):
Use the main entrance. Stealth past the first group of mobs to be greeted by a wall of see-through-stealth zombies on an appropriate moment (the zombies move around, some patrol). Lower Blackrock Spire:
This is easy up to Mother Smolderweb. To get to her, run past the first few groups until you enter the main spire. Jump down from the right side of the first platform to reach a walkway that leads to the "orc alley". Run past them and blink past the last group before Mother Smolderweb. Here you should use one Invisibility to get past the first spider group, then wait 5 minutes at the upper walkway and use another Invisibility to get past the second group. Run past the ogres and polymorph the closest one to the flame if you have to. Jump down to the walkway you used earlier and teleport out.

Dire Maul North:
There are some packs of AoEable critters on the opposite side of the first room. Get rid of them and find the spot where the wall has collapsed and there's a big pile of dirt next to it. Pull Guard Mol'dar and run back to the collapsed wall. When he gets close, jump to the pile of dirt and he turns around and tries to find an alternate path to you. Jump back and hit him when he is in range. Jump back to the pile of dirt. Repeat until he's dead and loot the courtyard key from him. Continue to the courtyard, avoiding any patrols and groups. As a rule, caster ogres are easy since you resist most of their spells, so if you have to fight, polymorph a melee ogre and kill the casters first. Use the key and open the courtyard door. Just soloed it as a warrior (arms-fury with decent gear).

Scholo part is by far the easiest and fastest. I killed just like 20 monsters including Rattlegore. Most packs can be avoided, even in that room with little dragonkins where I killed just one pack. Skellies have stun => more life and rage from Second Wind talent. Actually their stun worked better than my bandages.

LBRS is easy too. Packs of orcs aren't that hard and some of them also can be avoided, and Mother Smolderweb has skill that activates Second Wind as well. Only problem is two packs with two elite spiders and few non-elites, but still manageable without too much problem.

Stratholme is hardest part I'd say. Packs aren't easy and it is impossible (or very difficult) to avoid them. I killed like 40+ mobs in there on my way to the flame. But real problem are Ghouls. They got debuff that slows your health regeneration by 100% for 10 minutes, plus you getting 150 damage every 10 seconds in the duration of debuff. This debuff means you won't get any benefits from eating, so you just have to wait these 10 minutes until it ends. There are few ghouls patrolling between regular packs of skellies and zombies, some of them can be avoided but not all.
Rats are annoying as well since warriors aren't really good in AoE. Whirlwind and thunderclap will help you, but prepare for quite long and boring fight. As soon as you skip skellies, it is done. You'll have to kill just two scarlet to get to flame.

As a hunter, you would probably gain most from going through the alternative entrance to Strat (undead side) to avoid the rat-trap, most of the skeleton and ghoul packs have such a low aggro radius that you can sneak past them along the walls, and when you do pull them, go to your closest safe-spot and feign death.

Scholo is pretty straight forward. Jump down from the balcony before the first gate, run to the small stairs and feign. When you get to Rattlegore's room, pull his adds one by one and kill as many as you want to, so you feel comfortable pulling Rattlegore. The adds should be auto-shotted until they enrage in order for your pet to build aggro so you can nuke them when they enrage. I just finished retrieving the Flame of Dire Maul as a 70 warlock (30/10/21). Not raid-geared, but wearing a lot of high end crafted gear plus heroic items. Here's what I did:

-- Zone in, fought the Gordok Brute that pats from the right.          

-- Went left, avoided the groups, came to the entrance of the second room. Pack of mobs in the doorway: two Mage-Lords/Brute. Waited for patrol coming from the right (Mage-Lord/Mastiff) and killed them.          

-- Pulled group in the doorway, sending voidy to Brute while I dotted up the two casters, then focused on keeping my voidy's HP up while he tanked Brute. You will get aggro from your voidy, but casters will be almost dead by then. Once I got aggro from the Brute, I sacced my voidy and killed him.    

-- Went into the Courtyard and waited for pats to clear. Ran up the ramp and got the Courtyard Key, unlocked the door. Kiilled the wandering Eye that pats in the hallway.    

-- Group of three: Warlock/Doomguard/Reaver. Cast Shadow Ward before you pull and Banish Doomguard, send pet to Reaver. As pet tanks Reaver, dot up Warlock and kill him. You should be resisting/absorbing his shadowbolts, so he is cake. Dot up the Reaver, heal up your pet a bit, take the Reaver down. If you get aggro, use Death Coil/Fear to buy you some time. Using Fear with this group is risky; I feared the Reaver and he ran to the Courtyard and brought back some dogs. I AoE feared them, Healthstoned, re-banished Doomguard, feared Reaver, killed dogs,

The Deathstalker Agent for the Dragonmaw Rumors quest in WoW Forever is located in the Wetlands in the hills above the Dragonmaw encampment near Thelgen Rock (approximate coordinates 51.4, 59.2).

How to Get There

• Start the quest: Pick up "Dragonmaw Rumors" from Zaruk in Hammerfall, Arathi Highlands.
• Travel south: Cross the Thandol Span into the Wetlands and follow the road south past Dun Modr.
• Find the agent: Turn off near Thelgen Rock, next to the meeting stone, and walk up the new path uphill to the hills overlooking the Dragonmaw camp where the Deathstalker Agent waits.

OK--I camped this guy with a friend last night, here's the deal.  He has 2 spawn points that we found:

51/54, which is a split-off of the main path, it takes you down into a little area where there are bones (a rib cage) and a little fire, some boxes/crates/baskets, etc.  He SOMETIMES spawns here, but not frequently.

52/55 is the other loc, and this is in a little cubby off to the right of the main entrance.  He spawns here more frequently.

His spawn times seem to be about 6 to 10 minutes.  After he dies, it took about 6 minutes for him to spawn, 2 times in a row.  We waited for him for about 45 minutes at the 51/54 location, he never spawned there (but when we first got there his corpse was there, so he does spawn there sometimes).  He did spawn frequently at the 52/55 location.

-instead of turning right at the intersection, go straight and drop off slightly (about 6' - no damage) - and he may be there.  There's usually a deviate here, too, so be careful.

[b]Alliance Quests for Wailing Caverns[/b]

Since many people are trying out these low-level dungeons since the new dungeon tool appeared, perhaps for the first time, I thought it might be nice to make a summary of quests for WC for Alliance characters. Note that, for the Alliance, there isn't a quest for killing any of the bosses, although there is a quest triggered by a drop from the final boss.

Also note that since the mobs in the entry area (outside of the actual instance) are not elite, three of the four quests can be completed without actually grouping or entering the instance, as long as you're a high enough level to handle these non-elite mobs. On the other hand, since many people will be zoning directly in to the instance using the new tool, it's important to note that three of the four can be completed in the instance itself.

The name Kalidar has some history in WoW's early development! I looked it up because I hadn't heard the name before and found out it was the original in-development name for the island that Teldrassil was grown on. As development continued the name Kalidar was phased out in favor of just referring to the island as the tree's name: Teldrassil.

It was also used to refer to an unreleased battleground called Kalidar (or sometimes spelled Kaledar). It was going to be a MOBA-styled BG: a human barracks on one side and orcish stronghold on the other, with 3 pathways for people to take between the bases.

I also wasn't familiar with A. Crater, but this also seems to be a reference to a planned battleground: Azshara Crater. It was mentioned as early as 1.3.0 in 2005 but was never developed enough to be playable. In 2007 Blizzard mentioned in a Q&A at BlizzCon that they were prioritizing balancing Alterac Valley, so other battlefields weren't going to be a focus for a while. In 2011, also at BlizzCon, it was stated that AC was being considered for MoP and had a DOTA-style gameplay in mind, but they (obviously) ended up not choosing it as one of the new BGs. I can't find any reference of it being mentioned since then. 

With Forever returning to the old Alliance vs Horde conflicts and these two BGs being referenced in new story content, maybe we'll see these battlegrounds finished!
